dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip.formal: In the current-algebra description of the boundary modes (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-s-wave-current-algebra}) let $\varphi$ be a state invariant under the $U(1)$ gauge group of the currents, under charge conjugation $C$ ($J \mapsto -J$, $T \mapsto T$), and under the modular flow generated by the zero mode $L_0$ of the Sugawara stress tensor $T$: the conformal vacuum is such a state, and so is the induced state of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-s-wave-current-algebra} under premise (Q), with charge conjugation implemented on the mode array $\psi_k$ (the fermion modes of the singularity paper's array, Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-s-wave-current-algebra}) as the particle-hole reflection about the sea level, $C\psi_kC^{-1} = \psi^\dagger_{-k}$, so that $J \mapsto -J$ and $T \mapsto T$; the proof shows that this state has the three invariances, and the proposition is conditional on (Q) wherever it is applied to it. The graviton mode is $T$. Let $O$ be a probe that is gauge-charged (a fermion field, a condensate order parameter, any operator of nonzero $U(1)$ charge) or neutral and $C$-odd (the charge and spin currents), or, more generally, that lies in a nontrivial irreducible representation of any symmetry of the algebra that $\varphi$ respects and $T$ is invariant under. Then the linear susceptibility of the graviton mode to $O$ vanishes identically: $\varphi(T\,O) = 0$, and likewise for every mode $T_n$. At first order, nothing couples to the pair correlations except the $C$-even neutral subalgebra; in the conformal vacuum that subalgebra's overlap with $T$ is carried by $T$ alone, while in the thermal state it is the whole $C$-even neutral subalgebra, generated by the current bilinears and strictly larger than the conformal family of $T$, that can couple. In the conformal vacuum the statement is strengthened by Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-conformal-orthogonality-sugawara-construction}: every quasi-primary of dimension other than two is orthogonal to $T$ as well, so the only quasi-primary with nonzero overlap is $T$. The equivalence principle thereby acquires its converse at this level: fields differ in how strongly they couple, and the reduced theory proves there is no channel outside the $C$-even neutral sector through which to couple. \emph{Level:} the orthogonality is proved below for any state with the stated invariances; that the induced state of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-s-wave-current-algebra} has them is proved in the proof from premise (Q), and is conditional on (Q); that the thermal $C$-even neutral subalgebra is strictly larger than the conformal family of $T$ is a remark, not used.
dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip.technical:
In the current-algebra description of the boundary modes, let $\varphi$ be a state invariant under the $U(1)$ gauge group of the currents, under charge conjugation $C$ ($J \mapsto -J$, $T \mapsto T$) and under the modular flow of the zero mode $L_0$ of the Sugawara stress tensor $T$. The conformal vacuum is such a state, and so is the induced state under premise (Q). For a probe $O$ that is gauge-charged, neutral and $C$-odd, or in a nontrivial irreducible representation of any symmetry that $\varphi$ respects and $T$ is invariant under, the linear susceptibility of the graviton mode vanishes: $\varphi(T\,O) = 0$, and likewise for every mode $T_n$. For a probe of charge $q$, invariance gives $\varphi(TO) = e^{Jq\vartheta}\varphi(TO)$ for all $\vartheta$, with the gauge characters written in the modes' complex unit, the transverse bivector $J = e_{2}e_{3}$, which commutes with the modes (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.transverse-bivector-is-the-complex-unit-of-the-radial-atom}); for a $C$-odd probe, $\varphi(TO) = -\varphi(TO)$.

So at first order only the $C$-even neutral subalgebra can couple. In the conformal vacuum, conformal orthogonality of quasi-primaries of unequal dimension strengthens this: $T$ is the only quasi-primary with nonzero overlap with $T$. Wherever the result is applied to the induced state it is conditional on (Q).
dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip.lay: If the graviton is a collective, sound-like mode of the correlations among boundary modes, one can ask whether anything couples to it more efficiently than ordinary energy does. This result says no, at first order: in any state that respects the gauge symmetry, charge conjugation and the time flow the modes generate, symmetry forces the response of the graviton mode to any charged probe, or to any probe that flips sign under charge conjugation, to vanish exactly. Only probes sharing the symmetries of the stress tensor can couple, which is the sense in which gravity has one way to grip. The vacuum is such a state; for the thermal state induced from the modes the result rests on a stated premise about their joint state, premise (Q).

In the conformal vacuum, Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-conformal-orthogonality-sugawara-construction} adds the orthogonality of quasi-primaries of unequal dimension, which makes the overlap with every probe of dimension other than two vanish whatever its charges; the two arguments together leave $T$ as the unique quasi-primary with nonzero overlap. In the thermal state the dimension argument is not available: $\varphi_ eta(T) 
eq 0$ is already a nonvanishing pairing between dimensions two and zero, and for a charged ensemble ($\varphi(J_0) 
eq 0$, which breaks $C$) the energy-charge covariance $\varphi(L_0 J_0) - \varphi(L_0)\varphi(J_0)$ is a nonzero thermodynamic derivative. This is why the hypothesis is the symmetry of the state and not the vanishing of two-point functions by dimension, and why the $C$-symmetric charge-zero sector is named. __notes__.note.dark-energy.weakness-dimension-nonl: Four consequences, each at its level. \emph{Structural:} coupling to a dimension-two operator is irrelevant, suppressed at energy $E$ by $(E/\Lambda_{\mathrm{cut}})^2$ relative to dimension-one couplings, which is exactly the form $GE^2$ with the cutoff at the Planck scale: weakness is a consequence of compositeness, the collective mode being one dimension above the currents. This supplies the weakness's functional form, not its number; the smallness problem stands. \emph{Consistency:} the first nonvanishing vertex is cubic, $\langle TJJ\rangle \neq 0$, two currents fusing to the stress tensor: translated out of boundary-mode language this is the Gertsenshtein process \cite{Gertsenshtein1962}, already present in classical general relativity with its known and unobservably small efficiency; that the current algebra reproduces the correct leading vertex is a check passed, and that it produces nothing stronger is the conclusion on engineering. \emph{The coherence loophole, closed by the hypothesis:} a background with $\langle J\rangle \neq 0$ breaks the charge-conjugation symmetry that Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip} assumes, linearises the quadratic, and seems to offer a first-order channel; but the cross term is precisely the background's own stress-energy, which is what the broken symmetry admits: enhancement by coherence is general relativity's own gravitomagnetism, not a new coupling, and by reciprocity the same orthogonality that forbids a source forbids an enhanced detector. \emph{The open items, named so the no-go can be tested where they stand:} (i) the proposition is stated in the s-wave reduction, and the four-dimensional lift's inheritance must be established, not asserted; (ii) if the second variation of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}'s functional carries a component along fluctuations of $I$ itself, the argument must extend to that sector. Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation} closes (ii); Assembly \claimref{dark-energy.lift-inherits-no-go-steps-itemised} addresses (i) at its level.

__notes__.note.dark-energy.setting-introduction:
The geometry paper of this series proves that the vacuum field equations are exactly the covariant constancy of a distinguished section of the completion's ambient bundle, the \emph{frozen point}, null for $\Lambda = 0$ and of squared norm $\Lambda/3$ otherwise \cite{ButlerT6}. That was kinematics: the equations restated. This paper is dynamics: what is gravity's action principle, in the framework's terms, and what does it permit one to do?

The answers arrange themselves around one construction. MacDowell and Mansouri showed in 1977 that gravity's action can be written as the curvature-squared functional of an (anti-)de Sitter gauge connection \cite{MacDowellMansouri1977}, broken to Lorentz symmetry, in Stelle and West's form \cite{StelleWest1980}, by an internal vector of fixed norm whose covariant derivative is the tetrad; the geometric identity of that vector has remained an interpretive puzzle for fifty years. The framework supplies the identity in two steps, and the frozen point is the first step, not the vector itself. The frozen point is parallel: that is what the vacuum equations say. So it cannot be the Stelle-West vector, whose derivative is the tetrad. What the frozen point does is reduce the ambient $SO(2,4)$-structure to the de Sitter group $SO(1,4)$, the group MacDowell and Mansouri gauge, and then, inside the de Sitter fibre, select the Stelle-West vector canonically: the canonical tractor projected orthogonally to the frozen point (Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.stelle-west-vector-frozen-point}, Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}). The projected vector has squared norm $-3/\Lambda$, the square of the de Sitter radius with the sign of its fibre direction, and its covariant derivative is exactly the soldering form. Gravity's dynamical principle then reads: extremise the square of the curvature as seen from the point at infinity, the frozen point supplying the reduction and the prefactor, the point at infinity's own tractor supplying the Stelle-West slot.

Five consequences, at declared levels, organise the paper. \emph{Polynomiality} (the section “The action of the frozen point”): the functional contains no inverse metric, so it is defined wherever the ambient bundle and connection are, in particular across the singular locus where the sheaf paper's structure continues; and its curvature-squared presentation degenerates as $\Lambda \to 0$, because the prefactor is the inverse norm of the frozen point, so the presentation exists precisely because $\Lambda \neq 0$. What survives the limit, after a topological subtraction, is the Einstein-Cartan functional: the boundary is a boundary of the presentation, not of gravity's action principle, and the paper says so. \emph{Vacating} (the section “What the equations vacate, and what cannot evolve”): at a corank-one wall of the soldering form the field equations, which polynomiality keeps meaningful there, are strictly weaker than on the invertible region, and the paper computes exactly how much weaker, at the level of the torsion, the connection and the propagation: the equations determine the connection up to one symmetric bilinear form on the wall's tangent space, which they never propagate across the wall and which, on the flat model, they constrain by a single scalar relation (the wall's Hamiltonian constraint, with the form entering as a second extrinsic curvature); the curved-wall count is posed. The sheaf paper's wall turns out to be the dual degeneration, a cometric with a radical, at which the soldering form has a pole rather than a radical; there the wall opens exactly one new gauge generator, and that generator is the boost of the completion's ladder pair. At the Schwarzschild wall the paper then computes what the frozen-point datum does: its connection has a simple pole with the Kasner residue, the field equations reach the wall as the Kasner relations on that residue, the residues are exactly the weights the sheaf paper's completion is built from, and the curvature-squared value of the action diverges through its topological term alone, a divergence a local wall counterterm removes without touching the equations; the cosmological constant leaves the residue unchanged, and the statement holds pointwise for variable exponents. The equations do not permit or demand the completion; their singularity supplies its data. \emph{Dark energy} (the section “What the equations vacate, and what cannot evolve”): on the vacuum region the frozen point is parallel and its norm cannot evolve, $w = -1$ exactly, a maximally rigid stance registered against the DESI record; off the vacuum region the identification needs a definition the paper does not yet have, and the registration is conditional on it. \emph{Two kinds of action} (the section “What the equations vacate, and what cannot evolve”): the MacDowell-Mansouri mechanism does not extend to the internal factors by either of its two natural routes (the ninth refutation, shared with the Standard-Model paper): the internal forces are conformal-level, gravity alone is pre-metric, and what crosses the singularity is gravity and the $\theta$-terms. \emph{One way to grip} (the section “One way to grip: the acoustic no-go”-the section “The engineering conclusion, and scope”): in the neutral thermal sector of the s-wave current algebra of T5, the graviton mode is the Sugawara stress tensor and nothing outside the stress-energy sector couples to it at first order; the $(I,V)$-sector is pure gauge (the point at infinity has no physical fluctuation); the four-dimensional lift inherits the orthogonality at assembly level, the sphere's operators being boundary-mode bilinears by the counting paper's theorem, conditional on that paper's Indifference premise; and the engineering conclusion holds on either reading of the graviton's ontology, by derivation inside the framework and, at leading order, by Weinberg's soft theorem outside it.
__notes__.note.dark-energy.point-contact-why-form-: Per the series' practice the meeting point with the cosmological-constant problem is stated where it occurs, with its limits. Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(2) answers a narrower question than the one usually asked: not what value $\Lambda$ takes, and not why it is nonzero, but what its being nonzero yields. When $\Lambda \neq 0$ the frozen point has length, the ambient structure reduces to a reductive group, and gravity's action is a single curvature-squared invariant seen from the point at infinity. When $\Lambda = 0$ the frozen point is null, the prefactor $1/Q(I) = 3/\Lambda$ poles, and what remains is the Einstein-Cartan functional: an action principle still, but one that no longer reads as a curvature squared and no longer sees the point at infinity. The delimiters: this is a statement about the form of the action, not about its existence; it gives no value and no smallness, and the smallness problem is not addressed and is declared so in the section “The engineering conclusion, and scope”. That the boundary of the curvature-squared form is itself a division by zero (normalisation by a null vector, $1/Q(I)$) is, given this series' founding subject, worth recording; whether it is more than a coincidence is not something this paper can decide.

__notes__.note.dark-energy.setting-machine-verific:
The computational identities asserted in this paper are verified in exact arithmetic by the script \texttt{verify\_T10.py} \cite{ButlerVerifyT10}, which imports the series' shared library \texttt{GA.py}: rational matrix algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$, exact rank and congruence-signature routines, and rational functions in a formal variable. No floating point is used anywhere; ninety checks, all passing, organised in five parts keyed to statement tags; the fifth, on Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws}, computes the free-$\Lambda$ constraint count, the norm mode against the gauge images, and its identification with the tangent of the rescaling family, at the rational instance the Goldstone checks use, with $d(N^2)/d\Lambda$ as a rational-function identity. One check confirms that the withdrawn radical-vanishing claim fails, and two negative controls confirm that refuted alternative readings fail (the one-argument functional, the opposite tangential sign); the checks of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.gravity-pre-metric-forces-degenerate-exactly}(1) are the trace identities its proof uses, algebraic identities rather than tests, and are labelled so in the script.

\emph{Part A: the frozen point and the Stelle-West vector.} The scale-tractor norm $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ is confirmed as an identity of rational functions in a formal $\Lambda$, with $I = (1, 0, 0, 0, 0, \Lambda/6)$ in the flat model $\mathbb{R}^{2,4}$ carrying the form $\ip{(\sigma,\mu,\rho)}{(\sigma',\mu',\rho')} \;=\; g(\mu,\mu') + \sigma\rho' + \rho\sigma'$ with $g = \eta$; the normalisation $1/Q(I) = 3/\Lambda$ is confirmed to have a simple pole at $\Lambda = 0$ and nowhere else; the norm identity is also confirmed at the rational instance $\Lambda = 3$. For Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.stelle-west-vector-frozen-point}: with $X = (0,0,0,0,0,1)$ and $V = X - (3/\Lambda)I$ as rational-function vectors, $Q(X) = 0$, $\langle X, I\rangle = 1$, $\langle V, I\rangle = 0$ and $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$ are confirmed as identities; the model connection bivector $e_a\wedge W$ with $W = V/Q(V) = (1,0,0,0,0,-\Lambda/6)$ is confirmed to annihilate $I$, to send $X$ and $V$ to $e_a$, and to agree with the display \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry} on every basis tractor; the bracket $[e_a\wedge W, e_b\wedge W] = (\Lambda/3)\,e_a\wedge e_b$ is confirmed as a matrix identity in formal $\Lambda$; and the slot count of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(iii) is confirmed by computing, at $\Lambda = 3$ and for generic integer bivectors, that $\epsilon(I, \cdot, B_1, B_2)$ is a nonzero fibre vector (an integrand with one vector slot open is not a scalar) while $\epsilon(I, V, B_1, B_2) = \epsilon(I, X, B_1, B_2)$ is a scalar. At the rational instance $\Lambda = 3$ the image of all fifteen basis bivectors of $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)$ on $I$ has rank exactly $5$, every image vector is orthogonal to $I$, and $I^{\perp}$ has dimension exactly $5$ with induced form of signature $(1,4)$ by exact congruence, and at $\Lambda = -3$ of signature $(2,3)$, the anti-de Sitter branch; the induced form on $\{I,V\}^\perp$ is confirmed to have signature $(1,3)$ at both values; the first two facts are the stabiliser dimension $10$ and the de Sitter signature of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry}; for Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation} the joint action matrix of the fifteen basis bivectors on the pair $(I, V)$ is confirmed to have rank exactly $9$ (stabiliser of dimension $6$), the constrained fluctuation space to have dimension $9$, the one-argument failure to occur as displayed: $\epsilon(I, \xi\cdot X, B_1, B_2) = -\epsilon(I, V, B_1, B_2) \neq 0$ for $\xi = I\wedge V$; and the invariance $\epsilon(gI, gV, gB_1, gB_2) = \epsilon(I, V, B_1, B_2)$ to hold for three rational elements of $SO(2,4)$ (a boost, a rotation, and their product), each confirmed an isometry on all basis pairs. For the field-space clause of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(iii), $[I\wedge u, I\wedge v] = -Q(I)\,u\wedge v$ is confirmed as a matrix identity for $u, v \in I^\perp$ and $\epsilon(I, V, u\wedge v, B_1)$ confirmed nonzero: the $I$-leg components of an unconstrained connection would enter the Lorentz block quadratically.

\emph{Part B: the wall's free sector.} In the normal form $e = \mathrm{diag}(1,1,1,0)$ the connection equation is assembled as an exact $24\times 24$ integer matrix on the torsion components and its rank is confirmed to be $18$, with exactly $3$ identically vanishing rows, and $24$ on the invertible normal form; the frame equation is assembled as a $16\times 36$ matrix on the curvature components and its rank is confirmed to be $16$ in both cases, with no identically vanishing row. The kernel of the wall connection equation is confirmed to consist of torsion components with no $dx^3$ leg and no frame index $3$. At the connection level the equation is assembled as a $24\times 24$ matrix on the components of $\omega$ and its rank confirmed to be $12$, with the kernel confirmed to be exactly the symmetric parts of $K$ and $M$ of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.walls-free-sector}(b); the principal symbol of the frame equation is assembled in each of the four coordinate directions and its rank on the free sector confirmed to be $0$ on $M$ in every direction, $6$ on $K$ in the radial direction and $3$ on $K$ in each tangential direction; the full quadratic frame equation is evaluated on random elements of the free sector and confirmed to vanish in all components except $E_3(\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2)$, where it is confirmed to equal $\sigma_2'(M) - \sigma_2'(K)$ exactly with no cross term, and the cosmological coefficient $-6$ is confirmed. The torsion-level counts, the rank $12$, the symbol ranks and the single surviving component are confirmed for the Riemannian and null normal forms with identical counts (the null form in the frame adapted to its dying direction); the symmetric $K \oplus M$ split, the identity $\sigma_2'(M) - \sigma_2'(K)$ with vanishing cross term and the cosmological coefficient are confirmed for the Riemannian form as well, with the cosmological coefficient $+6$ there, and at the null form the surviving pair $E_0 = -E_1$ is confirmed to carry the cosmological term with coefficient $\pm 6$. The Bianchi-series check also confirms the quoted coefficients $h_{i,1} = (2, \tfrac12, \tfrac12)$ and $h_{i,2} = (-\tfrac{33}{20}, -\tfrac{3}{40}, -\tfrac{3}{40})$ at the Schwarzschild exponents with $\Lambda = 3$. For Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.variable-exponents-residue-pointwise-corrections-are}, the displayed connection (entered by the script as its connection one-forms) is confirmed torsion-free as an identity in the structure coefficients, replaced by independent rational placeholders, and the connection with the opposite tangential sign is confirmed not to be. For Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.wall-counterterm}, the Chern-Simons form $\mathrm{CS}$ of the Kasner connection is assembled by the script as an exact three-form in components and $d\,\mathrm{CS} = \epsilon_{abcd}R^{ab}\wedge R^{cd}$, the component form of that Proposition's identity $\nabla\wedge\mathrm{CS} = \mathcal{E}_{R}$, confirmed identically, and the same identity is confirmed on a generic $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$ connection with all six components nonzero and legs in all four coordinate directions, where the quartic step $\epsilon(\omega^2,\omega^2) = 0$ is exercised, and its slice component confirmed to be $8p_1p_2p_3\tau^{-2}$ at both Kasner points. For Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.cosmological-constant-does-not-change-residue}, the Bianchi I series with $\Lambda = 3$ is solved through order $\tau^5$ at the Schwarzschild exponents, the first coefficient confirmed to be $\Lambda(1-p_i)/2$, and the residuals of the evolution equations and of the constraint confirmed to vanish through order $\tau^4$, at two Kasner points and two values of $\Lambda$; the unit-boost reading of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-datum-kasner-wall}(ii) is confirmed by forming $B_w^2$ on the boost plane exactly. \emph{Part C: the two kinds, and $w$.} Trace cyclicity and the derivation identity $\operatorname{tr}([X,Y]Z) + \operatorname{tr}(Y[X,Z]) = 0$ are confirmed on exact integer matrices, and $\operatorname{tr}(\alpha\wedge\beta) = \operatorname{tr}(\beta\wedge\alpha)$ for matrix-valued two-forms on an exact instance: the algebraic content of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.gravity-pre-metric-forces-degenerate-exactly}(1). For Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-condition}(ii), the norm of $I_g = (1, 0, J/4)$ is confirmed to be $J/2$ as a rational-function identity in formal $J$, and the $\mu$-slot of $\nabla I_g$, formed from \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry} with a symbolic Schouten tensor, to be the trace-free Schouten tensor on an exact non-Einstein instance, and all three slots to vanish on an Einstein one; the $\rho$ slot is confirmed to be $\tfrac14\partial_aJ$ by forming $\nabla_a I_g$ from \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry} itself on a Schouten tensor whose entries are rational functions of a coordinate $s$ (the slot derivatives taken by the rational-function class, the algebraic part by \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry}), nonzero on that instance, where $J$ is not constant, and zero on an Einstein instance.

\emph{Part D: symmetry orthogonality.} On a six-mode fermionic window with exact rational occupancies, particle modes $k = 1,2,3$ and antiparticle modes $k = -1,-2,-3$, with energy $H = \sum |k| N_k$ and charge $Q_c = \sum_{k>0}N_k - \sum_{k<0}N_k$: the covariance $\langle HQ_c\rangle - \langle H\rangle\langle Q_c\rangle$ is confirmed to vanish exactly in the charge-conjugation-symmetric state and to be exactly nonzero at nonzero chemical potential. For the charged case, the vanishing of $\langle H\,\psi^\dagger_a\psi_b\rangle$ in a diagonal state is an identity (an operator that changes the occupation has no diagonal matrix element) and is labelled so in the script; the content is the negative control, that in a pure state superposing two charge sectors the same overlap is exactly nonzero, so the $U(1)$ hypothesis of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip} is seen to be necessary on this window. The window is a free-fermion proxy for the current algebra, with $H$ as the working substitute for $L_0$; the identification with the algebra of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-s-wave-current-algebra} is not tested.

__notes__.note.dark-energy.point-contact-what-dich: The theorem answers questions it was not asked, and the series keeps them in view per its practice: why gravity is universal (it is the one force whose action needs no metric); why it alone resists quantisation-as-a-force (it was never a force in the sense the others are: its action is pre-metric while theirs are conformal-level); and what survives the singularity (gravity, and the strong-CP parameter, which crosses). What the dichotomy does not determine, and what this paper does not supply: the three coupling normalisations $g_i$, the condensation data, and the chirality of the weak coupling, which are the task of the matter papers, the mass paper T11 \cite{ButlerT11} and the standard-model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12}.
__notes__.note.dark-energy.setting-one-way-grip-ac: If the graviton is a collective mode of the boundary-mode pairs, an acoustic mode of the correlations, then a question of principle precedes any question of engineering: does anything couple to the metric-forming correlations more efficiently than mass-energy does? Within the s-wave-reduced theory that T5 establishes, the answer is provably no, and this section closes every named open item of the argument.
__notes__.note.dark-energy.abstract: Gravity's MacDowell-Mansouri action needs a fixed-norm internal vector whose covariant derivative is the tetrad, and the framework supplies it from the frozen point, the parallel scale tractor of the geometry paper whose squared norm is the cosmological constant. The frozen point is parallel, so it is not the Stelle-West vector; it makes that vector: the canonical tractor projected orthogonally to it has squared norm $-3/\Lambda$ and covariant derivative exactly the soldering form; the action is the curvature squared of the ambient connection contracted with the two vectors, with the frozen point's inverse norm as prefactor. Consequences, at declared levels: the functional is polynomial and defined across the singular locus; its curvature-squared presentation exists precisely when $\Lambda \neq 0$, the $\Lambda \to 0$ limit being the Einstein-Cartan functional after a topological subtraction; at a wall of the soldering form the equations never propagate a symmetric form on the wall, which on the flat model they constrain by exactly one scalar relation, while at the Schwarzschild wall the datum's connection has a simple pole whose residues, fixed by the field equations, are the weights the completion is built from; dark energy cannot evolve on the vacuum region ($w = -1$), registered against DESI and conditional off it; the forces are conformal-level while gravity alone is pre-metric; and in the neutral thermal sector of the s-wave current algebra nothing couples to the metric-forming correlations at first order except the stress-energy sector, with the $(I,V)$-sector pure gauge. Exact-arithmetic checks accompany it.
__notes__.note.dark-energy.setting-prior-art: The prior work is acknowledged once. The curvature-squared form of gravity is MacDowell-Mansouri \cite{MacDowellMansouri1977}; the symmetry-breaking internal vector is Stelle-West \cite{StelleWest1980}; the Cartan-geometric reading of both, including the contraction $\Lambda \to 0$, is Wise's \cite{Wise2010}; the almost-Einstein and scale-tractor technology is Gover's \cite{Gover2010}, and its use to read the vacuum equations is the geometry paper's \cite{ButlerT6}. The graviton-photon conversion process is Gertsenshtein's \cite{Gertsenshtein1962}. The soft-theorem universality of massless spin two is Weinberg's \cite{Weinberg1964}. The Sugawara construction and the conformal orthogonality of unequal-dimension quasi-primaries are textbook two-dimensional field theory \cite{DiFrancesco1997}. The evolving-dark-energy preference is the DESI collaboration's second data release \cite{DESI2025}, with the literature's contest recorded where it is used. What this paper claims as new is the construction of the Stelle-West vector from the frozen point and the canonical tractor, with the norm and the soldering identity proved; the across-the-locus validity of the functional; the reading of the $\Lambda \neq 0$ boundary as a boundary of the curvature-squared presentation; the exact identification of what the field equations release at a corank-one wall of the soldering form, a symmetric form on the wall that is never propagated and, on the flat model, constrained by one relation; the registered rigidity of $w$ with its condition named; the pre-metric versus conformal-level dichotomy; and the acoustic no-go stated for the thermal state in which the boundary modes lie under the singularity paper's premise (Q).
__notes__.note.dark-energy.setting-position-series:
This paper is T10 of the series. \emph{It relies on eight papers:} the primer T0 \cite{ButlerT0} for the Clifford and bivector language; the root paper T1 \cite{ButlerT1} for the standard of proof and the Fact (imported) discipline every result here is held to; the sheaf paper T4 \cite{ButlerT4} for the continuation of the ambient structure across a tame wall and the corank-one radical (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-walls-sphere-theorem}); the singularity paper T5 \cite{ButlerT5} for the s-wave current algebra and, under the singularity paper's premise (Q), its thermal state (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-s-wave-current-algebra}); the geometry paper T6 \cite{ButlerT6} for the frozen point, the tractor connection and the exterior exactness (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry}, Assembly \claimref{dark-energy.lift-inherits-no-go-steps-itemised}); the Hawking paper T7 \cite{ButlerT7} for the finite-window quantification of the current algebra; the entropy paper T8 \cite{ButlerT8} for the sphere theorem that carries the sphere step (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-walls-sphere-theorem}); and, later in the series, the standard-model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} for the rescaling argument that the norm is not kinematic (Fact \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number}), with no circularity, since that argument uses only the conformal class and the pair structure.

\emph{Papers that rely on this one:} the mass paper T11 \cite{ButlerT11} imports the action theorem (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}) for its gravity assembly; the standard-model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} shares the two-kinds theorem (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.gravity-pre-metric-forces-degenerate-exactly}), uses the action's single coupling, and reads its classification's initial-data clause against Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws}; the dark-matter paper T14 \cite{ButlerT14} imports the acoustic no-go and the $w = -1$ registration (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-condition}); the entropy paper T8 \cite{ButlerT8} and the Hawking paper T7 \cite{ButlerT7} refer the engineering no-go and the lift's dynamics to this paper; and the capstone T17 \cite{ButlerT17} tabulates this paper's claims at their tiers.
__notes__.note.dark-energy.what-clause-3-requires-: The Standard-Model paper's dating observation reads $N$ as fixed at the origin and constant since, which is the (I) reading: a constant of integration. Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws} says the action as written does not deliver that reading; it delivers (P). The two are reconciled by a known class of modifications of the action (Henneaux-Teitelboim \cite{HenneauxTeitelboim1989}; Brown-Teitelboim \cite{BrownTeitelboim1988}; Kaloper-Padilla sequestering \cite{KaloperPadilla2014}), of which the Henneaux-Teitelboim promotion is the one used here (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-henneaux-teitelboim-promotion}): promote the Stelle-West norm from a fixed number to the value of a Lagrange-multiplier field whose constancy is an equation of motion, so that the norm mode of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws} acquires the equation $d\Lambda = 0$ and $\Lambda$ becomes a label of the solution rather than of the theory. This is a modification of the action, carrying a conjugate cosmic-time variable with it, and it is a decision for the series, not a theorem of this paper; it is recorded as open, with both branches stated, and the Standard-Model paper's classification is to be read with its clause (3) resting on it. Two things follow whichever way the decision goes. First, the entropic and null-endpoint forces that the classification's discussion names act on a measure over $\Lambda$, and a measure over the values of a parameter of the laws is a measure over theories, while a measure over initial data is a measure within one theory; the descent measure the series does not possess is one or the other, and which one is the decision just named. Second, the rescaling $\Lambda \to s^2\Lambda$ maps $\mathcal{S}_\Lambda$ to $\mathcal{S}_{s^2\Lambda}$ isomorphically: under (P) it is an isomorphism between different theories, under (I) a symmetry of one theory's solution space, and only in the second case is ``why this $\Lambda$'' a question the theory can be asked to answer. If the promotion is adopted, the Goldstone count of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation} is to be recomputed with the norm mode and its conjugate time as dynamical variables, a ten-dimensional constrained space with one physical direction; if it is rejected, the count stands and the dating observation is withdrawn from initial-data status. Successor problem (5) reads: the smallness of $\Lambda$ cannot be addressed until this decision is made, and then until the measure is available.

__notes__.note.dark-matter.setting-what-could-fix-: The rule needs one length common to all towers. The series fixes exactly one length, and this subsection follows it.

By Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-frozen-point-de-sitter-radius}, our world with $\Lambda > 0$ is de Sitter space of radius $\ell = \sqrt{\tfrac{3}{\Lambda}}$ at the level of the frozen point, and Euclidean de Sitter space $\dS_{4}$ is $\Sph^{4}$ of radius $\ell$, the boundary of $\B^{5}$ of radius $\ell$. The towers share one gravity, and $\Lambda$ is a parameter of the laws, so every tower has the same $\Lambda$ and its own Euclidean de Sitter sphere $\Sph^{n(r)}$ of the same radius $\ell$; the nesting of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.nesting}(iii) is the nesting of these spheres by equators. So the objects of the rule's sphere form (Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.equivalent-forms-assignment-not}), and the common unit R2 needs, are already in the series, with the unit the de Sitter radius rather than a microscopic spacing.
__notes__.note.mass.setting-exact-join: Theorem \claimref{mass.mass-weight-dictionary} and Proposition \claimref{mass.mass-symplectic-area-two-twistor-formula} both compute a mass. This section shows that the flat-space formula is the squared pairing of the composite against the frozen point, extends it to $\Lambda \neq 0$ exactly, and then reads the composite's weight off the dictionary. The plan: find the frozen point of de Sitter space in the flat chart and fix what the chart's normalisation does and does not decide (Lemma \claimref{mass.de-sitter-scale-frozen-point}, Remark \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes}); write the conformal generators in the chart (Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism}); define the grip of a composite on the frozen point, which is its de Sitter momentum, and prove it is a real vector (Definition \claimref{obj.mass.grip-mass-composite}, Lemma \claimref{mass.grip-real}); compute its squared length in closed form (Theorem \claimref{mass.exact-join}); recognise the result as a difference of Casimirs (Proposition \claimref{mass.casimir-form-join}) and identify the five broken generators (Lemma \claimref{mass.five-broken-generators}); and read off the composite's weight (Proposition \claimref{mass.weight-composite}).
__notes__.note.mass.setting-grip-composite-frozen-: Three properties follow at once. First, $\ip{P}{I} = M_{I\wedge I} = 0$: the grip lies in $I^{\perp}$. Second, $m^{2}$ is invariant under the stabiliser of $I$: for $\gamma$ with $\gamma I = I$, $\ip{P(\gamma Z)}{U} = M_{U\wedge I}(\gamma Z) = M_{\gamma^{-1}(U\wedge I)}(Z) = M_{\gamma^{-1}U\wedge I}(Z) = \ip{P(Z)}{\gamma^{-1}U} = \ip{\gamma P(Z)}{U}$, so $P(\gamma Z) = \gamma P(Z)$ and $Q(P)$ is unchanged; for the frozen point of Lemma \claimref{mass.de-sitter-scale-frozen-point} the stabiliser acts on the ambient space through $SO(1,4)$ (Fact \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection}; the Lie-algebra form of the surjection is Lemma \claimref{mass.five-broken-generators}), and $P$ is a de Sitter vector. Third, at $\Lambda = 0$, $I = n_{\infty}$ and $\ip{P}{x} = M_{x\wedge n_{\infty}}$ is, by Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism}(2), the value of the translation generator on the composite, that is, its total momentum in the direction $x$; the $x$-slot part of $P$ is therefore the momentum, the remaining part is $-d\,n_{\infty}$ with $d$ the dilation charge, and since $n_{\infty}$ is null and orthogonal to the $x$-slot, $m^{2}$ is the Poincar\'e Casimir $p^{2}$. Definition \claimref{obj.mass.grip-mass-composite} is the de Sitter extension of the mass of Proposition \claimref{mass.mass-symplectic-area-two-twistor-formula}: the composite's momentum is its grip on the point at infinity, and its mass is the length of that grip. Lemma \claimref{mass.five-broken-generators} below identifies the generators $A(e_{a}\wedge I)$, $e_{a} \in I^{\perp}$, whose charges are the components of $P$, with the five generators of $\mathfrak{su}(2,2)$ broken by $I$, the de Sitter translations, which is the representation-theoretic form of the same statement. That $P$ is a real vector, so that $Q(P)$ is a value of the real $(1,4)$ form on $I^{\perp}$, is the next lemma.
__notes__.note.mass.setting-machine-verification:
Every computational identity asserted in this paper has been verified in exact arithmetic by the script \texttt{verify\_T11.py} \cite{ButlerVerifyT11}, which imports the series' shared library \texttt{GA.py}: exact rationals and Gaussian rationals, exact rank, rational functions in a formal variable, and exact truncated power series. No floating point is used anywhere; thirty-nine checks, all passing, organised in five parts keyed to statement tags.

\emph{Part A: the dictionary.} The pairing $I \cdot D\sigma$ is formed slot by slot from Facts \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection} and \claimref{mass.imported-thomas-operator}, with $\sigma$ and $\Box\sigma$ as formal coordinates, and $m^{2}$ is read off the resulting Klein-Gordon equation: $m^{2} = -w(w+n-1)Q(I)$ on a $144$-point rational grid in $(w, n, J)$, with a separate check that the opposite sign fails at every grid point where $m^{2} \neq 0$; in $n = 4$, $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$, $\rho_{I} = \Lambda/6$ and $m^{2} = -w(w+3)\Lambda/3$ as rational-function identities in a formal $\Lambda$. Corollary \claimref{mass.weight-polynomial-two-series}: the conformally coupled scalar's $m^{2} = 2\Lambda/3$ from the pairing; the massless weights $w = 0$ and $w = 1-n$, and no others among four further test values; the shadow symmetry $m^{2}(w) = m^{2}(1-n-w)$ and the closed form $\tfrac{n(n-2)}{4}Q(I)$ at $w = 1 - n/2$ for four values of $n$; the completed square $-w(w+3) = \tfrac94 - (w+\tfrac32)^{2}$ as a polynomial identity, with $m^{2} \ge 0$ at six real weights inside $[-3,0]$ and $m^{2} < 0$ at six outside; and $w = -\tfrac32 \pm I_4\nu$ (numbers read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$, the Gaussian rationals standing for $\mathbb{Q}(I_4)$) solving the dictionary in exact Gaussian rationals.

\emph{Part B: the area.} On exact Gaussian-rational spinor instances: a single twistor's momentum is null; $p^{2} = 2|\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}|^{2}$ on all ten pairs with the imaginary part identically zero; aligned spinors give a null composite.

\emph{Part C: the chart and the de Sitter scale.} The chart on $\Lambda^{2}\CS$, the exterior square of twistor space, which is the complexified conformal vector space; its unit commutes with every conformal vector and is the central pseudoscalar $I_7$ of the odd extension $\Cl(3,4)$ (\claimref{std-algebra.complexification-is-the-odd-extension}), not the $I_4$ of the weight in Part A: $\ip{n_{0}}{n_{\infty}} = +1$ with both null; $Q(x) = -2\det x$ and the orthogonality of the slots; $Q(X_{c}) = Q(1+2c)$ with $c$ undetermined (Remark \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes}). Lemma \claimref{mass.de-sitter-scale-frozen-point}: every slot of the flat tractor connection on $(\sigma, \nabla\sigma, -\tfrac14\Box\sigma)$ vanishes and the norm is $\Lambda/3$, as rational-function identities in $\Lambda$ at rational points; $\ip{X(x)}{n_{\infty} + \lambda n_{0}} = 1 - \lambda Q/2$ at rational points and three values of $\lambda$, with the inverted order giving $\lambda - Q/2$, and the six point embeddings of the uniqueness argument of exact rank six; the ambient pairing of $n_{\infty} + \lambda n_{0}$ with itself formed and equal to $2\lambda$ at four values, with $2\lambda = \Lambda/3$, and the vector null, hence simple by Fact \claimref{mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-infinity}, exactly at $\lambda = 0$. Theorem \claimref{mass.exact-join}(1) and (4): both blocks of the deformed bracket on all ten twistor pairs, the assembled $B_{\Lambda}$ at $\Lambda = 3$, the point-supported factor $\sigma(x)$ at two points and two values of $\Lambda$, and the wedge identity $Z^{1}\wedge Z^{2} = \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}X(x)$ for twistors built on the incidence line $\mu_{x}\pi + \pi$, at four points and two spinor pairs.

\emph{Part D: the grip theorem.} The spin isomorphism is solved exactly: for each rotation $R_{U\wedge V}$ the construction needs, the script finds the traceless $A$ whose action on every basis bivector equals that of the rotation. The nine rotations whose matrices Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism} displays (the grading, four translations, four special conformal generators) are compared with these solutions entry by entry. The moment map $M_{A}(Z^{1}, \dots, Z^{N}) := i\sum_{i=1}^{N} \bar{Z}^{i}\cdot(A Z^{i}), \qquad A \in \mathfrak{sl}(\T)$ and the grip of Definition \claimref{obj.mass.grip-mass-composite} are then built from these solutions, on ten twistor pairs: at $\Lambda = 0$, $Q(P) = 2|\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}|^{2}$ and $P \perp n_{\infty}$; the grip on $n_{0}$, $M(n_{0})$, has squared length $2|[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]|^{2}$; the cross term $\ip{P_{\infty}}{P_{0}}$ equals $p\cdot k - d^{2}$ with the three forms in the components of the proof, $\det t = \overline{\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}}[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]$, and equals $2\,\mathrm{Re}(\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}\overline{[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]}) + C$; and the theorem itself, $Q(P) = 2|B_{\Lambda}|^{2} + 2\lambda C$, as an identity in $\lambda$ (all three coefficients of the quadratic), with $m^{2}$ real, $P \perp I_{\Lambda}$, and $P_{\Lambda} = P_{\infty} + \lambda P_{0}$ recomputed independently at three values of $\lambda$. The identities for $C$ in the relation displayed with \claimref{mass.grip-real} and its nonnegativity. Lemma \claimref{mass.grip-real}: on four real points of the slice \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes}, every generator of a real pair (grading, translations, special conformal, Lorentz) has $\Sigma A$ anti-Hermitian, the commutator identity of the proof holds on all sixteen pairs of points, and the grip on $I_{\Lambda}$ has real pairing with $n_{\infty}$, $n_{0}$ and the four real vectors on all ten pairs, and the anti-Hermiticity condition on the eight real parameters of $x$ has rank four (Remark \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes}). The doubled composite's $m^{2} = 2\lambda(\bar{Z}\cdot Z)^{2}$ on all five twistors and the non-doubled massless pair of Theorem \claimref{mass.exact-join}(5). Proposition \claimref{mass.casimir-form-join}: both Casimirs formed from the exact moment components in adapted bases, the decomposition (1), the value (2) and the closed form (3) on four pairs, and $\tr\mathsf{E}^{2} = 1$ on the grading element. Lemma \claimref{mass.five-broken-generators}: the dimensions $10$, $6$, $5$ by exact rank, and the five matrices $A(e_{a}\wedge I_{\Lambda})$ traceless, independent, with $\Omega A$ antisymmetric.

\emph{Part E: the weight.} $\nu^{2} = 6|B_{\Lambda}|^{2}/\Lambda + C - \tfrac94$ on three pairs at two values of $\Lambda$, real and positive there; the expansion $\sqrt{1 - \tfrac94\epsilon^{2}} = 1 - \tfrac98\epsilon^{2} - \tfrac{81}{128}\epsilon^{4} + \cdots$, $\epsilon = H/m$, as an exact truncated power series.

What the script does not check: the conformal invariance of the Thomas operator (imported, Fact \claimref{mass.imported-thomas-operator}); the flat-model dictionary and the spin isomorphism as theorems (imported, Fact \claimref{mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-infinity}; the script solves the isomorphism on the basis but does not prove it is one); Schur's lemma behind Lemma \claimref{mass.invariant-forms-simple-lie-algebra} (imported); the de Sitter classification against which Corollary \claimref{mass.weight-polynomial-two-series} is read (imported, Fact \claimref{mass.imported-unitary-representations-de-sitter-group}); the ``only if'' of the massless locus in Theorem \claimref{mass.exact-join}(5), which is the positivity argument of the proof; the normalisation $1/\sqrt2$ of the real slice \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes}, which the script carries as a scalar; the identification of the real form in Lemma \claimref{mass.five-broken-generators} (that the stabiliser is $\mathfrak{so}(1,4)$, that the five are the de Sitter translations, and the match with the action paper's Goldstone count), the script working over the Gaussian rationals, with no real-form check beyond the anti-Hermiticity checks of Lemma \claimref{mass.grip-real}; the $N$-constituent formulas of successor problem (5); and Proposition \claimref{mass.casimir-form-join}(2) beyond $N = 2$.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.what-adds-dark-energ: The dark-energy paper proves the parabolic-to-reductive rotation of the stabiliser at $\Lambda \neq 0$ at the level of groups. Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed} is the same rotation at the level of the Clifford algebra: the null direction of the parabolic case is the nilpotent generator of a degenerate algebra, and the reductive case is that generator given a sign. That the tangent image keeps signature $(1,3)$ whatever $\Lambda$ does is Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed}(iv) read through Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue}.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.dictionary-ascents-n:
The correspondence between the frozen point and the pair the transport adjoins, stated in the root paper's normalisation (which fixes the null basis up to the dilation, one hyperbolic plane being isometric to any other). The adjoined plane has the signed basis $e_{\pm}$ and the null basis $v = \tfrac12(e_{+} + e_{-})$, $v^{*} = \tfrac12(e_{+} - e_{-})$, with $v^{2} = v^{*2} = 0$ and $vv^{*} + v^{*}v = 1$, the pair the root paper adjoins and the tower paper reads as the one fermionic mode of the rung \cite[\S 2.2]{ButlerT1}, \cite[Prop.~4.1, Thm.~4.2]{ButlerT3}. The note's canonical frame is the same two null rays, $v = I_{0}$ and $v^{*} = \varphi/2$. Then: at $\Lambda = 0$ the frozen point is the null generator $v$ itself, the zero divisor of vector type, and the direction the completion adjoins is its partner $v^{*}$, canonical by Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through}(i); the Stelle-West vector does not exist there. For $\Lambda \neq 0$ the frozen point is a combination of both null generators,
\[
I_{\Lambda} \;=\; \alpha\, v + \beta\, v^{*}, \qquad Q(I_{\Lambda}) = \alpha\beta = \Lambda/3 ,
\]
and the Stelle-West vector is the same two components with the relative sign reversed,
\[
V \;\propto\; \alpha\, v - \beta\, v^{*}, \qquad Q(V) \propto -\alpha\beta ,
\]
orthogonal to $I_{\Lambda}$ and to the Lorentz frame. So $I$ and $V$ are the sum and difference of one pair of null components, which is why they form the signed basis up to scale and a boost (Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed}(i)); the sign of $\Lambda$ is the relative sign of $\alpha$ and $\beta$, de Sitter when they agree and anti-de Sitter when they differ, and the wall is either of them vanishing. The dilation acts as $v \mapsto tv$, $v^{*} \mapsto v^{*}/t$, an automorphism of the relation $vv^{*} + v^{*}v = 1$, and $\alpha\beta$ is its invariant (Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.boost-dilation-ratio-gauge}); in the frame of Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through}, $\alpha = a$ and $\beta = 2b$. In the tower paper's reading of $v$ and $v^{*}$ as the annihilation and creation operators of the rung's mode, the frozen point of a $\Lambda = 0$ universe is a pure annihilator and a nonzero $\Lambda$ is a creation component, the product of the two coefficients being $\Lambda/3$; this is what that reading says verbatim; only the vanishing of the creation component is invariant, its size being the dilation gauge, and the note attaches no claim to the reading. The script verifies the null pair, its normalisation, the identification with the canonical frame, and the norms and orthogonality of $\alpha v \pm \beta v^{*}$ on instances of both signs and zero.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.two-bits-compared: The root paper's Rule 2 leaves a sign free too, the square of the generator adjoined to a type-C obstruction, and records that the completed algebra forgets it. The sign left free here is of a different kind. The completed algebra, the rung $\Cl(2,4)$, forgets it in the same way; but the intermediate algebra of Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed} remembers it, the doubled $\Cl(1,4)$ against the complexified $\Cl(2,3)$, because the base $\Cl(1,3)$ is even-dimensional and exactly one of the two single extensions changes the parity of $q$ (Lemma \claimref{odd-extensions.volume-element-odd-dimension}). So the sign of $\Lambda$ is a geometric datum with an algebraic witness one level below the rung, and the witness is what the section “The rung's even subalgebra is the anti-de Sitter algebra” used to separate the oriented towers.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.what-transport-stanc: The programme reads a zero divisor as a signpost rather than a prohibition, and Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed}(iii) puts $\Lambda = 0$ on the wall. It is tempting to read the stance as saying that a universe does not sit on the wall, hence $\Lambda \neq 0$. Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through} is what the stance actually delivers: the transport off the wall is the passage from $\Cl(1,3;1)$ to the rung, which is the same rung for every $\Lambda$, and it says nothing about where in the rung's new plane the frozen point lies. The dark-energy paper's finding that the norm is a parameter of the laws under the action as written is the dynamical form of the same statement, and this note does not improve on it.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.setting-wall-cosmolo: Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed} gives a one-parameter family of intermediate algebras, nondegenerate for $\Lambda \neq 0$ and degenerate at $\Lambda = 0$. The sheaf paper has a theory of exactly such families: tame corank-one degenerations, their exceptional algebras, the residue of the metric at the wall, and a conservation law that says the degeneracy of a wall in spacetime can be displaced but never destroyed. This section runs that theory on the $\Lambda$ line. The family is a tame wall in the sheaf paper's sense, and the rung completes it on both sides, which the conservation law forbids for the completions it covers; the family lies in the case the conservation theorem's proof excludes by hypothesis, a complement whose signature switches across the wall, and that case is generic to any corank-one family of hyperplanes in a fixed nondegenerate space. The section's content is the identification of the dark-energy paper's frozen-point geometry with the sheaf paper's tame structure, and the placement of the $\Lambda$ family in that excluded case.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.setting-what-note-de:
The note makes no prediction; no observation can refute its identifications, and the only observational input it uses is the sign of $\Lambda$, which selects which branch describes this universe (Remark \claimref{note.odd-extensions.what-says-what-it-does-not}). What it claims is a set of identifications, each proved in the note from imported results, and this section says which imported result each identification depends on and what falls with it.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(D1)] \emph{The frozen point.} Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed}, Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.translation-bivectors-frozen-point} and all of the section “The soldering decides”, the section “Running the transport on the wall”, the section “Two negative results” and the section “The wall in the cosmological constant” rest on the dark-energy paper's frozen point (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point}): the parallel scale tractor of norm $\Lambda/3$ with the Stelle-West vector as the fifth direction of $I^{\perp}$. Without it the algebra of the section “The frozen point splits the ascent's pair” is a statement about an arbitrary vector of the rung's hyperbolic plane with no physical referent.

__notes__.note.programme.abstract: This capstone surveys the Transport Papers, eighteen papers, the primer T0 and the research papers T1 to T17, built on one principle: division by zero in a Clifford algebra is not a prohibition but a forced transport of the description into a minimally completed higher algebra. The series carries that principle from pure algebra (the no-go, the taxonomy, the tower, the sheaf theory) through the black hole (folded light cones to the Page envelope), the companions (the weighted limit, the Hawking spectrum, the boundary mode space, twistors, the frozen point's action), the matter programme (mass, the Standard Model, families, dark towers, neutrinos), and the synthesis (one relation, two shadows). Three things gathered here lie in no single series paper. First, the method: seventeen natural conjectures attempted, sixteen refuted and one placed, each failure locating a better statement one level up, tabulated against the papers that now prove the corrected statements. Second, the status: every paper's payload, epistemic tier, and machine-verified check count in one table, 1762 exact checks across sixteen companion scripts. Third, the falsifiable claims: six registered stances and six conditional absences, each with its dataset, current confrontation, and refutation condition, and the descent measure they leave over: two numbers and one bit, the weak scale's unit still open. The survey's script audits page counts against the companion PDFs, check counts against the counts the companion papers record, and the tables against one another. Nothing here is verified by publication; the claim table is where refutation should begin.
__notes__.note.programme.setting-introduction:
A single question opens the series: what happens where division fails. In a Clifford algebra the failure is a geometric object, the null vector on its cone, and the series' founding principle treats the failure as prescribing the next step. Division by an isotropic vector is impossible at the level of elements, provably, in every mixed-signature algebra of dimension at least three (the hyperbolic plane is the one exception, and the idempotent type needs no repair at all); it becomes possible, uniquely and minimally, at the level of the space, by adjoining one hyperbolic plane and letting the undefined values be taken at the adjoined ideal points. The inverse operation never appears. That one principle, pursued mechanically through seventeen natural conjectures, sixteen of them refuted, generates the series this paper surveys: eighteen papers running from pure algebra to the black hole, the Standard Model, the dark sector, and the foundations of quantum mechanics.

This capstone is the one paper of the series whose subject is the series. It does three things that no companion paper can do for itself. It states the \emph{method}: the refutation discipline, the three epistemic tiers, and the house rules that hold every paper to them (the section “The method”); the roadmap of the series reserves this narrative for the capstone alone, so the companion papers state their results neutrally and cite here. It records the \emph{status}: one table carrying every paper's payload, tier, and machine-verified check count, so that a reader can see in one place what has been proved, at what standard, and what remains (the section “The series, paper by paper”). And it gathers the \emph{falsifiable claims}: every registered stance in one place with its dataset, its current confrontation date-stamped, and the measurement that would refute it, together with the descent measure the whole framework leaves unexplained: two numbers and one bit (the section “The falsifiable claims” and the section “The measure: two numbers and one bit”). The closing sections carry the series' open directions, each item with the paper it is now assigned to, and the thesis the whole programme argues for: a theory of singularities in which a singularity is not a wall but an interface (the section “The open directions” and the section “The successor programme: a theory of singularities”).

One property of this paper is structural and is declared up front: it is \emph{kept current}. Every status line here depends on results that are, at this writing, under review; when review changes a source paper, the corresponding line here changes. The paper is therefore built to be mechanically refreshable: its tables are compiled from the series' own verified numbers, and its verification script audits the page counts quoted here against the companion PDFs, the check counts against the counts the companion papers record (or, on request, against a fresh run of every companion script), and the tables against one another, so that a stale quotation is a failing check rather than a silent error. The version of record is whichever compilation postdates the series it describes.
__notes__.note.programme.setting-prior-art: The sources of a survey are its series: the companion primer \cite{ButlerT0}, the sixteen research companions \cite{ButlerT1, ButlerT2, ButlerT3, ButlerT4, ButlerT5, ButlerT6, ButlerT7, ButlerT8, ButlerT9, ButlerT10, ButlerT11, ButlerT12, ButlerT13, ButlerT14, ButlerT15, ButlerT16}. The method itself has prior art and the paper says so: the discipline of exposing conjectures to refutation and treating each failure as information is Popper's \cite{Popper1963}, and the idea that a research programme should be judged by whether its problem-shifts are progressive, by what its refutations force it to predict next, is Lakatos's \cite{Lakatos1978}. What this paper claims under the name of method is not those philosophies but their unusually literal execution: a numbered refutation table, a declared standard of proof on every result, machine verification deposited with every computational paper, and registered predictions with named refutation conditions, maintained as a running discipline across one body of mathematics. The individual scientific sources (Hestenes' geometric algebra, Penrose's twistors, tractor calculus, MacDowell-Mansouri, bosonisation, modular theory, the Everett literature, and the rest) are acknowledged in the prior-art sections of the papers that use them, and this survey does not repeat those declarations except where a specific claim is discussed.
__notes__.note.programme.setting-contribution: (1) The method stated as method, with the refutations tabulated against the series papers that carry the corrected statements (the section “The method”). (2) The status table, per series paper, with tiers and check counts (the section “The series, paper by paper”). (3) The falsifiable claims: six registered stances and six conditional absences with datasets, current confrontations, and refutation conditions (the section “The falsifiable claims”). (4) The descent measure gathered: two numbers and one bit, with the verification that fixed the count (the section “The measure: two numbers and one bit”). (5) The open directions: the programme's open problems with the papers they are assigned to (the section “The open directions”). (6) The singularity thesis and the pattern's other applications (the section “The successor programme: a theory of singularities”). (7) A verification script that audits the page and check counts this survey quotes against the companion PDFs and the companion papers' recorded counts, and the survey's tables against one another \cite{ButlerVerifyT17}.
__notes__.note.programme.setting-three-tiers: Every paper in the series is assigned one of three epistemic tiers, and every result inside a paper declares its own level, so that typography matches epistemic content everywhere. Where a paper declares its tier itself, in its abstract or its introduction, the status table of the section “The series, paper by paper” records that declaration; where it does not, the tier in the table is this survey's assignment. Tier A papers (the algebra arc) are theorem papers: complete proofs at journal-mathematics standard, nothing conditional. Tier B papers (the geometric and quantum companions) are assembly papers: their proofs rest on named established theorems (Bisognano-Wichmann, MacDowell-Mansouri, Kostant, Araki, the Penrose transform), with the assembly steps itemised so a reader can see exactly which steps the paper proves and which it imports. Tier C papers (the programme papers of the matter arc and the foundations) derive from flagged structural premises, with the premises stated in their own environments, attacked in their own subsections where the roadmap demands it, and quantified by registered predictions with named refutation conditions. The tiers are the declared shape of a programme that runs from pure algebra to cosmology. A Tier C paper that states five ways it could be refuted is doing its job as well as a Tier A paper that proves its theorems.
__notes__.note.programme.setting-house-rules-why: Thirteen house rules bind every draft in the series; four carry the method and their rationale is given here. \emph{The Fact (imported) discipline}: the Theorem and Proof environments are reserved for results proved in that paper at full standard; anything imported (from an earlier series paper or the literature) is stated in a visually distinct Fact environment with its precise provenance. The rule exists because a chain paper that states imports as Theorems claims a standard it has not met. \emph{Machine verification}: every computational paper deposits a script, exact rational arithmetic wherever possible, no floating point, importing the series' shared exact-arithmetic library; across the sixteen companion scripts the series currently carries 1762 exact checks, every one passing, and several of the series' own errors (sign conventions, citation slips, a silently failing macro) were caught by the checks rather than by reading. \emph{Per-theorem scope}: each theorem carries its own hypotheses, and sharp boundaries (the hyperbolic atom, the AVTD class, the s-wave sector, the Gaussian class, even transport charge) are stated as results rather than buried as caveats, because a boundary stated as a result is where the next paper starts. \emph{Registered stances}: where the framework touches data it registers a position in advance, date-stamps the confrontation, and names the measurement that would refute it; the section “The falsifiable claims” is the gathered table, and the rule's rationale is the whole paper.
__notes__.note.programme.setting-series-paper-pape: The series is eighteen papers in six arcs, with two lettered companions to T14 (T14a, the odd extensions; T14b, the simulations), each paper one self-contained theorem cluster proved at the standard of its field. Arc A is the algebra (T1 through T4, with the primer T0 as its companion): the transport principle with its taxonomy of obstructions and transport rules, the applied completion note, the tower, and the sheaf theory over degenerate metrics. Arc B is the black hole (T5, T6): T5 chain from the folded light cones to the Page envelope, and its mathematical-relativity companion. Arc C is the quantum companions (T7, T8): the Hawking spectrum's state and lift, and the singularity's boundary mode space: its counting, scrambling, and observational record. Arc D is identification (T9, T10): the twistor correspondence and the action of the frozen point. Arc E is matter (T11 through T15): mass, the Standard Model, families, the dark towers, and the neutrino sector. Arc F is synthesis (T16 and this capstone). The eighteen papers are numbered consecutively, T0 through T17.

a table of the original is the status table: each paper's current version, its payload in one line, its epistemic tier, its machine verification, and what remains. Two conventions govern it. The tier column records the paper's declared tier, with the per-result levels stated in the papers themselves; and the verification column counts the exact checks in the paper's deposited script, all of which pass, for a series total of 1762 checks across the sixteen companion scripts T1 to T16 (the primer's small script and this paper's audit are counted separately in the section “Machine verification”). The page counts in the table are audited by that script against the compiled PDFs, and the check counts against the counts the companion papers record, or against a fresh run of every companion script when the audit is invoked that way.

__notes__.note.programme.setting-measure-two-numbe:
Every quantitative freedom the framework retains has been counted into one small object, and this section states it, with the one scale the count does not yet place. What the framework's laws contain, as derived across the series, is \emph{initial data of the descent}, and the count across T12, T14, and T16 gives that data as two continuous numbers and one discrete bit. Beside it stands the weak scale: the Standard-Model paper's status proposition leaves the rung unit $v/M_{P} \approx 2 \times 10^{-17}$ not derived, and either a second continuous number or an instance of the first, while its first successor problem records that this unit is rescaling-invariant and so not kinematically an instance of $N$ (in Hubble units $v/H = N\,v/M_{P} \approx 10^{44}$ inherits $N$); until it is placed, the count of two numbers is the count of the descent's data and not of every unexplained dimensionless constant \cite{ButlerT12}. The count's subject, dimensionless, is defined once the third constant is placed: the synthesis paper places $c$ as the conversion constant between the Witt chart and the metric chart, a conformal invariant below both $\hbar$ and $G$, and the three placements close the unit system, the exponent matrix of $(c, \hbar, G)$ over length, time and mass having determinant $-2$, so that every remaining constant is a dimensionless ratio \cite{ButlerT16}.

The first number is $N = M_{P}/H$, about $1.0 \times 10^{61}$, the square root, up to $\sqrt{\pi/\ln 2}$, of the universe's horizon mode count (about $4.8 \times 10^{122}$ under the black hole's counting rule). The Standard Model paper proves the compression as monomial identities: the strength of gravity ($G\Lambda = 3N^{-2}$), the weakness of matter's self-gravity ($N^{-2}$), and the hierarchy of the weak scale ($\operatorname{Im} w = (m/M_{P})\,N$) are one number for the first two, by the definition of $N$, while the third also carries the rung unit; the trichotomy classifies $N$: its coincidence with the present age is epochal, Dirac's law being excluded by the registered and conditional $w = -1$ prediction; it is not a dynamical variable (by the frozen point's rigidity); and it is a datum of the descent, dated to the origin, on one condition the action paper now names: under the action as written $N$ is a parameter of the laws, constant on every solution and varying across the family of theories, and it is initial data only if the Stelle-West norm is promoted to a Lagrange-multiplier field whose constancy is an equation of motion, a decision the series records open with both branches stated \cite{ButlerT12, ButlerT10}; the companion T14a \cite{ButlerT14a} states the same freedom at the level of the algebra, the transport returning the rung and a canonical null frame and constraining the frozen point only through its norm $\Lambda/3$. The second number is $\epsilon$, the strength of the matter asymmetry, carried as a declared stance and not a classification: the dark-matter paper has the framework inherit its asymmetry as initial data of the descent rather than generate it, and its universality across the oriented towers is a theorem for the mirror and void for the odd residues \cite{ButlerT14}. The bit is the orientation of the planted Witt flag, and the seventeenth refutation argues it is a bit on three stated premises, CPT covariance of the derived gauge sector, the Standard-Model paper's Hypothesis (S), and the exhaustiveness of the trichotomy: CPT conjugation is a covariance of every kinematic structure the series checks, so on those premises the absolute orientation is underivable, and the framework locates what it cannot determine. That one bit is spent once and read twice: it is the matter-antimatter asymmetry's sign and it is the arrow of time, the same choice in two readings \cite{ButlerT14}, and the synthesis paper proves at $\Cl(1,3)$ level that the two readings cannot come apart, given the law \cite{ButlerT16}; on the two-time fork the bit exists but the arrow does not, so there it is read once.

Backward, it is a constraint: because the count is fixed on its audited premises ($\epsilon$ a declared stance, the deposit energy a datum the framework does not fix, and, for the bit, the three premises of the seventeenth refutation, Hypothesis (S) among them), any proposal that requires fresh uncaused choices is not an open alternative within the framework, and the synthesis paper uses exactly this closure against dynamical collapse, which would produce one new uncaused bit per measurement event against a total of one on those premises \cite{ButlerT16}.

__notes__.note.programme.setting-thesis:
The programme's thesis can now be stated in one sentence, with every clause carried by a series paper rather than a promise: \emph{a singularity is not a place where physics ends but an interface where the description is forced up one level}, element to point \cite{ButlerT1}, metric to conformal \cite{ButlerT4, ButlerT6}, classical value to operator, c-number to ladder \cite{ButlerT3, ButlerT5}, by a completion that is minimal, unique, and one-way \cite{ButlerT1}. On this reading the singularity is a functor to be applied, not a pathology to be excised: its degeneration type determines its completion \cite{ButlerT1}; its rate of degeneration builds its exceptional geometry \cite{ButlerT4}; its blow-up weights are its Kasner exponents \cite{ButlerT6}; its boundary dynamics is a Levi excitation \cite{ButlerT6}; its field equations vacate exactly the directions its completion fills \cite{ButlerT10}; its modes are thermal at the temperature set by its own boost plane \cite{ButlerT5}; and its information deficit is a fixed, algebraically tracked projection rather than a loss \cite{ButlerT5}. The synthesis places the thesis inside a larger one: the completion functor acts on a spacetime already made, point by point, of the algebra's null elements, every point a projective line of quantum vacua, so a singularity is not where non-invertibility begins but where the vacuum family degenerates \cite{ButlerT16}.

Each clause is falsifiable in principle, and three tests are concrete enough to name. The BKL-weight identification can be tested in numerical relativity: Hubble-normalised holonomy should converge at the predicted power-law rate near generic singularities and fail to converge, in the predicted axis-rotating manner, in oscillatory ones. The mode count, repeated over the Kerr ring, must reproduce the known angular-momentum dependence of Kerr entropy or refute the counting (a table of the original, item 4).
