__notes__.note.programme.setting-other-application: The pattern (a classical description divides by zero; a completed description resolves it at the level of a larger space; the divergence is confined to a scale while a shape survives) is not specific to black holes. Cosmology is its principal successor, on four counts: isotropic big-bang singularities are conformally far tamer than black-hole interiors, so the tame sheaf theory applies to the early universe more directly than to the objects it was built for; the shadow wall gives the interface between aeons in cyclic proposals a precise algebraic description; signature change is already inside the formalism, as the clash of ascents at Euclidean-Lorentzian walls; and the programme's own dating places the descent at the origin, reading the big bang as the freezing itself, with $\Lambda$ the residue of that origin, $N$ the number that fixes the boundary modes it opened, and the dynamics of the first freezing left to cosmology as the framework's last question \cite{ButlerT12, ButlerT14}. Outside gravity, the oldest instance of the pattern is optics: a caustic is a locus where the ray description divides by zero, and its resolution by wave optics, the Airy function replacing the infinity and the Maslov index recording a monodromy, is a small instance of the transport principle. Analogue-gravity systems, whose effective acoustic metrics degenerate at sonic horizons, inherit the results wholesale. And one application is resolutely practical: engineering and robotics already compute in projective and conformal geometric algebra, where kinematic singularities are corank drops of a Jacobian, and the completion prescription (adjoin the dying direction, re-metrised by its rate of degeneration) is an algorithm that may yield principled regularisations where current practice damps singularities ad hoc \cite{ButlerT2}.
__notes__.note.programme.setting-machine-verificat:
A survey proves little and quotes much, so its script has a different task from the companion scripts': it is a \emph{consistency audit}. The script \texttt{verify\_T17.py} \cite{ButlerVerifyT17} imports the series' shared exact-arithmetic library \texttt{GA.py}; exact rationals, integers, and certified interval brackets throughout, no floating point anywhere; seventy-five checks when every companion file is present, all passing, in six parts. What it audits is stated exactly. For each of the seventeen companion papers T0 to T16 it opens the companion's compiled PDF and reads the page count from the file's own page tree, and it reads the companion's check count from the count the companion paper records in the version block of its source (or, when invoked with \texttt{--run-siblings}, from a fresh run of the companion script, counting the PASS lines it prints), and compares both with the status table and with the script's own recorded values; a companion file that is absent is reported as skipped, never as passing. It parses this paper's four tables from the source and counts their rows. It recomputes the physical numbers the paper quotes. Because this paper is kept current, the audit is also its refresh mechanism: when a review round changes a companion's page or check count, the corresponding check fails until this survey is regenerated, so a stale quotation is a reported error rather than a silent one.

\emph{Part A: the series' counts} (forty-seven checks). The paper inventory (eighteen papers, numbered consecutively, the identifiers 0 through 17 read from the file stems); the status table parsed and compared with the recorded page and check counts; the series total of 1762 computed from the recorded counts and compared with every place the body prints it; seventeen page counts read from the companion PDFs; seventeen check counts read from the companion papers' records or scripts; the version column read against the version printed on the title page of each of the twenty papers in the table; the refutation table's rows covering the ordinals 1 to 17 exactly once, each row naming its carrying paper; the stance table's six-plus-six, numbered in order; the ten open directions, each assigned; the measure's cardinality, two numbers and one bit, at each site the paper states it; and this paper's own compile log, which must carry no float-overflow warning (every table here is a breakable longtable) and no undefined reference.

\emph{Part B: the black-hole numbers}, as exact monomials in $\pi$ and $M$: $\beta = 8\pi M$ with $\beta/2\pi = 4M$; the epoch volume $V = \beta^{2} = 64\pi^{2}M^{2}$; the equivalence $\nu = 1/16\pi \iff N_{\mathrm{epoch}} = \nu V = 4\pi M^{2} = S_{\mathrm{BH}}$; and the naive count's overshoot by exactly $16\pi$, the horizon-area coefficient.

\emph{Part C: the dark count.} The sterile residues computed as the fixed points of $r \mapsto -r$ mod 8 (exactly $\{0, 4\}$); the count of five dark causal residues; and the ratio arithmetic T14 states, with five entering none of it: the symmetric remainder $4.364 = 5.364 - 1$ once the mirror's one share is removed; that remainder as $\Omega h^{2} = 4.364 \times 0.02237$, inside $0.0976 \pm 0.0012$; and the mirror's share of the dark density, $1/5.364$, between $18.6$ and $18.7$ percent.

\emph{Part D: the matter numbers.} The two exact one-loop rationals ($78761/379488$ and $6539/28320$) bracketed to four decimals, with the over-twenty-times-closer inequality against the measured angle; the integer bracket $2^{398} < 10^{120} < 2^{399}$; the hypercharge quadratic's roots, sum, and product; $3/8$ as the exact trace ratio; the frozen-point norm $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ as a rational-function identity in formal $\Lambda$, and the dictionary's sign, $m^{2} = -w(w+3)\Lambda/3$, positive at the midpoint $w = -\tfrac32$ of the real interval $[-3, 0]$ and negative at $w = 1$ outside it, with the principal-series form $m^{2} = (\nu^{2} + \tfrac94)\Lambda/3$ at $w = -\tfrac32 + I_4\nu$ (numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$) as a polynomial identity in formal $\nu$; and the compression identity $G\Lambda N^{2} = 3$.

\emph{Part E: the neutrino numbers}, by certified interval arithmetic (integer-square-root brackets on the mass-squared splittings): the normal-ordering floor confined to $(0.057, 0.061)$ eV and containing the predicted $0.059$; the $0.052$ eV zero-extending-prior bound strictly below the floor; the $0.092$ eV physical-prior bound above it; the inverted-ordering requirement above $0.097$ eV; the two $m_{\beta\beta}$ values recomputed from the splittings and the mixing brackets under the hierarchy premise and real breaking, bracketing $1.5$ and $3.7$ meV inside the hull $1.3$ to $3.9$ meV and below next-generation sensitivity; the quoted Koide value inside $2/3 \pm 10^{-5}$; and the Cabibbo bracket containing $0.225$.

What the audit does not and cannot check is what no script can: whether the source papers' proofs are correct (their own scripts and Leon's review carry that), whether the tiers are correctly assigned, whether the payload and remainder cells describe their papers faithfully, and whether the method section's claims about method are true of the practice. The audit guarantees a weaker and more useful thing: that the page and check counts this survey quotes are the companions' own, that its tables agree with one another, and that the physical numbers it repeats recompute.

dark-energy.conclusion-does-not-depend-o.formal: The gravitational-engineering conclusion, that the metric-forming structure admits exactly one coupling sector (stress-energy), with no selective coupling, no enhanced source and no enhanced detector at first order, holds on either reading of the graviton's ontology, with a different level on each. If the graviton is the framework's collective mode: by derivation, Propositions \claimref{dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip} and \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation} at proof level within the s-wave sector and Assembly \claimref{dark-energy.lift-inherits-no-go-steps-itemised} for the lift. If the graviton is fundamental: by Weinberg's soft theorem \cite{Weinberg1964}, the leading low-energy coupling of any massless spin-two particle is universal, which is the equivalence principle and rules out a selective coupling at leading order; non-minimal couplings, subleading in energy, are not excluded by the theorem, so the fundamental branch delivers the conclusion at leading order only. The conclusion is therefore common ground between the ontologies at leading order; what is distinctive to the composite reading is the ultraviolet behaviour (quantisation as output; no graviton loops to renormalise), the derivation of weakness as dimensional suppression (Remark \claimref{note.dark-energy.weakness-dimension-nonlinear-bound-open-items}), and the $\ell_P^2/A$ corrections carried by the spectrum paper; the discriminating experiments, if any, lie in those corrections, and the asymmetry (hard to refute, hard to confirm below the Planck scale) is stated rather than hidden. The steps: the composite branch is the cited chain with its declared levels; the fundamental branch is the imported theorem read within its scope; the structural consequence recorded is that were the composite reading wrong, the leading-order conclusion would survive it.
dark-energy.conclusion-does-not-depend-o.technical:
The engineering conclusion is that the metric-forming structure admits exactly one coupling sector, stress-energy, with no selective coupling, no enhanced source and no enhanced detector at first order. On the composite reading of the graviton it follows from the acoustic no-go and the pure-gauge character of the $(I,V)$-sector, proved within the s-wave sector, together with the itemised lift to four dimensions, at the levels those steps carry. On the fundamental reading it follows from Weinberg's soft theorem: the leading low-energy coupling of any massless spin-two particle is universal. Non-minimal couplings, subleading in energy, are not excluded by that theorem, so this branch gives the conclusion at leading order only.

The conclusion is therefore common ground between the two ontologies at leading order. What distinguishes the composite reading lies elsewhere: its ultraviolet behaviour, weakness as dimensional suppression, and the $\ell_P^2/A$ corrections, which is where any discriminating experiment would have to look.
dark-energy.conclusion-does-not-depend-o.lay: Can anything couple to gravity more strongly or more selectively than ordinary mass and energy do? This result says no, at first order, whether the graviton is a fundamental particle or a collective mode of deeper structure. Each reading reaches the verdict by a different route and at a different level: the composite route is proved within the simplest (s-wave) sector and carried to four dimensions by assembly, while the fundamental route covers only the leading effect at low energy. So the verdict on gravitational engineering, at leading order, would survive even if the composite picture turned out to be wrong.

\item \emph{(The datum's pole.)} At the singular locus $r = 0$ of the Schwarzschild gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) the frozen-point datum is regular in the exceptional chart except for a simple pole of the connection in its Levi-Civita block, the rotation-gauge field $\Omega$, with tangential legs, residue $-\sum_i p_iB_i\otimes\hat e^i$ (the sign of the Definition): Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-datum-kasner-wall}(i) on the Kasner model, transported to Schwarzschild by Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-weighted-limit-schwarzschild-singularity-matching} (the geometry paper's weighted limit, values-level, with its $O(\tau^{2/3})$ corrections in the boost block and $O(\tau^{1/3})$ in the rotation block).
\item \emph{(The residues satisfy the wall's field equations.)} The exponents obey the Kasner relations, which are the leading-order field equations, and the second relation is the statement that the residue bivector is a unit boost: Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-datum-kasner-wall}(ii), \cite[Prop.~8.26(3)]{ButlerT4}.
\item \emph{(The residues are the completion's weights.)} The sheaf paper's completion at this wall is built on weights that are forced, once the dying direction is named, to equal the Kasner exponents: \cite[Thm.~8.16]{ButlerT4}; and its exceptional frame is the frame in which (1) holds: \cite[Thm.~8.27]{ButlerT4}.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, at this wall, the field equations neither merely permit the completion nor demand it as a further condition: their own singular locus supplies the data the completion is built from. The pole of the dynamical connection is not removable (step 1), its residues are fixed by the equations (step 2), and those residues are the weights of the completion (step 3). This is the forcing half of the section “What the equations vacate, and what cannot evolve” answered in the residue sense. Three qualifications are discharged below: the cosmological corrections leave the residue unchanged (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.cosmological-constant-does-not-change-residue}); the divergent curvature-squared \emph{value} is removed by a local wall counterterm that does not change the equations (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.wall-counterterm}); and the residue statement holds pointwise for variable exponents in the diagonal class (Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.variable-exponents-residue-pointwise-corrections-are}), with the momentum constraints and the non-diagonal class remaining as the dynamical half of the sheaf paper's connection-level matching \cite[Rem.~8.28]{ButlerT4}.
dark-energy.forcing-half-schwarzschild-w.technical:
At the singular locus of the Schwarzschild field on flat spacetime the frozen-point datum is regular in the exceptional chart except for a simple pole of the connection's Levi-Civita block, the rotation-gauge field, with tangential legs, of residue $-\sum_i p_i B_i\otimes\hat e^i$ with $B_i = e_0\wedge e_i$: this is the Kasner computation, transported to Schwarzschild by the weighted limit at values level. The exponents obey the Kasner relations $\sum_i p_i = 1 = \sum_i p_i^2$, which are the leading-order field equations, and the second relation says that the residue bivector is a unit boost. The weights of the sheaf completion at this wall are forced to equal the Kasner exponents, and its exceptional frame is the frame in which the pole is computed.

Together: the pole is not removable, its residues are fixed by the field equations, and those residues are the weights of the completion. So at this wall the equations' own singular locus supplies the data the completion is built from, which answers the forcing question in the residue sense; the momentum constraints and the non-diagonal class remain as the dynamical half of the connection-level matching.
dark-energy.forcing-half-schwarzschild-w.lay: Near the central singularity of a black hole, Einstein's equations break down in a specific, structured way: one part of the gravitational field blows up like one over the time remaining, with coefficients that the leading-order equations themselves fix. Those coefficients turn out to be exactly the numbers on which the series' completion of the geometry at the singularity is built. So at this wall, in this residue sense, the equations do not merely tolerate the completion; they supply its ingredients. The dynamical half of the matching (the momentum constraints and the non-diagonal case) is left open.

dark-energy.four-alternatives-are-exhaus.formal: Every conserved $q$ is (D), (P) or (I), and exactly one of them; (K) can hold together with any of them and is excluded by none; (D) implies (K), while (P) and (I) are compatible with (K) and with its negation. A conserved $q$ that is neither (K), (D) nor (I) is (P). Hence the inference ``not kinematic, not dynamical, therefore initial data'' is valid only if (P) is excluded.
dark-energy.four-alternatives-are-exhaus.technical:
For a theory with kinematic structure $\mathcal{K}$ and actions $S_\mu$ with solution spaces $\mathcal{S}_\mu$, a conserved quantity $q$ is exactly one of: dynamically fixed (D), constant on $\bigcup_\mu\mathcal{S}_\mu$; a parameter of the laws (P), constant on each $\mathcal{S}_\mu$ but not on the union; or initial data (I), not constant on some $\mathcal{S}_\mu$. Being kinematic (K) can hold together with any of the three and is excluded by none; (D) implies (K), while (P) and (I) are compatible with (K) and with its negation.

Hence a conserved $q$ that is neither (K), (D) nor (I) is (P), and the inference "not kinematic, not dynamical, therefore initial data" is valid only once (P) has been excluded.
dark-energy.four-alternatives-are-exhaus.lay: A number in a physical theory can be fixed by the dynamics, can be a setting of the laws themselves, or can vary from one solution to another as initial data. These three options exclude one another and cover every case, while being kinematic is a separate question. So ruling out kinematic and dynamical does not leave initial data as the only possibility: the number might be a parameter of the laws.
dark-energy.four-alternatives-are-exhaus.typing_note: The proof is a case split on the definition alone, so the only edge added is the about link to the four-ways definition.

proofs.main: Either $q$ is constant on every $\mathcal{S}_\mu$ or it is not. If not, it is (I). If so, either its common value is the same for all $\mu$, which is (D), or it is not, which is (P). The three cases are disjoint by construction and cover every $q$; (K) is a statement about factoring through $\mathcal{K}$, which none of the three excludes; (D) implies it, since a constant factors through every kinematic class, while (P) and (I) are compatible with (K) and with its negation (a kinematic invariant can be constant, parameter-dependent, or vary within a solution space, according to how $\mathcal{K}$ is embedded in the configuration space). The last sentence is the contrapositive of the disjunction.

dark-energy.frozen-point-datum-kasner-wa.formal:
Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be the synchronous diagonal gravitational field on flat spacetime with $\hb^{-1}(e_0) = e_0$, $\hb^{-1}(e_i) = a_i e_i$ on the background frame of the labels $(\tau, x^i)$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}; derived metric, in components, $g = d\tau^2 - \sum_i a_i(\tau)^2(dx^i)^2$), a solution of the Einstein equations with cosmological constant $\Lambda \neq 0$ in the diagonal Bianchi I class of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.cosmological-constant-does-not-change-residue}, with residue $(p_1,p_2,p_3)$ at $\tau = 0$ and $p_1p_2p_3 \neq 0$ (which excludes exactly the permutations of $(1,0,0)$, the flat Milne point, where every curvature below vanishes and the pole is a coordinate horizon), so that $a_i = \tau^{p_i}(1 + O(\Lambda\tau^2))$ and the Kasner field $a_i = \tau^{p_i}$ (derived metric $d\tau^2 - \sum_i\tau^{2p_i}(dx^i)^2$) is its leading term; the physical frame is $\{e_0, e_i\}$, the unit physical vectors over the background directions $\hb(e_0) = e_0$, $\hb(e_i) = e_i/a_i$ (in components, the orthonormal coframe $e^0 = d\tau$, $e^i = a_i\,dx^i$), and $\omega(e_a) := \Omega(\hb(e_a))$. Let the ambient datum be that of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}: $I = \nInf + \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\nO$ and $X = \nO$ (tractor components $(1, 0, \Lambda/6)$ and $(0, 0, 1)$), and $\nabla$ the tractor connection \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry}, on flat spacetime the $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field $\Omega_{T}(a) = \Omega(a) - \nInf\wedge\hb^{-1}(a) + \nO\wedge\Sch(\hb^{-1}(a))$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}, whose Schouten map is $\Sch(a) = \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}a$ because the field is Einstein. (An exact Kasner metric is Ricci-flat and carries the null frozen point of $\Lambda = 0$. The statements of (i) and (ii) and the Gauss-Bonnet density of (iii) are computed on the leading Kasner term, with $\Lambda$ entering only through the Schouten summand, and hold verbatim for the exact Kasner metric at $\Lambda = 0$, the Schwarzschild exponents included; $\Lambda \neq 0$ is needed only for the statements about the curvature-squared form of the action, which are made on the Einstein family.) Then, in the orthonormal frame, which for the Schwarzschild-de Sitter interior is the sheaf paper's exceptional chart (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-weighted-limit-schwarzschild-singularity-matching} with Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.cosmological-constant-does-not-change-residue}), at leading order in $\tau$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(What is regular, and what is not.)} $I$ and $X$ are constant, of constant norm $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$, $Q(X) = 0$; the soldering $\Omega_{T}(a)\times X = \hb^{-1}(a)$, on the physical frame $e_a$, is regular of full rank; and the soldering and Schouten summands of $\Omega_{T}$ on the physical frame, $\Omega_{T}(\hb(e_a)) - \omega(e_a) = -\nInf\wedge e_a + \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\nO\wedge e_a$, are constant (in components, the constant matrices $\eta_{ab}$ and $(\Lambda/6)\eta_{ab}$). The only singular part of the datum is the Levi-Civita block, the rotation-gauge field, and its leading term is a simple pole:
\[
\omega(e_i) \;=\; -\frac{p_i}{\tau}\, B_i, \qquad \omega(e_0) = 0, \qquad B_i = e_0\wedge e_i ,
\]
in the sign of the Definition, $D_a = a \cdot \nabla + \Omega(a) \times$ (in components, a labelled reading: the Cartan forms $\omega^{i0} = (p_i/\tau)\,e^i$, $\omega^{ij} = 0$, which that sign takes to minus the boosts), with residue the bivector-valued linear map $a \mapsto -\sum_i p_i\,(a\cdot e^i)\,B_i$ of physical vectors, which vanishes on $e_0$: its legs are tangential to the wall (in components $-\sum_i p_i\,B_i\otimes \hat e^i$). It is not a gauge pole: its field strength is a double pole,
\[
\mathcal{R}(B_i) \;=\; \frac{p_i(p_i - 1)}{\tau^2}\, B_i, \qquad \mathcal{R}(e_i\wedge e_j) \;=\; \frac{p_i p_j}{\tau^2}\, e_i\wedge e_j \quad (i \neq j),
\]
in the store's sign (in components, the curvature two-forms $R^{i0} = \frac{p_i(p_i - 1)}{\tau^2}\, e^0\wedge e^i$ and $R^{ij} = -\frac{p_i p_j}{\tau^2}\, e^i\wedge e^j$). The datum therefore does not extend regularly across the wall in this chart, and in no chart: the Euler density of (iii) equals $\det(\hb)^{-1}$ times the Kretschmann scalar $2\langle\mathcal{R}(a\wedge b)\,\mathcal{R}(\partial_b\wedge\partial_a)\rangle$ on an Einstein field, because $-4\,\mathcal{R}(\partial_a)\cdot\mathcal{R}(a) + (\partial_a\cdot\mathcal{R}(a))^2 = -16\Lambda^2 + 16\Lambda^2 = 0$, so the Kretschmann scalar is $-16p_1p_2p_3\tau^{-4}$ at leading order, divergent when $p_1p_2p_3 \neq 0$, and a curvature scalar is gauge-invariant.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The field equations at the wall are conditions on the residue.)} In the store's curvature convention, that of the geometry paper, in which de Sitter has $\mathcal{R}(a) = \Lambda a$ and $\Sch(a) = \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}a$ (the convention that makes $I$ parallel), the Ricci map is diagonal on the physical frame,
\[
\tau^2\,\mathcal{R}(e_0) = \Bigl(\sum_i p_i^2 - \sum_i p_i\Bigr)e_0, \qquad \tau^2\,\mathcal{R}(e_i) = p_i\Bigl(\sum_j p_j - 1\Bigr)e_i
\]
(in components $R_{00} = e_0\cdot\mathcal{R}(e_0)$ and $R_{ii} = e_i\cdot\mathcal{R}(e_i)$, so $\tau^2 R_{ii} = -p_i(\sum_j p_j - 1)$),
so the vacuum equations at leading order are exactly the Kasner relations $\sum_i p_i = 1 = \sum_i p_i^2$; the second says that the residue bivector $-B_w$, with $B_w = \sum_i p_i B_i$, is a unit boost. With $\Lambda$ the Einstein-$\Lambda$ system of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.cosmological-constant-does-not-change-residue} replaces Ricci-flatness at relative order $\Lambda\tau^2$ and does not affect the residue.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The action at the wall.)} On the Kasner approach the three terms of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(2) have densities, per unit $d\tau\,d^3x$ and with the volume factor $\det(\hb)^{-1} = a_1a_2a_3 = \tau$ at leading order,
\[
E\,\det(\hb)^{-1} = -16\,p_1p_2p_3\;\tau^{-3}, \qquad
-2\,\bigl(\partial_a\cdot\mathcal{R}(a)\bigr)\det(\hb)^{-1} = O(\Lambda\,\tau), \qquad
24\,\det(\hb)^{-1} = 24\,\tau ,
\]
with $E = 2\langle\mathcal{R}(a\wedge b)\,I_4^{-1}\,\mathcal{R}(I_4\partial_b\wedge\partial_a)\rangle$ the Euler density, $I_4 = e_0e_1e_2e_3$ the pseudoscalar (in components, a labelled reading: these are $\epsilon_{abcd}R^{ab}\wedge R^{cd}$, $\epsilon_{abcd}\,e^a e^b R^{cd}$ and $\epsilon_{abcd}\,e^ae^be^ce^d$ against $d\tau\wedge d^3x$). For the Schwarzschild-de Sitter exponents $p_1p_2p_3 = -4/27$ and the first density is $\tfrac{64}{27}\tau^{-3}$ (for Schwarzschild itself, $\Lambda = 0$, this is the divergence of the bare Gauss-Bonnet integrand, $\det(\hb)^{-1}$ times the Kretschmann scalar $64/(27\tau^4)$): the curvature-squared form of the action diverges at the wall as $\tau^{-2}$, through the topological term alone, which is exact and contributes nothing to the field equations; the Einstein-Cartan and cosmological terms are finite. The value of the frozen-point action is not defined at the singularity; its variational principle is, and its equations reach the wall as the residue conditions of (ii).
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Level:} (i)-(iii) proved by the displayed computations on the leading Kasner term, which the script confirms in exact arithmetic at two rational Kasner exponent triples and two non-Kasner points (where the Ricci tensor is confirmed nonzero), with the $\Lambda$-corrections controlled by Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.cosmological-constant-does-not-change-residue}; the script also runs the excluded point $(1,0,0)$ and confirms that every curvature coefficient and the Gauss-Bonnet density vanish there, so the hypothesis $p_1p_2p_3 \neq 0$ is needed. The application to the Schwarzschild and Schwarzschild-de Sitter interiors is through Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-weighted-limit-schwarzschild-singularity-matching}; the Kantowski-Sachs sphere adds its own relative corrections, $O(\tau^{1/3})$ in the rotation block and $O(\tau^{2/3})$ in the boost block, which do not reach the residue.
dark-energy.frozen-point-datum-kasner-wa.technical:
Take the derived metric of a synchronous diagonal gravitational field on flat spacetime, a Bianchi I Einstein-$\Lambda$ metric with Kasner residue $(p_1,p_2,p_3)$ at $\tau = 0$, $p_1p_2p_3\neq 0$, and the frozen-point datum $I = (1,0,\Lambda/6)$, $X = (0,0,1)$ with its tractor connection. In the orthonormal frame $I$, $X$, the soldering form and the Schouten summand are regular; the only singular part is the Levi-Civita block, the rotation-gauge field, whose leading term on the physical frame is the simple pole $\Omega(\hb(e_i)) = -(p_i/\tau)\,B_i$, $\Omega(\hb(e_0)) = 0$, with residue $a \mapsto -\sum_i p_i\,(a\cdot e^i)\,B_i$ tangential to the wall. Its curvature is a double pole, and the Kretschmann scalar is $-16p_1p_2p_3\tau^{-4}$ at leading order, so the datum extends regularly across the wall in no chart.

At leading order the Ricci map is $\tau^2\mathcal{R}(e_0) = (\sum_ip_i^2 - \sum_ip_i)\,e_0$ and $\tau^2\mathcal{R}(e_i) = p_i(\sum_jp_j - 1)\,e_i$, so the vacuum equations at the wall are exactly the Kasner relations $\sum_ip_i = 1 = \sum_ip_i^2$, the second saying that the residue bivector is a unit boost; $\Lambda$ enters only at relative order $\Lambda\tau^2$. Of the three densities of the curvature-squared action, which exists for $\Lambda \neq 0$, only the topological Gauss-Bonnet term diverges, as $-16p_1p_2p_3\tau^{-3}$, so the action's value is undefined at the wall while its field equations reach it as conditions on the residue. The application to the Schwarzschild interiors goes through the weighted limit.
dark-energy.frozen-point-datum-kasner-wa.lay: Approaching a Kasner-type singularity at which none of the three Kasner exponents vanishes, and working at leading order near the wall, the structure built from the frozen point stays well behaved except for one piece, the part of the connection that describes how the frame turns, which blows up in a simple way that no change of frame removes. The coefficients of that blow-up are the Kasner exponents, and Einstein's equations at the wall become exactly the classic Kasner conditions on them. When the cosmological constant is nonzero, so that the curvature-squared form of the action exists, that action takes an infinite value at the wall, but only through a term that does not affect the equations, so the equations still make sense there.

dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-we.technical:
On the Einstein region with $\Lambda\neq 0$ of a gravitational field on flat spacetime, parallelism of the frozen point $I$ for the tractor gauge field, with $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$, reduces the ambient $SO(2,4)$-structure to $SO(1,4)$ for $\Lambda > 0$ or $SO(2,3)$ for $\Lambda < 0$, and the tractor connection to a metric connection on $I^\perp$. The vector $V = X - (3/\Lambda)I$, made from the frozen point and the canonical tractor, has $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$, stabiliser the Lorentz group of $\{I,V\}^\perp$ and covariant derivative the soldering form, and the pair (reduced connection, $V$) is exactly the MacDowell-Mansouri datum. The action is $S[\nabla,I,V] \sim Q(I)^{-1}\int\epsilon(I,V,F,F)$, with $I$ and $V$ constrained fields.

This functional is polynomial in the connection, $I$ and $V$, with no inverse metric. Its prefactor $3/\Lambda$ has a simple pole at $\Lambda = 0$; by the imported expansion $S \sim (3/\Lambda)\int\epsilon_{abcd}R^{ab}\wedge R^{cd} + 2\int\epsilon_{abcd}e^a\wedge e^b\wedge R^{cd} + (\Lambda/3)\int\epsilon_{abcd}e^a\wedge e^b\wedge e^c\wedge e^d$, the first term is topological, and after its subtraction the limit $\Lambda\to 0$ is the Einstein-Cartan functional, defined at degenerate $e$.
dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-we.lay: The frozen point is a fixed direction in the larger conformal space whose length encodes the cosmological constant. On the region where Einstein's equations hold with a nonzero cosmological constant, this result shows that the frozen point, together with one canonical geometric object, produces exactly the extra vector that a known reformulation of gravity, due to MacDowell and Mansouri and to Stelle and West, requires. Gravity's action can then be written as the square of the curvature as seen from the point at infinity, with no inverse metric anywhere, so it is defined wherever the connection stays regular. At the black hole's wall, where the connection is singular, its value diverges but its field equations still reach the wall; and the curvature-squared form itself exists only while the cosmological constant is nonzero.
dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-we.typing_note: Kept all four premises; the Kasner-wall proposition cited in consequence (1) was not added, because it uses this theorem and is cited only to illustrate the wall, so adding it would make a cycle. Levels pass: the lay level now states the Einstein region with nonzero cosmological constant, and no longer says the action makes sense where the metric degenerates (at the wall only the field equations reach, not the value).

dark-energy.gravity-pre-metric-forces-de.technical:
The MacDowell-Mansouri mechanism does not extend to an internal gauge factor along either route. The frozen point is an internal singlet and an internal field strength carries no tractor index, so no invariant $\epsilon(I,\cdot,F_i,F_i)$ exists; and the star-free quadratic invariants $\int\tr(F_i\wedge F_i)$ are topological, a boundary term with no field equations. Whether a polynomial functional of some other shape could serve is not decided. What exists instead are the Yang-Mills functionals $(1/2g_i^2)\int\tr(F_i\wedge *F_i)$, and the Hodge star on two-forms in four dimensions depends on the conformal class $[g]$ alone.

So the internal forces are conformal-level objects, defined where the conformal class is nondegenerate, while gravity's action is pre-metric: polynomial in the connection, the frozen point and the Stelle-West vector. At a tame corank-one wall the cometric acquires a radical and the metric a pole, the star on two-forms is no longer a nondegenerate map, and the internal actions degenerate; what crosses is gravity together with the topological $\theta$-terms.
dark-energy.gravity-pre-metric-forces-de.lay: Gravity's action can be written without ever inverting the metric, but the standard actions of the other forces cannot: they need the Hodge star, which depends on the metric's angles though not its overall scale. The two natural ways of writing the other forces in gravity's style either give nothing or give only a term without dynamics; whether some other kind of action could work is left open. So at a mild (tame) singular wall, where the metric loses one direction and degenerates, the ordinary forces break down with it, while gravity and the topological part of each force carry on across.
dark-energy.gravity-pre-metric-forces-de.typing_note: Added the action theorem, which clause (2) cites for gravity's action being pre-metric; the refutation-record citation is context only. Levels pass: the lay level now restricts the wall to a tame corank-one wall, speaks of the standard actions of the other forces, and keeps the formal's open question about actions of a different shape.

proofs.main:
The proof is in Gauge Theory Gravity, with forms read as multivector fields on flat spacetime: a $k$-form is a field of background $k$-vectors, $\alpha = \tfrac{1}{k!}\alpha_{\mu\ldots}\,e^{\mu}\wedge\cdots$, the exterior derivative is $\nabla\wedge$, and the wedge of forms is the outer product of their background parts. An internal gauge field is a one-form $\mathcal{A} = e^{\mu}A_{\mu}$ whose values $A_{\mu}$ lie in the internal Lie algebra, realised as bivectors of an internal Clifford algebra (a compact Lie algebra is a Lie subalgebra of the bivectors of some $\Cl(n,0)$, acting on its own vectors), multiplied by the internal geometric product, which commutes with the background factor; the trace form is the scalar part $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{int}}$ of that product, cyclic, and proportional to the Killing form on each simple factor. The field strength is $\mathcal{F} = \nabla\wedge\mathcal{A} + \mathcal{A}\wedge\mathcal{A}$, a background bivector with values in the Lie algebra.

(1) Internal invariance of $I$ is structural: $I$ is a vector of the tractor factor $\Cl(2,4)$, the internal groups act on the internal factor, and $\mathcal{F}$ is a background bivector with internal Lie-algebra values, with no tractor slot for $\epsilon$ or $I$ to contract. Topologicality: the Bianchi identity $D\wedge\mathcal{F} := \nabla\wedge\mathcal{F} + \mathcal{A}\wedge\mathcal{F} - \mathcal{F}\wedge\mathcal{A} = 0$ holds identically ($\nabla\wedge\nabla = 0$ and associativity), so $\nabla\wedge\langle\mathcal{F}\wedge\mathcal{F}\rangle_{\mathrm{int}} = 2\langle D\wedge\mathcal{F}\wedge\mathcal{F}\rangle_{\mathrm{int}} = 0$, using that background bivectors commute under the outer product and the scalar part is cyclic; on a contractible region $\langle\mathcal{F}\wedge\mathcal{F}\rangle_{\mathrm{int}} = \nabla\wedge\mathcal{C}$ with the Chern-Simons trivector $\mathcal{C} = \langle\mathcal{A}\wedge\nabla\wedge\mathcal{A} + \tfrac23\,\mathcal{A}\wedge\mathcal{A}\wedge\mathcal{A}\rangle_{\mathrm{int}}$; and the variation is $\delta\int\langle\mathcal{F}\wedge\mathcal{F}\rangle_{\mathrm{int}} = 2\int\langle D\wedge\delta\mathcal{A}\wedge\mathcal{F}\rangle_{\mathrm{int}} = 2\int\nabla\wedge\langle\delta\mathcal{A}\wedge\mathcal{F}\rangle_{\mathrm{int}} + 2\int\langle\delta\mathcal{A}\wedge D\wedge\mathcal{F}\rangle_{\mathrm{int}}$, a boundary term plus zero: no field equations. The background metric is never used.

(2) Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a gravitational field with derived metric $g(a,b) = \hb^{-1}(a)\cdot\hb^{-1}(b)$. The physical field strength of a two-form $\mathcal{F}$ is $\hb^{T}(\mathcal{F})$ (on physical vectors $A = \hb^{-1}(a)$, $B = \hb^{-1}(b)$: $(a\wedge b)\cdot\mathcal{F} = (A\wedge B)\cdot\hb^{T}(\mathcal{F})$), and the Hodge dual of a physical bivector is multiplication by the pseudoscalar $I$. Read back on the background with $\hb^{-T}(X) = I\,\hb(I^{-1}X)/\det\hb$, and normalised to the background orientation as the component formula is,
\[
{*}_{g}\mathcal{F} \;=\; \frac{1}{|\det\hb|}\; I\,\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{F}), \qquad \mathcal{G} = \hb\,\hb^{T},
\]
where $\mathcal{G}$ is the cometric map ($g^{\mu\nu} = e^{\mu}\cdot\mathcal{G}(e^{\nu})$), acting on bivectors as an outermorphism, and $|\det\hb|^{-1} = \sqrt{|g|}$. A change of scale $g \mapsto \lambda^{-2}g$ is $\hb \mapsto \lambda\hb$: $|\det\hb|^{-1}$ gains $\lambda^{-4}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ on bivectors gains $\lambda^{4}$, so ${*}_{g}$ is unchanged. A rotation-gauge change $\hb(a) \mapsto \hb(\tilde R aR)$ leaves $\mathcal{G}$ and $\det\hb$ unchanged. Since $\mathcal{G}$ determines $g$ ($g(a, b) = a\cdot\mathcal{G}^{-1}(b)$), ${*}_{g}$ depends on $[g]$ only, and not on the scale that the frozen point fixes; it does depend on $[g]$ (the check exhibits two non-conformal fields with different stars), and ${*}_{g}^{2} = -1$, from $\mathcal{G}(I\,\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{F})) = \det(\mathcal{G})\,I\,\mathcal{F}$ and $\det\mathcal{G} = (\det\hb)^{2}$. Gravity's action, by contrast, contains no inverse frame (\claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(1)).

(3) is (2) read at a corank-one wall. There the cometric acquires a one-dimensional radical and the metric a pole (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-walls-sphere-theorem}): along a family approaching the wall, $\mathcal{G}_{s} \to \mathcal{G}_{0}$ of rank three and $\det\hb_{s} \to 0$, $\sqrt{|g|} = |\det\hb_{s}|^{-1}$ diverging. If ${*}_{g}$ had a finite limit $S$, then $I\,\mathcal{G}_{s} = |\det\hb_{s}|\,{*}_{g}$ would tend to $0\cdot S = 0$; but it tends to $I\,\mathcal{G}_{0} \neq 0$. So ${*}_{g}$ has no limit, and its bounded rescaling $|\det\hb_{s}|\,{*}_{g} \to I\,\mathcal{G}_{0}$ has rank three on the six-dimensional bivectors (the bivectors of the three-dimensional image of $\mathcal{G}_{0}$): ${*}$ on two-forms is not a nondegenerate map there, for every representative of the conformal class alike, since the scale cancels. The $\theta$-terms $\theta\int\langle\mathcal{F}\wedge\mathcal{F}\rangle_{\mathrm{int}}$ use no $\hb$, hence cross.

The check confirms in exact arithmetic the Bianchi identity and $\langle\mathcal{F}\wedge\mathcal{F}\rangle_{\mathrm{int}} = \nabla\wedge\mathcal{C}$ for polynomial $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued fields (bivectors of $\Cl(3,0)$, one abelian and one nonabelian sample), the formula for ${*}_{g}$ against the component star, its scale and rotation-gauge invariance and ${*}_{g}^{2} = -1$, and the divergence and rank three at a wall.

\emph{In components} (a reading): ${*}\alpha_{ab} = \tfrac12\sqrt{|g|}\,\epsilon_{abcd}\,g^{ce}g^{df}\alpha_{ef}$, $\sqrt{|g|}$ scaling by $\lambda^{-4}$ and the two inverse metrics by $\lambda^{4}$ under $g \mapsto \lambda^{-2}g$; at the wall $g^{ce}$ has a one-dimensional radical and $\sqrt{|g|}$ a half-power pole; and $d\,\tr(F\wedge F) = 2\tr(DF\wedge F) = 0$, $\tr(F\wedge F) = d\,\mathrm{CS}(A)$, with the internal algebra as matrices and the trace for $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{int}}$ (the earlier checks compute these for $\mathfrak{gl}(2)$).

dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geomet.technical:
On the invertible region of a gravitational field on flat spacetime the vacuum equations are exactly the covariant constancy of the null scale tractor. For the Einstein condition with $\Lambda
eq 0$ the parallel tractor $I$ has $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ and stabiliser the reductive de Sitter group $SO(1,4)$ for $\Lambda > 0$, anti-de Sitter for $\Lambda < 0$, the parabolic-to-reductive rotation of the stabiliser being proved with the sign fixed internally. The stabiliser of a non-null fibre vector has dimension ten, and its orthogonal complement carries a form of signature $(1,4)$ or $(2,3)$.

The tractor connection reads in the scale $g$ as $
abla_a(\sigma,\mu_b,ho) = (
abla_a\sigma - \mu_a,\ 
abla_a\mu_b + g_{ab}ho - P_{ab}\sigma,\ 
abla_aho + P_a{}^b\mu_b)$, with Schouten tensor $P_{ab} = (\Lambda/6)g_{ab}$ on the Einstein region, and it preserves the tractor metric. The fact restates results of the geometry paper, with Gover's tractor technology as the external input. A remark, not part of the fact: on flat spacetime this connection is the $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field $\Omega_{T}$ of the tractor gauge-field theorem, which itself rests on this fact.
dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geomet.lay: This fact collects earlier results about the frozen point, a fixed direction in the six-dimensional conformal model attached to flat spacetime. Einstein's vacuum equations amount to this direction staying constant as the gravitational gauge fields carry it from place to place, and its length is set by the cosmological constant. The symmetries that leave it alone form the de Sitter group, or the anti-de Sitter group when the cosmological constant is negative. The fact also writes down the rule, the tractor connection, that says what constant means here.

dark-energy.imported-henneaux-teitelboim.formal:
In the unimodular formulation of general relativity the cosmological constant is not a parameter of the action but the value of a Lagrange-multiplier field, conjugate to a cosmic-time variable, whose constancy $d\Lambda = 0$ is an equation of motion; $\Lambda$ is then a constant of integration, a label of the solution rather than of the theory, and the formulation is generally covariant. \emph{Provenance:} \cite{HenneauxTeitelboim1989}; the transcription to the Stelle-West norm, promoting the value $\Lambda/3$ of the constraint $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ to that field, is Remark \claimref{note.dark-energy.what-clause-3-requires-what-it}'s; the series keeps $\Lambda$ fixed by the frozen point (the registered input) and records this promotion as the variational form of the Clausius route.

\emph{Note (a local release is not this promotion).} The promotion is global: $\Lambda$ is constant by its own equation of motion, with a conjugate three-form (a cosmic time) carrying the variational freedom. Releasing the norm of the Stelle-West vector locally instead, with no three-form, so that its value varies pointwise, gives for the frozen-point functional the pointwise equation $\epsilon(I, V, F, F) = 0$, which fails at every point of the Schwarzschild-de Sitter field with nonzero mass, and in the constant-coupling family with the MacDowell-Mansouri term a solution of constant norm needs the Weyl square constant, which that field also violates; such a release excludes Schwarzschild-de Sitter (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.stelle-west-norm-is-no-local-output}(iv)).
dark-energy.imported-henneaux-teitelboim.technical: In the unimodular formulation of general relativity the cosmological constant is not a parameter of the action but the value of a Lagrange-multiplier field, conjugate to a cosmic-time variable, whose constancy $d\Lambda = 0$ is an equation of motion. $\Lambda$ is then a constant of integration, a label of the solution rather than of the theory, and the formulation is generally covariant. Transcribing this to the Stelle-West norm, by promoting the value $\Lambda/3$ of the constraint $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ to such a field, is the series' own step, not the source's: the series keeps $\Lambda$ fixed by the frozen point, the registered input, and records the promotion as the variational form of the Clausius route. Released locally instead, without the three-form, the norm obeys a pointwise equation that every Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole violates, so a local release excludes those fields.
dark-energy.imported-henneaux-teitelboim.lay: In a well-known reformulation of general relativity, the cosmological constant stops being a fixed setting of the theory and becomes a quantity that the equations hold constant, much like a conserved charge. Different solutions can then carry different values. The series makes the same move for the frozen point's length, keeping the cosmological constant fixed by it, and reads the move as the variational form of its thermodynamic route to Einstein's equations.

imported_from.citation: M. Henneaux and C. Teitelboim, The cosmological constant and general covariance, Phys. Lett. B 222 (1989), 195--199.

dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-.technical:
In Gauge Theory Gravity, adjoin to the vectors of $\Cl(1,3)$ one vector $V$ with $Q(V) = -\ell^2$, $\ell^2 = 3/\Lambda$ (negative on the anti-de Sitter branch), giving the vectors of $\Cl(1,4)$, the fibre of the de Sitter group. A de Sitter connection is then a gauge field $A(a)$ on flat spacetime valued in the bivectors of $\Cl(1,4)$; in the gauge where $V$ is constant it is $A(a) = \Omega(a) - \hb^{-1}(a)\wedge V/\ell^2$, the rotation-gauge field plus a soldering term built from the physical frame. Its field strength has a Lorentz block $\mathcal{F}(B) = -(\mathcal{R}(B) - \ell^{-2}B)$ (in forms exactly $F^{ab} = R^{ab} + \ell^{-2}e^a\wedge e^b$), which vanishes exactly on de Sitter space, and a translational block proportional to the torsion. The functional $S_{\mathrm{MM}} \sim \ell^2\int\epsilon_{abcd}F^{ab}\wedge F^{cd}$ decomposes into the Gauss-Bonnet, Einstein-Cartan and cosmological terms.

Its Euler-Lagrange equations are the Einstein-Cartan equations, equivalent on the invertible region to vanishing torsion together with the field equations $\mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a = 0$. The anti-de Sitter branch reads identically with $SO(2,3)$, and the reduction uses the sign-independent identity $Q(I)\,Q(V) = -1$. The variational identity is used at assembly level.
dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-.lay: MacDowell and Mansouri, and later Stelle and West, showed that gravity with a cosmological constant can be written as a theory of a larger symmetry group, the de Sitter group, broken by a vector of fixed length. On flat spacetime this means adding one extra direction to the algebra in which the gravitational fields take their values. The action is then the square of a field strength, and it splits into a topological piece, the usual Einstein term and the cosmological term. Its equations are the Einstein equations with that cosmological constant.

dark-energy.lift-inherits-no-go-steps-it.formal:
The remaining open item, that the four-dimensional lift might introduce a coupling invisible to the s-wave sector, is addressed by covering the spacetime in two pieces, with one step upgraded. The steps, each with its provenance:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Partial waves (exact, kinematic).} Near the horizon the four-dimensional two-point function between the graviton mode and any probe decomposes over partial waves, and the angular integration is diagonal in $\ell$ by spherical-harmonic orthogonality.
\item \emph{Near-horizon reduction (assembly, at the level it carries in T5).} Each fixed-$\ell$ sector reduces, at the horizon where the potential barrier vanishes, to a two-dimensional copy of the setting of the current algebra, in which the $\ell$-th component of the graviton mode is the $\ell$-th $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-harmonic of the current bilinears. Which operator is the stress tensor in the $\ell$-th copy is fixed by step (4), not assumed.
\item \emph{Exterior exactness (imported theorem).} On any region where the gauge-theoretic metric is invertible, the horizon included, the description coincides exactly with classical general relativity, by the geometry paper's import of gauge-theory gravity from Lasenby, Doran and Gull \cite[Fact~2.1]{ButlerT6}, whose couplings to the metric are stress-energy alone. The two pieces overlap and cover the spacetime.
\item \emph{The sphere step (conditional on the entropy paper's Indifference premise; then proved by covariance).} By the sphere theorem (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-walls-sphere-theorem}, \cite[Thm.~5.5]{ButlerT8}, conditional on \cite[Principle~5.4]{ButlerT8}) every angular operator of the lift is a boundary-mode bilinear of definite spin under the adjoint $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, of spin $\ell \geq 1$ for every non-trivial harmonic, while the s-wave stress tensor $T$ is an $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ singlet. In an $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-invariant state the symmetry orthogonality of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip} applies verbatim: nonzero spin, zero overlap. Orthogonality by dimension would \emph{not} do here, the bilinears having dimension two like $T$; it is the spin that separates them. The lift inherits the no-go because the sphere is built from the same correlations to which the no-go applies, and those correlations carry spin.
\end{enumerate}
With Propositions \claimref{dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip} and \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation} and these steps, the acoustic programme is closed at the mixed level of its inputs: the metric-forming correlations admit exactly one coupling sector, its weakness is dimensional, its leading nonlinearity is Gertsenshtein's, and its Goldstones are eaten. Step (2), the near-horizon reduction, is at assembly level, its promotion shared with T5 and T7; step (4) is conditional on the entropy paper's Indifference premise, and the closure of the acoustic programme inherits that condition.

dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physic.formal:
Take the functional in its three-argument form, $S[
abla, I, V] \sim Q(I)^{-1}\int\epsilon(I, V, F, F)$, with $
abla$ the tractor connection, on flat spacetime the $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field $\Omega_{T}$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection} (its curvature $F$ the field strength of $\Omega_{T}$), and $I$ and $V$ independent sections subject to the Stelle-West constraints $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$, $\ip{V}{I} = 0$, $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$; Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.stelle-west-vector-frozen-point} exhibits $V = X - (3/\Lambda)I$ as the canonical solution of the constraints on the Einstein region, but inside the variational principle $V$ is a field, since the canonical tractor $X$ is a fixed section and a transformation acting on $
abla$ and $I$ alone is not a symmetry of a functional that contains $X$. Then: the constrained fluctuation space of $(I, V)$ has dimension $9$ (twelve components less three independent linearised constraints; it fibres over the five tangential directions of $I$ with four-dimensional affine fibres of $\delta V$, and is not a direct sum); the stabiliser of the pair $(I, V)$ in $SO(2,4)$ is the Lorentz group of $\{I,V\}^\perp$, of dimension six, so the broken generators number $15 - 6 = 9$; and the infinitesimal action $\xi \mapsto (\xi\cdot I, \xi\cdot V)$ of the broken generators onto the constrained fluctuation space is bijective. Unitary gauge $\delta I = \delta V = 0$ therefore exists and is complete: every fluctuation of the pair is a gauge transformation, the eaten Goldstone modes reappearing as the frame freedom of the soldering form (the physical frame $\hb^{-1}(a)$ of the gravitational field, up to rotation gauge), the Stelle-West mechanism read in reverse. In unitary gauge the second variation of the action has legs only on the connection: the graviton carries no $(\delta I, \delta V)$ polarisation. This closes open item (ii) of Remark \claimref{note.dark-energy.weakness-dimension-nonlinear-bound-open-items} within the action's own variational principle; the four-dimensional lift of the s-wave no-go is the task of Assembly \claimref{dark-energy.lift-inherits-no-go-steps-itemised}, not of this proposition. \emph{Level:} the counting, the bijectivity, and the invariance of the integrand $\epsilon(I,V,F,F)$ under the ambient group acting on all three arguments are proved outright below; that the functional so gauge-fixed is the MacDowell-Mansouri functional is Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(ii)-(iii), with its assembly-level clause.
dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physic.technical:
In the three-argument functional $S[\nabla,I,V] \sim Q(I)^{-1}\int\epsilon(I,V,F,F)$, with $\nabla$ the tractor connection, on flat spacetime the $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field built from gravity's fields, with $I$ and $V$ independent fields subject to $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$, $\langle V,I\rangle = 0$ and $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$, the constrained fluctuation space of $(I,V)$ has dimension $12 - 3 = 9$. The stabiliser of the pair in $SO(2,4)$ is the Lorentz group of $\{I,V\}^\perp$, of dimension six, so there are $15 - 6 = 9$ broken generators, and $\xi\mapsto(\xi\cdot I, \xi\cdot V)$ maps them bijectively onto the constrained fluctuations.

Hence unitary gauge $\delta I = \delta V = 0$ exists and is complete: every fluctuation of the pair is a gauge transformation, the Goldstone modes reappearing as the frame freedom of the soldering form, and the second variation has legs only on the connection. The counting, the bijectivity and the invariance of the integrand are proved outright; that the gauge-fixed functional is the MacDowell-Mansouri one carries the assembly-level clause of that identification.
dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physic.lay: Gravity's action here, written for gauge fields on flat spacetime, contains two fixed-length vectors tied to the point at infinity. One might worry that their wobbles are extra physical fields to which matter could couple. This result counts the possible wobbles and the broken symmetries, finds nine of each, and shows they match one to one, so every wobble can be undone by a symmetry. The graviton therefore carries no extra polarisation from this sector. This holds within the action's own variational principle, with both vectors treated as fields held to their fixed lengths; that the action so fixed is the known MacDowell-Mansouri one rests on the earlier theorem's assembly-level step.

proofs.main:
Read in Gauge Theory Gravity: the metric $g$ below is the derived metric of the gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime, the manifold is the invertible region, and the tractor connection is the flat-space $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}; the index computation below is its reading in the splitting of $g$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}).

Constraints: $\delta Q(I) = 2\ip{\delta I}{I} = 0$, $\delta\ip{V}{I} = \ip{\delta V}{I} + \ip{V}{\delta I} = 0$, $\delta Q(V) = 2\ip{\delta V}{V} = 0$: three independent linear conditions on the twelve components of $(\delta I, \delta V)$ (independent because $I$ and $V$ are non-null and orthogonal), leaving nine. Stabiliser: a bivector annihilating both $I$ and $V$ is a bivector of $\{I,V\}^\perp$, which has signature $(1,3)$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(ii)), so the stabiliser algebra is $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$, of dimension six, and the broken complement has dimension nine. The map $\xi \mapsto (\xi\cdot I, \xi\cdot V)$ maps into the constrained space, since $\ip{\xi\cdot I}{I} = 0$, $\ip{\xi\cdot V}{V} = 0$ and $\ip{\xi\cdot V}{I} + \ip{V}{\xi\cdot I} = 0$ by antisymmetry of $\xi$; restricted to the broken complement it is injective, because a $\xi$ in the complement with $\xi\cdot I = \xi\cdot V = 0$ lies in the stabiliser; by equal dimensions it is bijective. Any constrained $(\delta I, \delta V)$ is thus $(\xi\cdot I, \xi\cdot V)$ for a unique broken $\xi$, and the gauge transformation by $-\xi$, acting simultaneously on $
abla$, $I$ and $V$, removes it while shifting $\delta
abla$: the Goldstone eating. In the resulting gauge the second variation is a quadratic form in $\delta
abla$ alone. Invariance of the functional: a gauge transformation is a section $g$ of the ambient group bundle, acting on the fibre by $g(x) \in SO(2,4)$ at each point; it acts on the connection by $
abla \mapsto g
abla g^{-1}$, so that the curvature, $F = 
abla^2$, transforms by $F \mapsto gFg^{-1}$, that is, its bivector value at each point is carried by $g(x)$ (a bivector $a\wedge b$ goes to $ga\wedge gb$, since $g$ is an isometry), and on $I$ and $V$ by $I \mapsto gI$, $V \mapsto gV$. The volume form of a six-dimensional fibre with a nondegenerate form is invariant under its special orthogonal group, so at each point $\epsilon(gI, gV, gF, gF) = \det(g)\,\epsilon(I, V, F, F) = \epsilon(I, V, F, F)$; the prefactor $1/Q(I)$ and the three constraints $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$, $\ip{V}{I} = 0$, $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$ are preserved because $g(x)$ is an isometry of the fibre; and a pointwise identity between integrands is an identity between the integrals. The functional is therefore invariant, and the constraint surface is carried to itself, under the ambient gauge group acting on all three arguments. The script confirms the fibrewise identity on rational elements of $SO(2,4)$ (a boost, a rotation, and their product, each confirmed an isometry). That the one-argument version fails is worth recording, since it is the error to avoid: with $\xi = I\wedge V$ one has $\xi\cdot I = -(\Lambda/3)V$, a tangential fluctuation of $I$, but $\xi\cdot X = -(3/\Lambda)I - V$, so that $\epsilon(I, \xi\cdot X, F, F) = -\epsilon(I, V, F, F)$: acting on $
abla$ and $I$ while holding $X$ fixed changes the integrand by minus itself, not by zero. The script performs the counting exactly in the flat model over $\mathbb{Q}$ at $\Lambda = 3$: the joint action matrix of the fifteen basis bivectors on $(I, V)$ has rank exactly nine, so the stabiliser has dimension six; the image of the bivector algebra on $I$ alone has rank five and equals $I^\perp$; and the one-argument failure is confirmed on the displayed $\xi$.

dark-energy.stelle-west-vector-frozen-po.formal:
Let a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) be Einstein with $\Lambda \neq 0$ on its invertible region, and work in the scale $g$ of its derived metric determined by the frozen point, so that $I = (1, 0, \Lambda/6) = \nInf + \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\nO$ and $\nabla I = 0$ (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry}). Let $X := (0, 0, 1) = \nO$ be the canonical tractor, and define
\[
V \;:=\; X - \frac{\ip{X}{I}}{Q(I)}\, I \;=\; X - \frac{3}{\Lambda}\, I \;=\; \Bigl(-\frac{3}{\Lambda},\; 0,\; \frac12\Bigr),
\qquad
W \;:=\; \frac{V}{Q(V)} \;=\; \Bigl(1,\; 0,\; -\frac{\Lambda}{6}\Bigr) \;=\; \nInf - \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\nO .
\]
Write $e_a$ for the tractor $(0, g_{ab}, 0)$, the unit vector of the $\mu_a$ slot: on flat spacetime the physical frame vector $\hb^{-1}(a)$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $Q(X) = 0$, $\ip{X}{I} = 1$, $\ip{V}{I} = 0$, and $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda = -\ell^2$.
\item[(ii)] $\nabla_a X = e_a$, the soldering form, and $\nabla_a V = e_a$ as well; $\ip{e_a}{I} = 0$.
\item[(iii)] On a tractor with no $\mu$-component the connection \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry} acts as $\nabla_a = \partial_a + e_a\wedge W$; on a general tractor it is the Levi-Civita connection on the $\mu$-slot plus the same bivector: $\nabla_a = D_a + e_a\wedge V/Q(V)$. On flat spacetime this is the $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field $\Omega_{T}(a) = \Omega(a) + \hb^{-1}(a) \wedge W$: the rotation-gauge field plus the soldering bivector built from the physical frame, with Schouten map $\tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\,\mathrm{id}$.
\item[(iv)] $[\,e_a\wedge W,\; e_b\wedge W\,] = -Q(W)\; e_a\wedge e_b = (\Lambda/3)\, e_a\wedge e_b$.
\end{enumerate}

dark-energy.stelle-west-vector-frozen-po.lay: Starting from the frozen point and one canonical fixed direction of the six-dimensional conformal model, this lemma builds a vector perpendicular to the frozen point whose length is set by the cosmological constant. dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-pa.technical:
In the three-argument functional, $\Lambda$ enters as the value of the Stelle-West constraints $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$, $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$, a number fixed before variation, so it is the index $\mu$ of the four-way classification. With $\Lambda$ fixed, the pure-gauge count leaves no fluctuation of the norm, and $N = M_P\sqrt{3/\Lambda}$ is constant on each solution space $\mathcal{S}_\Lambda$. It varies across the family, $d(N^2)/d\Lambda = -3M_P^2/\Lambda^2\neq 0$, so it is not dynamically fixed, and by the rescaling argument it is not kinematic; by exhaustiveness it is a parameter of the laws and not initial data, for the action as written.

If $\Lambda$ is allowed to vary, the constrained space of $(\delta I,\delta V,\delta\Lambda)$ has dimension ten against a nine-dimensional gauge orbit, leaving one non-gauge norm mode, $(\delta I,\delta V,\delta\Lambda) \propto (I/2\Lambda, -V/2\Lambda, 1)$, the tangent of the rescaling family $(sI, V/s, s^2\Lambda)$; it needs an equation of motion that the action does not supply.

Under the action exactly as written, this length cannot fluctuate within any one solution, yet it differs between theories with different cosmological constants. dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-c.formal:
Three clauses, at three levels. Gravity is a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime with derived metric $g$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}); the tractor connection is its $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Proved.)} On the Einstein region the frozen point is parallel (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry}) and the tractor connection preserves the fibre metric, so $\partial_aQ(I) = 2\ip{\nabla_a I}{I} = 0$: the norm $\Lambda/3$ cannot vary in space or time. A constant $\Lambda$ enters the Einstein equations as the stress-energy $T^{\Lambda}_{ab} = (\Lambda/8\pi G)\,g_{ab}$, that is $T^{\Lambda}(a) = (\Lambda/8\pi G)\,a$ (in the store's convention, where de Sitter space has $\Ric = \Lambda g$ in signature $(+,-,-,-)$, field strength $\mathcal{R}(a) = \Lambda a$, and the Einstein equation reads $\Ric + 8\pi G\,T = (\Lambda + 4\pi G\,g^{ab}T_{ab})\,g$), with energy density $\rho = \Lambda/8\pi G > 0$ for $\Lambda > 0$ and pressure $p = -\rho$ identically: $w = -1$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Proved.)} Off the Einstein region write $I_g$ again for the scale tractor of a general field's derived metric $g$ in its own scale, $I_g = (1, 0, J/4) = \nInf + \tfrac{J}{4}\nO$ (the object written $I$ above is its Einstein case, $J/4 = \Lambda/6$), with $J = P_a{}^a$ the trace of the Schouten tensor, the slot that makes $I_g$ parallel exactly when $g$ is Einstein (proved below); by $\ip{(\sigma,\mu,\rho)}{(\sigma',\mu',\rho')} \;=\; g(\mu,\mu') + \sigma\rho' + \rho\sigma'$, $Q(I_g) = J/2 = R/12$, which equals $\Lambda/3$ precisely when $R = 4\Lambda$. On a matter-dominated cosmology $R$ is not constant, so the naive extension of the identification to the epochs at which $w$ is measured does not give a constant.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Registered, conditional, under Premise (FS).)} If dark energy is the norm of the frozen point (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}), and if on matter-filled regions the frozen point is kept parallel by the gravitational connection, the $\Cl(2,4)$ connection that preserves $I$, in the physical scale, $\ip{X}{I} = 1$ (successor problem (3) of the section “The engineering conclusion, and scope”; this is Premise \claimref{synthesis.field-space-premise-parallel-frozen-point}, which the store adopts), then $w = -1$ exactly, at every epoch, with no evolution and no quintessence. This is a maximally rigid stance in a field of flexible proposals: most dark-energy models add freedom to $\Lambda$CDM, this one removes it. \emph{The confrontation, recorded as of 2026:} the second data release of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument \cite{DESI2025}, combining baryon-acoustic-oscillation, cosmic-microwave-background and supernova data, reports a preference for an evolving equation of state at roughly three to four standard deviations, with significance depending on the supernova compilation. The preference is contested on three grounds (it concentrates in the derivative of $w$ rather than any mean offset from $-1$; it is prior-sensitive; the driving dataset combinations exhibit internal tensions), so it is not a detection. The framework does not rely on the dispute and states its exposure plainly: a confirmed detection of $w \neq -1$ at any epoch refutes the frozen-point reading of dark energy, with no parameter available to absorb the result. The condition in (iii) is the one way the reading could avoid such a refutation, and the paper names it rather than uses it: a definition of the frozen point off the vacuum region that made the norm track $R/12$ would be refuted already.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Note (the wording of the condition, version 8).} The paper's wording of the condition, that the frozen point admits a definition on a matter-filled region that keeps it parallel, names neither the connection nor the scale. Read literally it is met for every field by the connection that preserves $I$, and without the scale clause by transport-parallel tractors whose own scale is not the physical one and whose norm is unrelated to the $\Lambda$ of the field equations (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.parallel-frozen-point-on-matter-regions-is-the-field-space-premise}(i), (iii)); for the series' transport, the tractor gauge field, it fails wherever matter is (part (ii) there). Worded with the connection and the physical scale, as above, it is Premise (FS): adopting (FS) implies it, and read as fixing which connection carries the frozen point it is (FS) restated (same theorem, Reading). On the reduced field space $\rho$ is constant, so $\Lambda$ is a constant parameter and $w = -1$ is the $\Lambda$CDM equation of state: a confirmed $w = -1$ supports $\Lambda$CDM with a frozen point and is not independent evidence for (FS), while a confirmed $w \neq -1$ would refute (FS), and $\Lambda$CDM with it.
dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-c.technical:
For a gravitational field on flat spacetime, on the Einstein region the frozen point is parallel for the tractor gauge field, which preserves the fibre metric, so $\partial_aQ(I) = 2\langle\nabla_aI, I\rangle = 0$ and the norm $\Lambda/3$ cannot vary in space or time; a constant $\Lambda$ acts as the stress-energy $T^\Lambda(a) = (\Lambda/8\pi G)\,a$ in the store's curvature convention (de Sitter has $\Ric = \Lambda g$), a positive energy density with $p = -\rho$, so $w = -1$. Off the Einstein region the scale tractor $I_g = (1,0,J/4)$ of a general field's derived metric is parallel exactly when $g$ is Einstein, and $Q(I_g) = J/2 = R/12$, which is not constant on a matter-dominated cosmology.

The registration is conditional: if dark energy is the norm of the frozen point, and if on matter-filled regions the frozen point is kept parallel, in the physical scale ($\ip{X}{I} = 1$), by the gravitational connection, the $\Cl(2,4)$ connection that preserves $I$ (the field-space premise (FS), which the store adopts), then $w = -1$ exactly at every epoch. On that field space $\Lambda$ is a constant parameter and $w = -1$ is the $\Lambda$CDM equation of state, so a confirmed $w = -1$ is not independent evidence for (FS). A confirmed detection of $w\neq -1$ at any epoch would refute the frozen-point reading; the evolving-$w$ preference in the 2025 survey data is recorded as contested, not a detection.
dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-c.lay: Where space is empty apart from the cosmological constant, the frozen point's length cannot change as the gravitational gauge fields carry it across flat spacetime, so dark energy behaves exactly like a cosmological constant, with pressure equal to minus its energy density. The paper goes further, on a stated condition: if dark energy is this length, and if the gravitational field is of the kind that keeps the frozen point fixed in regions full of matter, measured in the spacetime's own scale (an assumption the series now adopts; its own transport rule does not do this), then dark energy never evolves. With that assumption the cosmological constant is simply a fixed number, the standard cosmological model's assumption, so finding that dark energy never changes would not be separate evidence for it. That is a rigid, testable stance, and a confirmed measurement of evolving dark energy would refute it.

Read in Gauge Theory Gravity: the metric $g$ below is the derived metric of the gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime, the manifold is the invertible region, and the tractor connection is the flat-space $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}; the index computation below is its reading in the splitting of $g$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}).

(i) is the displayed computation. For its sign: in the store's convention the Einstein equation with source $T$ and no cosmological constant is $\Ric + 8\pi G\,T = 4\pi G\,(g^{ab}T_{ab})\,g$; with the source $T + c\,g$ this becomes $\Ric + 8\pi G\,T = (8\pi G\,c + 4\pi G\,g^{ab}T_{ab})\,g$, which is the equation with cosmological constant $\Lambda$ exactly when $c = \Lambda/8\pi G$ (for $T = 0$ it is $\Ric = \Lambda g$, de Sitter for $\Lambda > 0$). For a unit timelike $u$ ($Q(u) = 1$) the energy density is $T^{\Lambda}(u, u) = \Lambda/8\pi G$, and for a unit spacelike $e$ ($Q(e) = -1$) orthogonal to it the pressure is $T^{\Lambda}(e, e) = -\Lambda/8\pi G$, reading $T = (\rho + p)\,u\otimes u - p\,g$; so $p = -\rho$. (ii): by \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry}, for $I_g = (1, 0, J/4)$ the $\sigma$ slot of $\nabla_a I_g$ is $0 - 0 = 0$, the $\rho$ slot is $\tfrac14\partial_a J + P_a{}^b\cdot 0 = \tfrac14\partial_a J$, and the $\mu$ slot is $0 + (J/4)g_{ab} - P_{ab}$, minus the trace-free Schouten tensor. The $\mu$ slot vanishes if and only if $P_{ab}$ is pure trace, that is if and only if $g$ is Einstein; and an Einstein four-metric has constant scalar curvature by the contracted Bianchi identity, hence constant $J$, so the $\rho$ slot vanishes with it. Thus $\nabla I_g = 0$ exactly when $g$ is Einstein. The norm is $\ip{(\sigma,\mu,\rho)}{(\sigma',\mu',\rho')} \;=\; g(\mu,\mu') + \sigma\rho' + \rho\sigma'$: $Q(I_g) = 2\cdot 1\cdot J/4 = J/2$, and $J = R/6$ in four dimensions. The script confirms the $\mu$ slot on an exact non-Einstein instance and on an Einstein one, and the $\rho$ slot $\tfrac14\partial_a J$ on an instance with non-constant $J$. (iii) is a registration, not a computation; its hypothesis rests on \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}, in which the cosmological constant enters the action as the norm $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ of the frozen point, and its condition is Premise \claimref{synthesis.field-space-premise-parallel-frozen-point}: the varied gravitational connection admits a parallel tractor $I$ with $\ip{X}{I} = 1$. Given it, $D_{a}I = 0$ on every region, matter included, and since the connection is bivector-valued it preserves the fibre metric, so $\partial_{a}Q(I) = 2\ip{D_{a}I}{I} = 0$ as in (i): the norm $\Lambda/3$ is constant at every epoch and the computation of (i) gives $w = -1$.

Wherever this paper calls a datum initial data of the descent ($\epsilon$, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.asymmetry-arrow-counted-fifteenth-refutation}, clause (1) only, as a stance; the orientation bit, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.orientation-arrow-seventeenth-refutation}, which as corrected cites none of these clauses and in particular not clause (3): it reaches clause (I) of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-energy.four-ways-number-enters-theory-shape} directly from CPT covariance, with no exhaustiveness), these clauses are premises of the sentence, and clause (4) names the alternative for each, a parameter of the laws rather than data of the event: for the bit that would require the laws to distinguish the two orientations, for which the CPT covariance of the structures Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.orientation-arrow-seventeenth-refutation} lists leaves no room within them, so the bit is data if it is anything; for $\epsilon$ the paper takes no position.

The dark-matter paper relies on this classification whenever it calls something initial data, and names the alternative each time.

mass.de-sitter-scale-frozen-point.formal:
Let $\eta$ be the fixed product of flat spacetime, the chart of Fact \claimref{mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-infinity}, $Q(x) = \eta(x,x)$, and $\sigma(x) := 1 - \Lambda Q(x)/12$; on the region $\sigma \neq 0$ let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be the gravitational field with $\hb(a) = \sigma\,a$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), whose derived metric is $g = \sigma^{-2}\eta$. Write tractors in the flat scale as the vectors $\sigma\,n_{\infty} + \mu + \rho\,n_{0}$ of $\Cl(2,4)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scale tractor of $\sigma$ in the flat scale is
\[
I_{\sigma} = \bigl(\sigma,\; \nabla\sigma,\; -\tfrac14\Box\sigma\bigr) = \Bigl(1 - \frac{\Lambda Q}{12},\; -\frac{\Lambda}{6}\,x_{a},\; \frac{\Lambda}{6}\Bigr),
\]
it is parallel for the connection \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection} of $\eta$, and $\ip{I_{\sigma}}{I_{\sigma}} = \Lambda/3$ identically. Hence the derived metric $g = \sigma^{-2}\eta$ is Einstein with cosmological constant $\Lambda$, on the region $\sigma \neq 0$: the gravitational field $\hb = \sigma$ is de Sitter space on flat spacetime, and $I_{\sigma}$ is its frozen point.
\item The constant ambient vector whose scale function is $\sigma$ is
\[
I_{\Lambda} := n_{\infty} + \frac{\Lambda}{6}\, n_{0},
\]
and it is the only one: $\ip{X(x)}{n_{\infty} + \lambda n_{0}} = 1 - \lambda Q(x)/2$, which equals $\sigma$ iff $\lambda = \Lambda/6$, and the points $X(x)$ span the ambient space. The vector $n_{0} + \lambda n_{\infty}$, of the same norm, has scale function $\lambda - Q/2$: the inverted chart, not this one.
\item $\ip{I_{\Lambda}}{I_{\Lambda}} = 2 \cdot \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\ip{n_{\infty}}{n_{0}} = \Lambda/3$, in agreement with (1). At $\Lambda = 0$, $I_{\Lambda} = n_{\infty}$: the frozen point of flat space is the point at infinity $n_{\infty}$ of the conformal model (the infinity twistor), and, read through the Klein correspondence as a bivector, it becomes non-simple exactly when $\Lambda \neq 0$.
\end{enumerate}

proofs.main:
Read in Gauge Theory Gravity: the metric below is the derived metric of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), and the manifold is its invertible region.

\emph{(1) The scale tractor.} By Fact \claimref{mass.imported-thomas-operator} at $w = 1$ with $J = 0$ for the flat scale, the scale tractor of $\sigma$ is $\tfrac14 D\sigma = (\sigma, \nabla\sigma, -\tfrac14\Box\sigma)$. With $\nabla_{a}Q = 2x_{a}$ and $\Box Q = 2\eta^{ab}\eta_{ab} = 8$,
\[
\nabla_{a}\sigma = -\tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\,x_{a}, \qquad \Box\sigma = -\tfrac{2\Lambda}{3}, \qquad -\tfrac14\Box\sigma = \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}.
\]
\emph{Parallelism}, slot by slot in \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection} with $P = 0$: the first slot is $\nabla_{a}\sigma - \mu_{a} = 0$ by construction; the second is $\nabla_{a}\mu_{b} + \eta_{ab}\rho = -\tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\eta_{ab} + \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\eta_{ab} = 0$; the third is $\nabla_{a}\rho = 0$ since $\rho$ is constant. \emph{The norm:}
\[
2\sigma\rho + \eta^{ab}\mu_{a}\mu_{b} = 2\Bigl(1 - \frac{\Lambda Q}{12}\Bigr)\frac{\Lambda}{6} + \frac{\Lambda^{2}}{36}Q = \frac{\Lambda}{3}.
\]
\emph{Einstein.} The tractor metric and parallelism are scale-independent, so in the scale $\sigma$ itself, where the density is the constant $1$ and the section therefore reads $(1, 0, \rho')$ by Fact \claimref{mass.imported-thomas-operator} (its middle slot is $n\nabla 1 = 0$), with $2\rho' = \Lambda/3$, Fact \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection} gives that $g = \sigma^{-2}\eta$ is Einstein with $P_{ab} = \rho' g_{ab}$, that is with cosmological constant $6\rho' = \Lambda$.

\emph{(2) The flat-model dictionary.} In the form used here it is elementary. A section $(\sigma, \mu_{b}, \rho)$ is parallel for \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection} with $P = 0$ iff the three slot equations $\nabla_{a}\rho = 0$, $\nabla_{a}\mu_{b} = -\eta_{ab}\rho$, $\nabla_{a}\sigma = \mu_{a}$ hold; integrating them in turn,
\[
\rho = \text{const}, \qquad \mu_{b} = v_{b} - \rho\, x_{b}, \qquad \sigma = \alpha + \ip{v}{x} - \tfrac12\rho\, Q(x),
\]
with $v$ a constant covector and $\alpha$ a constant: a six-parameter family. Since $\ip{X(x)}{\alpha n_{\infty} + \rho n_{0} + v} = \alpha - \tfrac12\rho Q(x) + \ip{v}{x}$ is exactly this $\sigma$-slot, the parallel sections are the constant vectors $V = \alpha n_{\infty} + \rho n_{0} + v$, with scale function $\ip{X(x)}{V}$.

\emph{The scale function of $I_{\Lambda}$.} $\ip{X(x)}{n_{\infty}} = \ip{n_{0}}{n_{\infty}} = 1$ and $\ip{X(x)}{n_{0}} = -\tfrac12 Q\ip{n_{\infty}}{n_{0}} = -\tfrac12 Q$, since $n_{0}, n_{\infty}$ are null and orthogonal to $x$; so
\[
\ip{X(x)}{n_{\infty} + \lambda n_{0}} = 1 - \tfrac12\lambda Q(x), \qquad \ip{X(x)}{n_{0} + \lambda n_{\infty}} = \lambda - \tfrac12 Q(x),
\]
and the first equals $\sigma$ iff $\lambda = \Lambda/6$.

\emph{Uniqueness.} The scale function $x \mapsto \ip{X(x)}{V}$ determines $V$ because the vectors $X(x)$ span the ambient space: the six values at $x = 0$, at the four coordinate unit vectors $e_{a}$ of $\eta$, and at $x = 2e_{0}$ are independent, since $X(0) = n_{0}$, $X(e_{a}) - X(0) = e_{a} - \tfrac12\eta_{aa}n_{\infty}$, and $X(2e_{0}) - 2X(e_{0}) + X(0) = -n_{\infty}$.

\emph{(3) The norm in the chart.} $\ip{n_{\infty} + \lambda n_{0}}{n_{\infty} + \lambda n_{0}} = 2\lambda\ip{n_{\infty}}{n_{0}} = 2\lambda$, using $\ip{n_{\infty}}{n_{\infty}} = \ip{n_{0}}{n_{0}} = 0$; and by Fact \claimref{mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-infinity} a bivector is simple iff its norm vanishes, so $n_{\infty} + \lambda n_{0}$ is simple iff $\lambda = 0$. The general statement behind (3), that the frozen point (the infinity twistor), read as a bivector, is simple iff $\Lambda = 0$, is \cite[Cor.~4.8]{ButlerT9}; here it is the chart computation.

\emph{Script.} It confirms (1) as rational-function identities in $\Lambda$ at rational points (the second slot of the connection, the only one that is not an identity by construction, and the norm $\Lambda/3$), the scale-function values of (2) at rational points and three values of $\lambda$ together with the spanning of the six listed points by exact rank, and the ambient norm of (3) formed and equal to $2\lambda$ at four values (null, hence simple by Fact \claimref{mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-infinity}, exactly at $\lambda = 0$).
