obj.dark-energy.four-ways-number-enters-.technical: The setting is a theory with a kinematic structure $\mathcal{K}$ carrying a notion of isomorphism, and a family of action functionals $S_\mu$, indexed by parameters $\mu$, with solution spaces $\mathcal{S}_\mu$ and an evolution on each. A conserved real quantity $q$ on $\bigcup_\mu\mathcal{S}_\mu$ is kinematic (K) if it factors through the kinematic isomorphism class; dynamically fixed (D) if it is constant on the whole union; a parameter of the laws (P) if it is constant on each $\mathcal{S}_\mu$ but not on the union, so a function of $\mu$ alone; and initial data (I) if it is not constant on some $\mathcal{S}_\mu$.
obj.dark-energy.four-ways-number-enters-.lay: This definition sorts the ways a number can enter a physical theory. It might be fixed by the kinematic setting, forced to a single value by the dynamics, be a setting of the laws that differs between versions of the theory, or vary from one solution to another as initial data. It makes precise the question of what kind of number a constant such as the cosmological constant is.

odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed.technical:
In the tractor bundle of signature $(2,4)$, with frozen point $I$, $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$, and for $\Lambda\neq 0$ the Stelle-West vector $V$, the pair spans a hyperbolic plane: $\langle I,V\rangle = 0$, $Q(I)$ and $Q(V)$ have opposite signs, and the unit directions $e_I$, $e_V$ anticommute with each other and with the Lorentz frame of $\{I,V\}^\perp$. The algebra $\Cl(I^\perp)$ is the space extension $\Cl(1,4)$ for $\Lambda > 0$ and the time extension $\Cl(2,3)$ for $\Lambda < 0$, and adjoining $e_I$ returns the rung, so $\Cl(1,3)\subset\Cl(I^\perp)\subset\Cl(2,4)$, with the sign of $\Lambda$ deciding which signed direction is adjoined first.

At $\Lambda = 0$ the frozen point $I_0$ is null and lies in its own complement, so $I^\perp$ has signature $(1,3;1)$ and $\Cl(I^\perp)\cong\Cl(1,3;1)$, with $I$ the nilpotent generator, $Q(I) = 0$, and $I\,\Cl(1,3;1)$ a sixteen-dimensional ideal of square zero. The Lorentz frame $\{I,V\}^\perp$ has signature $(1,3)$ for every $\Lambda$, zero included.
odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed.lay: When the cosmological constant is not zero, the frozen point and the Stelle-West vector together make up the two extra directions by which the spacetime algebra climbs to the larger conformal algebra. The sign of the cosmological constant decides which of the two, a space-like or a time-like extra direction, comes first. When the cosmological constant is zero the frozen point has zero length and the intermediate algebra becomes degenerate. In every case the ordinary spacetime frame is unchanged.
odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed.typing_note: Kept all three premises, each used in the proof; the E204 comes from the four-extensions corollary, a premise outside this list. Levels pass: lay and one-liner now restrict the hyperbolic-pair clause to nonzero Lambda, where V exists.

proofs.main: Write the rung's hyperbolic plane orthogonal to the Lorentz frame as $\mathrm{span}(e_{+}, e_{-})$ with $e_{+}^{2} = +1$, $e_{-}^{2} = -1$; the frozen point is $I = c\,e_{+} + d\,e_{-}$ with $c^{2} - d^{2} = \Lambda/3$, and the orthogonal vector in the plane is $w = d\,e_{+} + c\,e_{-}$ with $Q(w) = d^{2} - c^{2} = -Q(I)$ and $\ip{I}{w} = cd - cd = 0$. (i) For $\Lambda \neq 0$, $V$ is the section of $I^{\perp}$ of norm $-3/\Lambda$ orthogonal to the Lorentz frame (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point}), so $V$ is a multiple of $w$ and $Q(I)\,Q(V) < 0$ is the identity of Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point-degenerate-algebras}. Orthogonal vectors anticommute in a Clifford algebra. (ii) $I^{\perp} = \{I,V\}^{\perp} \oplus \mathrm{span}(w)$ by dimension, and $e_{V}^{2} = \operatorname{sign}Q(V) = -\operatorname{sign}\Lambda$; so the five generators have signature $(1,3) + (0,1) = (1,4)$ for $\Lambda > 0$ and $(1,3) + (1,0) = (2,3)$ for $\Lambda < 0$, which are the two extensions of Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-oriented-pair}. The five together with $e_{I}$ are an orthogonal basis of the rung's vector space, so they generate $\Cl(2,4)$. (iii) At $c = d$, $Q(I) = 0$ and $w = I$, so $I \in I^{\perp}$, the induced form has the one-dimensional radical $\mathrm{span}(I)$, and the Clifford algebra of the five generators has one null generator: $\Cl(1,3;1)$, with the ideal and its square as in Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point-degenerate-algebras}. (iv) The Lorentz frame is orthogonal to both $e_{+}$ and $e_{-}$ and its signature does not depend on $c, d$. The script verifies (i) to (iv) on exact rational instances with $Q(I) = 3$, $-3$ and $0$: the orthogonality relations, the signatures $(1,4)$, $(2,3)$ and $(1,3;1)$ by exact congruence, the anticommutation, the generation of all sixty-four dimensions when $Q(I) \neq 0$, the nilpotent generator and its ideal in $\Cl(1,3;1)$, and the signature $(1,3)$ of the Lorentz frame in all three cases.

odd-extensions.cosmological-constant-und.formal: The transport, run on the wall, returns the rung and a canonical null frame in its new plane, and stops; the frozen point's position in that plane is data the transport receives, not data it produces, and the one invariant of that position is the norm $\Lambda/3$, sign and magnitude together. Within the series the sign is a choice between two options that the construction makes inequivalent (Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through}(iv)) and that nothing in the construction decides, which is the status the dark-matter paper's Premise P2 gives to the choice of which oriented tower is the visible one; the analogy is one of status, since P2's choice is binary and this one is a real modulus. Nothing here says the sign has no cause: only that the transport is not it.
odd-extensions.cosmological-constant-und.technical:
When the transport is run on the wall at $\Lambda = 0$ it returns the rung $\Cl(2,4)$ and a canonical null frame $\{I, \varphi\}$ in its new hyperbolic plane, and stops. A frozen point of cosmological constant $\Lambda$ is a vector $aI + b\varphi$ of that plane with $Q(aI + b\varphi) = 2ab = \Lambda/3$; its position is data the transport receives, not data it produces, and under the symmetries the transport supplies its one invariant is the norm $\Lambda/3$, sign and magnitude together.

Within the series the sign is a choice between two options that the construction makes inequivalent and that nothing in the construction decides. This is the status the dark-matter paper's Premise P2 gives to the choice of which oriented tower is the visible one, with the difference that that choice is binary and this one is a real modulus. The result does not say the sign has no cause, only that the transport is not it.
odd-extensions.cosmological-constant-und.lay: The series has a procedure, the transport, for dealing with places where its algebra breaks down. Running it at the point where the cosmological constant would be zero produces a definite structure, but it leaves the value of the cosmological constant, including whether it is positive or negative, entirely open. So within the series the cosmological constant is an input rather than an output. This does not mean nothing could fix it, only that the transport does not.

odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point.formal: On the invertible region of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) with $\Lambda \neq 0$, the parallel scale tractor $I$ has squared norm $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ in the tractor metric of signature $(2,4)$, the square of $\Cl(2,4)$; its orthogonal complement $I^{\perp}$ is a rank-five bundle carrying the induced form of signature $(1,4)$ for $\Lambda > 0$ and $(2,3)$ for $\Lambda < 0$, with stabiliser $SO(1,4)$ or $SO(2,3)$; the Stelle-West vector $V$ is a section of $I^{\perp}$ of squared norm $-3/\Lambda$, its stabiliser is the Lorentz group of $\{I, V\}^{\perp}$, of signature $(1,3)$, and its covariant derivative is the soldering form, the physical frame $a \mapsto \hb^{-1}(a)$ of the gravitational field, so that in the gauge where $V$ is constant the reduced connection splits as a Lorentz connection, the rotation-gauge field $\Omega$, plus the translation part $\hb^{-1}(a)\wedge V/Q(V) = -\hb^{-1}(a)\wedge V/\ell^{2}$ ($\ell^{2} = -Q(V) = 3/\Lambda$, negative for $\Lambda < 0$). \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Fact~2.1, Thm.~3.1]{ButlerT10}; the construction is MacDowell and Mansouri's \cite{MacDowellMansouri1977} in Stelle and West's form \cite{StelleWest1980}.
odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point.technical:
On the invertible region of a gravitational field on flat spacetime with $\Lambda \neq 0$ the parallel scale tractor $I$ satisfies $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ in the tractor metric of signature $(2,4)$. Its orthogonal complement $I^{\perp}$ is a rank-five bundle of signature $(1,4)$ when $\Lambda > 0$ and $(2,3)$ when $\Lambda < 0$, with stabiliser $SO(1,4)$ or $SO(2,3)$.

The Stelle-West vector $V$ is a section of $I^{\perp}$ with $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$; its stabiliser is the Lorentz group of $\{I,V\}^{\perp}$, of signature $(1,3)$, and its covariant derivative is the soldering form, the physical frame of the gravitational field. In the gauge where $V$ is constant the reduced connection splits as the rotation-gauge field $\Omega$ plus the translation part $\hb^{-1}(a)\wedge V/Q(V) = -\hb^{-1}(a)\wedge V/\ell^{2}$ ($\ell^{2} = -Q(V) = 3/\Lambda$, negative for $\Lambda < 0$). The construction is MacDowell and Mansouri's in Stelle and West's form, as established in the series' dark-energy paper.
odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point.lay: Where the cosmological constant is nonzero, and on the region where the gravitational field on flat spacetime can be inverted, a third of it is the squared length of a fixed reference vector called the frozen point. Fixing that vector cuts the theory's larger symmetry down to a de Sitter or anti-de Sitter symmetry, depending on the sign. A second vector built alongside it, the Stelle-West vector, cuts it down further to the ordinary Lorentz symmetry and splits the gauge field into a rotation part, gravity's own rotation field, and a translation part, its frame. This is a known construction, imported here from earlier work.

odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point-deg.formal: At $\Lambda = 0$ the parallel scale tractor is null, its stabiliser is parabolic (the Poincar\'e-type stabiliser of a null direction), and the rotation to the reductive de Sitter stabiliser happens exactly when $Q(I) \neq 0$; the identity $Q(I)\,Q(V) = -1$ holds for $\Lambda \neq 0$. A quadratic space with a one-dimensional radical has Clifford algebra $\Cl(p,q;1)$ with a nilpotent generator $n$, $n^{2} = 0$, and $n\,\Cl(p,q;1)$ is a two-sided ideal of square zero; the series treats these algebras, their nilpotent ideals and their one-sided completions in the sheaf paper, and a nilpotent generator is the vector-type zero divisor whose resolution is the transport. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Fact~2.1, Thm.~3.1]{ButlerT10}; \cite[Thm.~3.1, Prop.~3.4, Thm.~4.4]{ButlerT4}; \cite[\S 4]{ButlerT1}.
odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point-deg.technical:
At $\Lambda = 0$ the parallel scale tractor $I$ is null and its stabiliser is parabolic, the Poincar\'e-type stabiliser of a null direction; the stabiliser rotates to the reductive de Sitter type exactly when $Q(I) \neq 0$, and for $\Lambda \neq 0$ the identity $Q(I)\,Q(V) = -1$ holds.

On the algebraic side, a quadratic space with a one-dimensional radical has Clifford algebra $\Cl(p,q;1)$ with a nilpotent generator $n$, $n^{2} = 0$, and $n\,\Cl(p,q;1)$ is a two-sided ideal of square zero. The series treats these degenerate algebras, their nilpotent ideals and their one-sided completions in the sheaf paper, and a nilpotent generator is the vector-type zero divisor whose resolution is the transport.
odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point-deg.lay: When the cosmological constant is exactly zero, the frozen point becomes a vector of zero length, and the symmetry it preserves changes character. On the algebra side, a geometry with one degenerate direction gives an algebra containing an element whose square is zero. The series has already studied such algebras, and treats that element as exactly the kind of breakdown its transport procedure is built to resolve. This entry collects those facts from earlier papers.

odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point-ext.technical:

odd-extensions.not-coupling-between-towe.formal: The cosmological constant is a datum of this tower's ascent (Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed}), and its coincidence with the residue-$5$ tower's abstract algebra carries no structure across the superselection, since the dark-matter paper's exactness argument is precisely that isomorphisms between towers that do not respect the soldering carry nothing (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue}). The coupling rule the dark-matter paper's odd towers need is not supplied by $\Lambda$.
odd-extensions.not-coupling-between-towe.technical:
The cosmological constant is a datum of this tower's ascent: the frozen point and the Stelle-West vector are the ascent's pair, signed by $\Lambda$. For $\Lambda > 0$ the algebra $\Cl(I^{\perp}) \cong \Cl(1,4)$ coincides with the residue-$5$ tower's abstract algebra, but the isomorphism is induced by an isometry of quadratic spaces and not by a map of soldered data.

The dark-matter paper's exactness argument is that isomorphisms between towers that do not respect the soldering carry no structure across the superselection. So the coincidence carries nothing, and the coupling rule the dark-matter paper's odd towers need is not supplied by $\Lambda$.
odd-extensions.not-coupling-between-towe.lay: The framework has several towers, separate families of possible matter sectors, kept apart by a rule that only maps respecting how each algebra is tied to spacetime can carry anything between them. The cosmological constant belongs to our own tower. For a positive cosmological constant its algebra happens to look like that of one dark tower, but the match ignores that tie to spacetime, so it carries nothing across. The cosmological constant therefore cannot be the link that couples the dark towers to ours.

odd-extensions.translation-bivectors-fro.technical:
Under the imported frozen-point geometry, let $e_{5} = V/|V|$ be the unit Stelle-West direction, which together with the Lorentz frame $e_{1},\ldots,e_{4}$ of $\{I,V\}^{\perp}$ generates $\Cl(I^{\perp})$ fibrewise. odd-extensions.transport-constrains-froz.technical:
Take $W = I_{0}^{\perp}$, the degenerate space of signature $(1,3;1)$ at $\Lambda = 0$ whose radical is spanned by the null frozen point $I$. Its minimal completion $\widetilde W$ has signature $(2,4)$ and is the rung, and the isometry fixing $W$ pointwise is unique, so the null partner $\varphi$ with $Q(I,\varphi) = 1$, $Q(\varphi) = 0$ and $\varphi$ orthogonal to the Lorentz frame of $W$ is canonical. Every vector orthogonal to the Lorentz frame is $aI + b\varphi$ with $Q(aI + b\varphi) = 2ab$, and a frozen point of cosmological constant $\Lambda$ has $2ab = \Lambda/3$.

The isometries of the completion fixing the Lorentz frame act on this plane as $O(1,1)$, whose orbits on nonzero vectors are exactly the level sets of the norm. So the norm $\Lambda/3$, sign and magnitude, is the one modulus of the frozen point the transport leaves free. No symmetry of the completion carries a positive norm to a negative one, the intermediate algebras $\Cl(I_{\Lambda}^{\perp})$ for the two signs are non-isomorphic, and nothing in the transport chooses between them.
odd-extensions.transport-constrains-froz.lay: When the cosmological constant is zero the frozen point becomes a vector of zero length, a degenerate spot that the series' transport completes into a larger, well-behaved space. That completion comes with a canonical plane and a preferred pair of directions in it. Every possible value of the cosmological constant corresponds to a point in this plane, and the available symmetries can move that point anywhere except to a point of different length. So the transport pins down everything about the frozen point except its length, which is the cosmological constant, and gives no reason to prefer a positive value over a negative one.

pred.dark-energy-w-minus-one.formal:
Dark energy cannot evolve: $w = -1$ exactly, at every epoch; registered with its one condition, that on matter-filled regions the gravitational connection, the $\Cl(2,4)$ connection that preserves the frozen point $I$, keeps it parallel in the physical scale, $\ip{X}{I} = 1$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-condition}(iii)); in that form the condition is the field-space premise (FS) of the gravitational action (Premise \claimref{synthesis.field-space-premise-parallel-frozen-point}), which the store adopts.

\emph{Note (deflation).} On the reduced field space of (FS) the norm $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ is constant, so $\Lambda$ is a constant parameter and $w = -1$ is the $\Lambda$CDM equation of state. A confirmed $w = -1$ therefore supports $\Lambda$CDM with a frozen point but is not evidence for (FS) independent of $\Lambda$CDM; a confirmed $w \neq -1$ would refute (FS), and $\Lambda$CDM with it (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.parallel-frozen-point-on-matter-regions-is-the-field-space-premise}, Reading).

\emph{Note (the registered region).} In the two-parameter form $w(a) = w_{0} + w_{a}(1 - a)$ the prediction is the single point $(w_{0}, w_{a}) = (-1, 0)$. The series counts it refuted when two independent surveys each exclude that point at five standard deviations or more. Two surveys are independent when their late-time data (galaxy, supernova and lensing samples) are disjoint; each may use the shared CMB prior. The significance is the collaboration's published frequentist distance of the point (the two-parameter $\Delta\chi^{2}$ converted to standard deviations); the Bayesian evidence is recorded beside it and does not decide. The wording ``at any epoch'' stays as the model-independent reading: an exclusion of constant dark-energy density at some epoch, at the same significance and by two independent surveys, in an analysis not tied to the two-parameter form, counts the same. The rule is conservative: under it the series counts $w = -1$ as standing through releases in which a combined analysis reports a preference for evolution at three or four standard deviations, and it says so here.

\emph{Note (no fallback; argued).} A search of the store, not a proof, finds no adopted structure that permits a dark-energy equation of state different from $-1$ on an accelerating solution, so the series has no fallback for $w \neq -1$. Of the two stored ways of making the norm a variable, the promoted norm keeps $w = -1$ on every solution, and the norm released locally gives, under hypothesis (Mat), for the bare functional on isotropic fields with flat slices, a cosmological term that tracks one fluid with deceleration, no solution with radiation and no prediction in vacuum (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.norm-released-locally-on-isotropic-fields-tracks-dust-and-never-accelerates}(iv)-(vii), within its scope). The same search finds one stored structure with a late-time equation of state different from $-1$: the branch of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.unit-ball-clauses-hold-at-one-epoch-unless-hidden-direction-co-expands}(ii) with R3 standing and a static hidden direction, in which a fraction between $0.316$ and $0.317$ of the dark matter dilutes with effective $w = -\tfrac14$. It is not a fallback: the branch is not adopted; it is a dark-matter component and not a variable norm, with no pressure derived; read with the constant as one dark energy it has $w > -1$ at every epoch and approaches $-1$ from above, so $w_{a} > 0$ and no crossing of $-1$, against the quadrant $w_{0} > -1$, $w_{a} < 0$ of the survey fits in the observations below; and its share grows by the factor between $189$ and $190$ from $1 + z = 1090$ stated there, so the dark-matter densities inferred at that epoch and today would disagree (not confronted with data here). The exponent of the hidden direction in that branch is therefore not a parameter available to absorb a detection, and adopting it after one would be a fit. A detection by the registered rule would refute (FS) and the reading of dark energy as the frozen point's norm, and the series would need a new premise.
pred.dark-energy-w-minus-one.technical:
The stance reads dark energy as the norm of the frozen point, $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$. On the Einstein region the frozen point is parallel, so the norm cannot vary and enters the Einstein equations as stress-energy with $p = -\rho$, that is $w = -1$. The prediction extends this to every epoch: $w = -1$ exactly, with no evolution, under its one registered condition, that on matter-filled regions the gravitational connection, the one preserving the frozen point, keeps it parallel in the physical scale. That condition is the field-space premise (FS) of the gravitational action, which the store adopts.

On that field space $\Lambda$ is a constant parameter and $w = -1$ is the $\Lambda$CDM equation of state, so a confirmed $w = -1$ supports $\Lambda$CDM with a frozen point and is not independent evidence for (FS). A confirmed detection of $w \neq -1$ at any epoch would refute it, with no parameter available to absorb the result.

What counts as confirmed is registered. In the two-parameter form $w(a) = w_{0} + w_{a}(1 - a)$ the prediction is the point $(w_{0}, w_{a}) = (-1, 0)$, and it is refuted when two independent surveys (disjoint late-time data, the CMB prior allowed in each) each exclude that point at five standard deviations by the collaboration's published frequentist distance, with the Bayesian evidence recorded beside it; a model-independent exclusion of constant dark-energy density at some epoch counts by the same rule. The rule is conservative: combined analyses at three or four standard deviations do not meet it. The series has no fallback (argued, from a search of the store and not a proof): the promoted norm keeps $w = -1$, the locally released norm tracks one fluid and decelerates within the scope of the stored result, and the one stored structure with a late-time equation of state different from $-1$, an unadopted dark-matter branch with effective $w = -\tfrac14$, has $w_{a} > 0$ and never crosses $-1$, the opposite of the survey fits, and would make the dark-matter densities inferred early and late disagree.
pred.dark-energy-w-minus-one.lay: The framework says dark energy is not a substance that can change over time but a fixed geometric quantity. That means its equation of state, the ratio of its pressure to its energy density, must be exactly minus one at all times. This rests on one stated assumption about how the underlying geometry extends into regions filled with matter, an assumption the series now adopts for its law of gravity. Under that assumption dark energy behaves exactly as in the standard cosmological model, so a measurement that it never changes would agree with the series without being separate evidence for the assumption. Any confirmed measurement of a different value at any point in cosmic history would rule the idea out. What counts as confirmed is fixed in advance: two independent surveys must each exclude an unchanging dark energy at five standard deviations, the usual threshold for a discovery, by the survey team's own published measure. This is a cautious rule, and it means the series will keep the prediction standing through results that fall short of it, including combined analyses at three or four standard deviations. As far as a search of the collection shows, the series has nothing to fall back on if the rule is met: it would need a new assumption.

programme.n-parameter-of-the-laws.formal:
Under the action as written, with $\Lambda$ fixed before variation, $N = M_{P}/H$ is a parameter of the laws (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws}). The series adopts the Henneaux-Teitelboim promotion of the Stelle-West norm to the value of a Lagrange-multiplier field with $d\Lambda = 0$ as an equation of motion (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-henneaux-teitelboim-promotion}). Under the promoted action $N$ is initial data of the descent, dated to the origin: the norm mode is one global pair $(\Lambda, \tau)$ with no local mode, $N$ is constant on each solution and takes every positive value across the solution space (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.promoted-norm-one-global-pair}), and on the Clausius route alone it is initial data even without the promotion (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-route-makes-n-initial-data}(i)). The weak scale's constant of the laws is the D-term level, strictly $\xi G$ (Premise \claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-second-free-number}, version 3), so $v/M_{P}$ is the law up to relative order $(H/v)^{4}$, $v/H = (v/M_{P})N$ is initial data, and $Gv^{2}N^{2} = (v/H)^{2}$ is an identity, not a law (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-route-makes-n-initial-data}(iii), Theorem \claimref{synthesis.constant-d-term-level-fixes-weak-scale-against-planck-under-promotion}). \emph{Note (register, 2026-11-01).} Until version 5 this sentence read that the rung unit $v/H$ stays a parameter of the laws, so that $v/M_{P}$ is initial data and $Gv^{2}N^{2} = (v/H)^{2}$ holds as a law; the stored D-term action with a constant level, read under the promotion, makes $v/H$ initial data instead, and the register was restated accordingly. The time $\tau$ conjugate to the promoted norm is that of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.promoted-norm-weyl-clock-flat-weight}: for the frozen-point action it advances by the Euler-density excess, the integral over the background region of a density built from the field strength $\mathcal{R}(B)$ of the gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), with measure $\det(\hb)^{-1}d^{4}x$, which in vacuum is the integral of the square of the Weyl part $\mathcal{W}$ and stands still on the de Sitter field, and with matter runs on every FLRW gravitational field with dust or radiation; it is not monotone, changing sign for dust at $8\pi G\rho = \Lambda$, so it is a record of the history and not a time ordering it, and by an argued reading its advance is dominated by the earliest, hottest epoch. Why $\Lambda$, and so $N$, is small is outside the series: the promotion makes it initial data, the only measure it names, the Liouville density per unit $\tau$, is flat in whichever function of the norm is promoted (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.promoted-norm-one-global-pair}), and a normalisable measure over $\Lambda$ would need a further number.

\emph{Beyond one flat chart.} The compact spatial slices on which the promoted norm mode is one global pair $(\Lambda, \tau)$ are global and are not carried by a single gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime; the statements above that hold on the invertible region are in GTG, and the compact slices are read on the manifold assembled from the derived metric's charts.

\emph{Note (the Hubble unit).} Here $H$ is the de Sitter rate of $\Lambda$, $H^{2} = \Lambda/3$, that is $H_{0}\sqrt{\Omega_{\Lambda}}$, the $H$ of $N = M_{P}/H$; some texts quote $v/H$ with $H_{0}$, which differs from it by the factor $\sqrt{\Omega_{\Lambda}}$, of order one ($v/H \approx 2.1 \times 10^{44}$ against $v/H_{0} \approx 1.7 \times 10^{44}$; $\ln(v/H)$ changes by about $0.2$). No number here depends on the choice.

\emph{Note (register, 2026-11-01).} $N$ is now registered as a free input of the series by Premise \claimref{synthesis.number-n-registered-free-input}, as the D-term level $\xi G$ is by Premise \claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-second-free-number}; that premise carries the statement above of what kind of number $N$ is, unchanged, and this entity's placement of it stays a conjecture.

standard-model.dating-descent.formal:
(i) The one apparent indication fails. Near the onset of $\Lambda$-domination the age of the universe is automatically of order $N$ Planck times, since $t \sim 1/H$ there and $N = M_{P}/H$ (later the age grows while $1/H$ stays fixed): the Dirac coincidence is a property of the epoch we observe from, not a clock pointing at the descent. The programme's last indication was never one. (ii) The framework then answers, as its own claim and under the promotion it adopts: the descent froze at the beginning. The initial singularity is a division event; the classical era is the descended phase; under the Henneaux-Teitelboim promotion of the Stelle-West norm to the value of a Lagrange-multiplier field whose constancy is an equation of motion (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-henneaux-teitelboim-promotion}), which the series adopts, the frozen point, hence $\Lambda$, hence $N$, was fixed at the origin and has been constant since, which matches the registered stance $w = -1$ (registered with its own condition, \claimref{pred.dark-energy-w-minus-one}). $N$ is then initial data of the descent (\claimref{programme.n-parameter-of-the-laws}); with the weak scale's constant of the laws the D-term level $\xi G$ (Premise \claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-second-free-number}, version 3), $v/M_{P}$ is the law up to relative order $(H/v)^{4}$, the rung unit $v/H$ is initial data too, and $Gv^{2}N^{2} = (v/H)^{2}$ is an identity (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-route-makes-n-initial-data}(iii)). \emph{Note (register, 2026-11-01).} Until version 4 this sentence kept $v/H$ as a parameter of the laws, with $v/M_{P}$ initial data and $Gv^{2}N^{2} = (v/H)^{2}$ a law; the register was restated when the stored D-term action, read under the promotion, made $v/H$ initial data (\claimref{synthesis.constant-d-term-level-fixes-weak-scale-against-planck-under-promotion}). Under the action as written, with $\Lambda$ fixed before variation, $N$ would instead be a parameter of the laws (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws}, Remark \claimref{note.dark-energy.what-clause-3-requires-what-it}). The time conjugate to the promoted norm (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.promoted-norm-weyl-clock-flat-weight}) runs with matter, is not monotone and, by an argued reading, advances fastest in the earliest epoch: it is a record of the descended history, not a clock that dates the descent. Why $\Lambda$ is small is outside the series. The big bang, in this reading, is not an explosion in spacetime but the freezing of spacetime out of the ascended phase: the universe's descent is its origin. (iii) At observation level: pre-descent physics is the pre-metric sector, the polynomial action and the $\theta$-remnants alone (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.gravity-pre-metric-forces-degenerate-exactly}), and the dating reads the descent event, not an inflationary epoch, as the source of the earliest correlations. In the descended phase no mode at or below the pivot scale leaves the Hubble length after the descent, so the descent can source the measured primordial spectrum only through a pre-metric deposit correlated over hundreds (descent at $1$ MeV) to about $10^{18}$ (descent at $10^{12}$ GeV) Hubble lengths of the descent, for a deposit that is a perturbation (one-point variance at most one), or through a source acting after the descent (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.finite-range-descent-deposit-cannot-seed-cmb}). The series supplies neither, so it has no mechanism for the measured spectrum, neither its amplitude nor its index $n_{s}$; it registers no prediction of the tensor amplitude. The join of the frozen phase to the descent has two readings. The primary one, (F), takes the late de Sitter stage of the observed $\Lambda$ to be the frozen point's own field, so the descent slice sits at $|x_{d}| = \eta_{\infty} - \eta_{d}$ in the frozen point's chart, about $4.3$ present Hubble radii, and the observed modes have $k|x_{d}|$ from about $2.7$ to about $10^{4}$ (about $960$ at the pivot). The second reading takes the frozen phase to end at the descent with the scale factor continuous; the observed modes then lie inside the frozen phase's Hubble length by $k/(a_{d}H_{\Lambda}) > 4 \times 10^{9}$ at $1$ MeV ($> 7 \times 10^{9}$ for $k \ge a_{0}H_{0}$). In both readings every observed mode is inside the frozen phase's Hubble length at the descent, so a deposit correlated by the frozen point supplies the range the amplitude needs but reads as the vacuum, $n_{s} - 1 = 2$ (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-geometry-reads-descent-as-vacuum}); the readings differ in how far inside the modes sit, and only in (F) does the frozen point's one length enter the observed range, at the largest scales. (iv) The residue: the dynamics of the freezing itself, declared beyond this paper's scope. The last question of the theory is the first event of the universe.

\emph{Note (the Hubble unit).} Here $H$ is the de Sitter rate of $\Lambda$, $H^{2} = \Lambda/3$, that is $H_{0}\sqrt{\Omega_{\Lambda}}$, the $H$ of $N = M_{P}/H$; some texts quote $v/H$ with $H_{0}$, which differs from it by the factor $\sqrt{\Omega_{\Lambda}}$, of order one ($v/H \approx 2.1 \times 10^{44}$ against $v/H_{0} \approx 1.7 \times 10^{44}$; $\ln(v/H)$ changes by about $0.2$). No value of $v/H$ is quoted here.
standard-model.dating-descent.technical:
At observation level. In any $\Lambda$-dominated epoch the age of the universe is of order $N$ Planck times, since $t \sim 1/H$ and $N = M_{P}/H$, so the Dirac coincidence is an identity of the era we observe from and not a clock pointing at the descent. The framework then takes as its own claim, under the promotion it adopts, that the descent froze at the beginning: the initial singularity is a division event, the classical era is the descended phase, and with the Stelle-West norm promoted to a Lagrange-multiplier field in the manner of Henneaux and Teitelboim, the frozen point, hence $\Lambda$ and $N$, was fixed at the origin and has been constant since, which matches the registered stance $w = -1$ with its own condition. $N$ is initial data; the weak scale in Planck units is the law (through the D-term level), so the rung unit $v/H$ is initial data too, and $Gv^{2}N^{2} = (v/H)^{2}$ is an identity. For the action as written $N$ would be a parameter of the laws. The promotion's conjugate time runs with matter but is not monotone, a record of the history rather than a date for the descent, and the smallness of $\Lambda$ is outside the series.

The dating reads the descent event rather than an inflationary epoch as the source of the earliest correlations. After the descent no mode at or below the pivot scale leaves the Hubble length, so the measured spectrum would need a pre-metric deposit correlated over hundreds to about $10^{18}$ Hubble lengths of the descent, depending on its temperature, or a source acting after the descent. The series supplies neither, so it has no mechanism for the measured spectrum or its index; no tensor amplitude is registered. Whether the frozen phase is read as the late de Sitter stage of the observed $\Lambda$ (the primary reading) or as a phase ending at the descent with a continuous scale factor (a second reading), the observed modes were inside its Hubble length at the descent, so a deposit correlated by the frozen point gives the vacuum's spectrum, not the measured one. The dynamics of the freezing itself are declared beyond scope.
standard-model.dating-descent.lay: A famous coincidence says that the age of the universe, measured in the tiniest natural unit of time, is about the same huge number that appears elsewhere in the framework. This observation argues that the coincidence is automatic in any universe dominated by dark energy, so it is not a clue about when anything happened. Instead the framework proposes that the number was fixed at the very beginning, with the big bang read as spacetime freezing out of an earlier phase. That proposal uses a known modification of the theory, which the framework adopts, making the cosmological constant a quantity set by the particular universe; why its value is so small is left outside the framework. The framework would like the first event to have laid down the ripples later seen in the cosmic background, but those ripples span distances far larger than anything in contact at that event, so they would need correlations already present before spacetime, or a later source, and the framework provides neither. How the freezing happened is also left open.

standard-model.imported-frozen-point-dic.formal:
On the Einstein region with $\Lambda \neq 0$ of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), the frozen point $I$ is the scale tractor parallel for the tractor gauge field of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}, of squared norm $Q(I) = \Lambda/3 = H^{2}$, and in the flat chart of the conformal model (the flat twistor chart, the flat background itself) its frozen point is $I_{\Lambda} = n_{\infty} + (\Lambda/6)\,n_{0}$, in the normalisation $n_{0}\cdot n_{\infty} = +1$ (there $Q(I_{\Lambda}) = \Lambda/3$; in T01's normalisation the same vector has $Q(I_{\Lambda}) = -\Lambda/3$). Mass is conformal weight read against it: a density of weight $w$ coupled to the frozen point obeys the Klein-Gordon equation with
\[
m^{2} = -\,w(w+3)\,\frac{\Lambda}{3} = \Delta(3-\Delta)\,H^{2}, \qquad \Delta = -w,
\]
so a real weight gives $m^{2} \ge 0$ only on $w \in [-3, 0]$, where $m \le 3H/2$, and every heavier field has complex weight $w = -\tfrac32 \pm I_4\nu$ (numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$) with $\nu \approx m/H$. In particular the weight of the Planck mass is complex, and its imaginary part is
\[
N := \operatorname{Im} w(M_{P}) \approx M_{P}/H, \qquad\text{about } 1.0 \times 10^{61}.
\]
Throughout this paper $N$ means $M_{P}/H$, the number the dictionary attaches to the Planck mass. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Thms.~4.5, 4.7]{ButlerT6} for the frozen point and its norm; \cite[Thm.~3.1, Cor.~3.2]{ButlerT11} for the dictionary and the complex weights; \cite[Lem.~5.1]{ButlerT11} for the chart form of $I_{\Lambda}$. The value, about $1.0 \times 10^{61}$ for $G = M_{P}^{-2}$, is the measured ratio $M_{P}/H$ and carries the record's status \cite{PDG2024}.

standard-model.imported-norm-frozen-poin.formal: In the three-argument form of the gravitational action the frozen point enters subject to the Stelle-West constraint $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$, every fluctuation of the constrained pair $(I, V)$ is a gauge transformation (unitary gauge $\delta I = \delta V = 0$ exists and is complete), and the second variation of the action involves only the connection. The action therefore carries no equation of motion for $\Lambda$: the norm is fixed by a constraint, not evolved by a field equation. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Prop.~5.4]{ButlerT10}; covariant constancy of the frozen point of norm $\Lambda/3$ is \cite[Prop.~4.2(i)]{ButlerT10} and \cite[Thms.~4.5, 4.7]{ButlerT6}.

Every fluctuation of the constrained pair $(I,V)$ is a gauge transformation, so the unitary gauge $\delta I = \delta V = 0$ exists and is complete, and the second variation of the action involves only the connection.

standard-model.largeness-number-universe.formal: Observations \claimref{standard-model.what} through \claimref{standard-model.dating-descent} force a unification of questions: `why is $N$ large' is `why is the universe's own horizon mode space so large', which is the dating question just registered. The size of that space is fixed by $N$ and is not $N$: the cosmological horizon's entropy is exactly $\pi N^{2}$ under the Einstein-Hilbert area law (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-entropy-pi-n-squared}, from Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gibbons-hawking-entropy}); the Gauss-Bonnet term of the MacDowell-Mansouri action as written (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}) contributes $-\pi N^{2}$, so the reading below presupposes that topological term subtracted or normalised away. Under the black hole's counting rule its boundary modes number $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$, about $4.8 \times 10^{122}$ (a count of registered units of capacity $\ln 2$, not of rungs or of ladder pairs), with $N$, about $1.0 \times 10^{61}$, the square root of that count up to $\sqrt{\pi/\ln 2}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-mode-count}). standard-model.one-number-explain.formal: The gravitational action of the action paper carries, in its curvature-squared presentation, a single dimensionless combination of scales, $G\Lambda$, the relative coefficient of its Einstein-Hilbert and Gauss-Bonnet terms (\cite[Thm.~3.1(2)]{ButlerT10}; reading that coefficient as \emph{the} dimensionless coupling is this paper's, not the action paper's). Let $N = M_{P}/H$, the number the dictionary of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-frozen-point-dictionary} attaches to the Planck mass, about $1.0 \times 10^{61}$. Then, as an exact exponent computation, the framework's well-known smallness problems are all powers of $N$: the cosmological-constant problem is $G\Lambda = 3N^{-2}$; the weakness of gravity relative to a dimension-one matter coupling, evaluated at the Hubble scale, is $N^{-2}$; and the mass hierarchy is the statement that the imaginary weight of a mass $m$ is $\operatorname{Im} w = (m/M_{P})\,N$. The numerical layer of the programme therefore reduces to a single question: why is $N$ large? That question this framework does not answer; what it has done is ensure there is only one of it. The computation is exact and script-checked; the choice of $H$ as the comparison scale for gravity's weakness, and the reading of the three problems as one, are conventions, which is why this is an Observation. The reading has a limit the computation shows. The first two problems are one number by the definition of $N$: both are $(H/M_{P})^{2}$, the first times $3$. The third is not a power of $N$, and not exact as written: $\operatorname{Im} w = (m/M_{P})\,N$ holds to relative order $H^{2}/m^{2}$ for $m > 3H/2$ (exactly, the weight's Casimir is $-w(w+3) = (m/M_{P})^{2}N^{2}$, Proposition \claimref{synthesis.smallness-monomials-exact-hierarchy-casimir}), and it carries a second ratio, $m/M_{P}$, which for the weak scale is the rung unit $v/M_{P} \approx 2.0 \times 10^{-17}$, between $N^{-0.28}$ and $N^{-0.27}$; it is invariant under the rescaling of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number}(1) and so kinematically not a function of $N$ (Proposition \claimref{families.why-kinematic-attacks-had-fail}, at the level of its observation-level invariance premise). One number is to be explained for the cosmological-constant problem and gravity's weakness; the mass hierarchy adds the second continuous modulus that Proposition \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number}(1) lists beside $N$, the weight spectrum.

standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-numb.formal:
The question the paper ends by pointing at can itself be classified. The classification has four parts, of which the first contains a proved statement and a reading, the second is an import, the third is conditional on the first two, on Observation \claimref{standard-model.dating-descent} and on a decision the fourth names, and the fourth is imported from the action paper; the levels are marked clause by clause.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Kinematic.)} Proved: under $\Lambda \to s^{2}\Lambda$ at fixed $M_{P}$, that is $I \to sI$ on the frozen point with the conformal class unchanged, $H \to sH$ and $N \to N/s$, while every discrete invariant this paper derives (the algebra and its dimension twelve, the global form and its $\mathbb{Z}_{6}$, the dimension four, the content and the hypercharges, and under (S) the ratio $3/8$) is unchanged, since each is computed from the conformal class, the pair structure and the group alone, none of which the rescaling affects. Reading, at observation level: since the conformal class and the pair structure carry no scale, no construction from them alone can fix $N$, which lies in the ratio of the frozen point's norm to the Planck scale; on this reading the kinematic layer determines all discrete invariants and no continuous modulus, and $N$ and the weight spectrum are its only continuous moduli.
\item \emph{(Non-dynamical, imported.)} $\Lambda$ is the norm of the frozen point, and the norm is not a field: it is fixed by a constraint, the fluctuations of the frozen point are pure gauge, and the action carries no equation of motion for it (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-norm-frozen-point-not-field}).
\item \emph{(Initial data, conditional.)} If the alternatives kinematic, dynamical and initial-data are exhaustive, then by (1) and (2) $N$ is initial data, and Observation \claimref{standard-model.dating-descent}(ii) locates the boundary that carries it at the origin. The exhaustiveness is not proved here, and the location is an Observation; the clause is conditional on both, and clause (4) says what the exhaustiveness costs.
\item \emph{(Parameter of the laws, imported.)} The three alternatives are not exhaustive: a conserved quantity that is constant on every solution of a theory but varies across a family of theories indexed by a parameter is a parameter of the laws, and the action paper proves that under the action as written, with $\Lambda$ the value of the Stelle-West constraints fixed before variation, $N$ is exactly that: constant on each solution space $\mathcal{S}_{\Lambda}$ by the rigidity of (2), varying across $\Lambda$, so neither dynamically fixed nor initial data \cite[Prop.~5.8]{ButlerT10}. Clause (3) therefore holds only if the norm is promoted from a fixed number to the value of a Lagrange-multiplier field whose constancy is an equation of motion, the Henneaux-Teitelboim mechanism, which makes $\Lambda$ a label of the solution rather than of the theory; that promotion is a decision for the series, recorded open with both branches stated \cite[Rem.~5.9]{ButlerT10}, which the store adopts (\claimref{programme.n-parameter-of-the-laws}), and the entropic and null-endpoint effects named below act on a measure over theories or on a measure within one theory according to it.
\end{enumerate}
At observation level, two competing effects are then named without being balanced: an entropic weighting of the freezing by $\exp(S_{\Lambda}) = \exp(\pi N^{2})$, with $S_{\Lambda} = \pi N^{2}$ the cosmological horizon's area-law entropy (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-entropy-pi-n-squared}), favours large $N$ overwhelmingly (the well-known entropic argument for small $\Lambda$, inherited with every one of its known objections, listed as inherited and not solved), while at the endpoint $\Lambda = 0$ the frozen point is null and the curvature-squared presentation of the action, whose prefactor is $3/\Lambda$, does not exist; the action paper is explicit that this is a boundary of the presentation and not of the action, the Einstein-Cartan functional remaining \cite[Thm.~3.1, Rem.~3.2]{ButlerT10}, so what is lost at $\Lambda = 0$ is the reductive structure and the frozen point's length, not gravity. Large because large boundary mode spaces dominate the measure; nonzero because the descent selects a frozen point of nonzero length; the value is the balance point, and the balance point awaits the descent measure, the one object this framework does not possess. Last, a statement of units only, flagged as such: in the boundary modes' own units, qubits, one per rung of the Fock module (Theorem \claimref{tower.fock-module-one-qubit-per-rung}), the horizon's capacity $S_{\Lambda} = \pi N^{2}$ is $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$, about $4.8 \times 10^{122}$ qubits (the mode count of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-mode-count} under the black hole's counting rule), whose base-two logarithm is about $407$. The qubit is here a unit of capacity, $\ln 2$: the horizon count is a count of registered units of that capacity, not of rungs or of ladder pairs, and no integrality of $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$ is claimed. The paper's $R = \log_{2} N^{2} \approx 405$ counts the rungs of a module of dimension $N^{2}$, whose capacity is only $\ln N^{2} = 2\ln N$ nats, not the horizon's. Neither number is a count of turns of the mod-8 clock, which no rung moves: each rung preserves the residue $p - q \pmod 8$ (Theorem \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial}). This is the question in the framework's own coordinates, not an answer to it.

\emph{Note (the Hubble unit).} The numbers for $N = M_{P}/H$ here use $H^{2} = \Lambda/3$, that is $H_{0}\sqrt{\Omega_{\Lambda}}$ (with $H_{0} = 67.4$ km/s/Mpc and $\Omega_{\Lambda} = 0.685$), the $H$ in which the register states the rung unit $v/H$; some texts quote $v/H$ with $H_{0}$, which differs by the factor $\sqrt{\Omega_{\Lambda}}$, of order one ($\ln(v/H)$ changes by about $0.2$). No value of $v/H$ is quoted here.

standard-model.what.formal: (i) The boundary-mode count of the entropy paper T8 \cite[\S 3, Thm.~3.4]{ButlerT8}, applied to the cosmological horizon rather than to the black-hole singularity, was offered here as a preliminary indication that the de Sitter horizon entropy is of order $N^{2}$, so that $N$ is the square root of the pair capacity of the universe's own boundary mode space. No paper of the series performs that application; it is now performed in the store. Under the Einstein-Hilbert area law the horizon entropy is exactly $S_{\Lambda} = \pi N^{2}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-entropy-pi-n-squared}), and if the horizon's modes are counted by the black hole's rule they number $|J| = \pi N^{2}/\ln 2$, about $4.8 \times 10^{122}$, with capacity $C = |J|\ln 2 = S_{\Lambda}$, so that $N = \sqrt{C/\pi}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-mode-count}). The indication therefore holds exactly for the entropy and up to the factor $\sqrt{\pi}$ for the capacity; $N$, about $1.0 \times 10^{61}$, is not itself the number of the universe's boundary modes but the square root of that number up to $\sqrt{\pi/\ln 2}$. (ii) This bears on the question as posed. The ascended action is polynomial with no dimensionless constants, and every scale enters through the frozen point. Under the action as written, with the frozen point's norm fixed before variation, $N$ is a parameter of the laws, an import recorded in Proposition \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number}(4); under the promoted action, where the norm is the value of a Lagrange-multiplier field, the frozen point is a property of the selected descent, $N$ is a state-count and not a coupling, and to ask that it be derived from the laws is to ask a question that refutes itself as posed. Which reading holds is the decision Proposition \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number}(4) records open, which the store adopts (\claimref{programme.n-parameter-of-the-laws}), and the capstone \cite[Table~1]{ButlerT17} keeps the count. (iii) The Dirac coincidence ($N$ is also, at present, the age of the universe in Planck units) would suggest $N$ is a clock and $\Lambda$ decays as $1/t^{2}$; but the series' registered prediction $w = -1$ exactly \cite[Prop.~4.2(iii)]{ButlerT10}, itself registered and conditional there, forbids this: the frozen point is frozen. The framework predicts that the coincidence is epochal, and that prediction is tested by the dark-energy measurement of $w$ already registered in the series.

standard-model.why-large.formal: (i) \emph{The exponential reading, and what it is.} If the pair construction is iterated from the base case of three so that each level's objects are the fermionic pairs of the level above (a reading of the tower that no paper of the series proves: the tower paper's rungs add one qubit each \cite[Thm.~4.2]{ButlerT3}, and the exponential reading is stated here as a reading), the counts run $3$, then $2^{3} = 8$, then $2^{8} = 256$, then $2^{256}$ of order $10^{77}$, within three steps. Made precise, the reading is the iterated Fock construction: the $2^{k}$ states of $k$ ladder pairs become the creators of a new level and as many annihilators are adjoined, and under that rule the counts hold exactly (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.exponential-reading-of-the-tower-is-the-iterated-fock-functor-not-the-ascent}(i)). It is not a step of the proved ascent, which adjoins one pair per step, so that three pairs become four, with sixteen states, and not eight; the levels of the reading are the floors $3$, $8$, $256$ of the one tower, reached by $2^{k} - k$ ascents each, and no level of $j$ pairs holds more than $j$ anticommuting pairs of any elements (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.exponential-reading-of-the-tower-is-the-iterated-fock-functor-not-the-ascent}(ii), (iii)). It is one of at least two counting rules with a claim to the wording: taking the states of a level, with an invariant symmetric form of the Fock module, as the generating vectors of the next gives the pair counts $3, 4, 8, 128, 2^{127}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.invariant-forms-on-the-fock-module-and-the-pair-counts-of-a-next-level}(v), where calling this a reading of the same phrase is recorded as a judgement). Nothing stored selects one rule, or the floors that either rule names (argued in both results, from a reading of the stored tower results and not from an audit). The base count is a choice too: the three of the reading is the complex capacity of the space of signature $(2,4)$, whose real capacity is two (Theorem \claimref{one-relation.two-capacities-three-consequences}), while the precise forms are established on three real pairs, $\Cl(3,3)$; from two real pairs the first rule would read $2, 4, 16, 65536$ and the second does not start. What the reading supports is therefore conditional: given a rule of this kind, counts of order $10^{38}$ (second rule) or $10^{77}$ (first rule) arise within four or three steps. It does not support the statement that large counts are the generic output of the tower: on the proved tower the number of pairs at the floor $j$ is $j$ and only the number of states, $2^{j}$, grows exponentially, so the reading supplies no mechanism for the largeness of $N$. (ii) \emph{The inverted question, as a comparison of sizes only.} Given a rule, the question the reading puts in place of `why is $N$ large' is why the universe's horizon count is as small as it is: $|J| = \pi N^{2}/\ln 2$, of order $10^{122}$, with $N$ of order $10^{61}$ its square root up to $\sqrt{\pi/\ln 2}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-mode-count}, under the black hole's counting rule), lies between the third level of the first rule ($2^{256}$, of order $10^{77}$) and its fourth ($2^{2^{256}}$), and between the terms $2^{127}$ and $2^{2^{127} - 1}$ of the second (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.exponential-reading-of-the-tower-is-the-iterated-fock-functor-not-the-ascent}(v), Theorem \claimref{synthesis.invariant-forms-on-the-fock-module-and-the-pair-counts-of-a-next-level}(v)). The comparison is of sizes only: the stored count is of registered units averaging two arrays, not of ladder pairs or rungs (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.the-residue-requires-two-arrays-per-unit-on-average-and-fixes-no-grouping}), so the horizon count is not a level of either rule; and every number whose base-two logarithm lies between $256$ and $2^{256}$ falls between the same two levels of the first rule, so the count neither tests the reading nor separates the rules. (iii) A candidate selection, at observation level: the Standard Model exists precisely at the minimal massive level of the hierarchy (Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite}); higher levels carry different and vastly larger automorphism structures; so matter of the observed kind, and observers made of it, exist only in low-level descents. The physics we see is the physics of the bottom of the tower, and a boundary mode space of order $10^{122}$ is what a descent near the base case, but old enough to have grown, looks like; `near the base case' is meant in the levels of whichever rule is adopted, and the candidate is not tied to one. (iv) The residue, exactly posed: derive the descent-selection dynamics, at which tower level a division event freezes, by which counting rule if by any, and whether boundary mode spaces of order $10^{122}$ are typical of descents near the base case. (v) \emph{The number itself.} Nothing here derives or bounds $N$. It is a registered free input of the series (Premise \claimref{synthesis.number-n-registered-free-input}), and at tree level on the lift family, at fixed D-term level and couplings, there is a vacuum for every value of $N$, with every stored relation found to contain $N$ holding in the models exhibited; that nothing stored fixes $N$ is argued there on a pattern search of the store (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.number-n-free-at-fixed-d-term-level-on-the-stored-relations}).

Given a rule, the question inverts: why is the universe's horizon count as small as order $10^{122}$ (with $N$, of order $10^{61}$, roughly its square root), between the third and fourth levels of the first rule and between $2^{127}$ and $2^{2^{127}-1}$ of the second. This compares sizes only: the stored count is of registered units, not of ladder pairs, and it neither tests the reading nor separates the rules. A candidate selection: the Standard Model sits at the minimal massive level of the hierarchy, higher levels carry different and much larger automorphism structures, and so matter of the observed kind, and observers made of it, exist only in low-level descents. The residue is to derive the descent-selection dynamics, the counting rule if any, and whether boundary mode spaces of order $10^{122}$ are typical of descents near the base case. $N$ itself stays a registered free input (Premise \claimref{synthesis.number-n-registered-free-input}); nothing stored is found to fix it (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.number-n-free-at-fixed-d-term-level-on-the-stored-relations}, argued on a pattern search).
standard-model.why-large.lay: One unproved reading of the framework's tower has it grow exponentially at each step, so that huge numbers appear almost at once and a large number like $N$ would need no special explanation. Made exact, that reading is a standard construction, in which every state of one level becomes a basic mode of the next, and it is not the step the tower's theorems describe: the proved step adds one mode at a time, so three modes become four, not eight. It is also only one of at least two ways of counting that fit the original wording; the other gives $3$, $4$, $8$, $128$ where the first gives $3$, $8$, $256$, and, as far as the stored results have been read (an argument, not a complete audit), nothing in the theory picks one. Even the starting value three is a count over complex numbers on a space whose real count is two. So the reading does not show that large numbers come for free. It says only that if levels are built by such a rule, large numbers follow quickly. The boundary of the observable universe holds about $10^{122}$ counted units, roughly the square of $N$, which in size lies between two consecutive steps of either rule; this is a comparison of sizes only, because those units are not the modes the rules count. The observation's proposal that observers like us can exist only near the bottom of the tower stays as a proposal, and working out the dynamics that would settle it is left open. $N$ itself remains a number the theory takes from observation.

synthesis.de-sitter-static-boost-frozen-.formal:
In the conventions of Lemma \claimref{mass.de-sitter-scale-frozen-point} ($\ip{\nO}{\nInf} = 1$, $X(x) = \nO + x - \tfrac12 Q(x)\,\nInf$) let $I_{\Lambda} = \nInf + \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\nO$ be the frozen point and $W = \nInf - \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\nO$, the value at the origin $x=0$ (for $\Lambda\neq0$) of the vector $W = V/Q(V)$ of Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.stelle-west-vector-frozen-point}, so that $\ip{W}{I_{\Lambda}} = 0$ and $Q(W) = -\Lambda/3$. Put $B_{\Lambda} := e_{0}\wedge W = e_{0}W$. Then, for every real $\Lambda$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $B_{\Lambda}$ commutes with $I_{\Lambda}$, so it lies in the stabiliser of the frozen point, and
\[
B_{\Lambda}^{2} \;=\; Q(I_{\Lambda}) \;=\; \frac{\Lambda}{3},
\]
a scalar.
\item[(ii)] Its Killing field $\xi = X \cdot B_{\Lambda}$ is tangent to the null cone, $Q(\xi)$ equals the flat-chart square of the velocity it induces, and $Q(\xi) = \bigl(1 + \tfrac{\Lambda}{12}Q(x)\bigr)^{2} - \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}x_{0}^{2}$. On the slice $x = r e_{1}$, with scale $\sigma = \ip{X}{I_{\Lambda}} = 1 + \tfrac{\Lambda}{12}r^{2}$ and areal radius $R = r/\sigma$, the physical norm is $g(\xi,\xi) = Q(\xi)/\sigma^{2} = 1 - \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}R^{2}$: $B_{\Lambda}$ generates the static time of the observer at $x = 0$, normalised to unit norm there.
\item[(iii)] For $\Lambda > 0$ the static patch has its Killing horizon at $R_{h} = \sqrt{3/\Lambda}$ with surface gravity $\kappa_{\Lambda} = \sqrt{\Lambda/3}$, so
\[
\kappa_{\Lambda}^{2} \;=\; B_{\Lambda}^{2} \;=\; Q(I_{\Lambda}) ;
\]
with $H = \sqrt{\Lambda/3}$, $B_{\Lambda} = H\,u$ where $u = e_{0}e_{W}$, $e_{W} = W/H$, $u^{2} = +1$: the static flow is generated by the unit ambient boost in the plane of $e_{0}$ and the unit Stelle-West direction at the origin $x=0$, at rapidity $H$ per unit Killing time. Its fixed set in the region $\sigma \neq 0$ is the bifurcation sphere $\{x_{0} = 0,\ Q(x) = -12/\Lambda\}$ ($R = R_{h}$), where the induced velocity vanishes and its linearisation is $H$ times the unit boost of the normal $(x_{0}, r)$ plane and zero along the sphere: the horizon's local boost rate is the same $\kappa_{\Lambda} = H$. The Euclidean section of the static patch is smooth at the horizon if and only if imaginary Killing time has period $2\pi/\kappa_{\Lambda} = 2\pi/\sqrt{Q(I_{\Lambda})}$, the counterpart of the $8\pi M$ of Proposition \claimref{singularity.euclidean-section-period}.
\item[(iv)] The sign of the frozen point's norm sorts the static flow: for $\Lambda > 0$ a boost, with a horizon; for $\Lambda = 0$, $B_{0} = e_{0}\nInf \neq 0$ with $B_{0}^{2} = 0$, a null rotation (the Poincar\'e time translation), no horizon and $\kappa = 0$; for $\Lambda < 0$, $B_{\Lambda}^{2} < 0$, a rotation, so the static time closes with period $2\pi/\sqrt{-\Lambda/3}$ and there is no horizon.
\item[(v)] Under reversal of the ambient form, $Q \mapsto -Q$ (the signature $(4,2)$ of the mirror's tractor bundle), $Q(I_{\Lambda})$ changes sign while $B_{\Lambda}^{2}$ does not. The convention-free statement is therefore $\kappa_{\Lambda}^{2} = B_{\Lambda}^{2}$, which reads $Q(I)$ in this world's convention and $-Q(I)'$ in the reversed one.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.de-sitter-static-boost-frozen-.lay: In the series the cosmological constant is carried by one fixed vector of the enlarged algebra, the frozen point. This result shows that the time flow seen by an observer in a universe with a positive cosmological constant is a single boost built from that vector, and that the boost's rate, which fixes how strongly the observer's horizon pulls, is exactly the square root of the frozen point's squared length. With no cosmological constant the same construction gives ordinary time translation and no horizon; with a negative one it gives a rotation, and time closes on itself.

proofs.main:
\emph{Step 1 (the pair).} By Lemma \claimref{mass.de-sitter-scale-frozen-point}, $I_{\Lambda} = \nInf + \lambda\nO$ with $\lambda = \Lambda/6$ and $\ip{\nO}{\nInf} = 1$, so $Q(I_{\Lambda}) = 2\lambda = \Lambda/3$. The vector $W = \nInf - \lambda\nO$ satisfies $\ip{W}{I_{\Lambda}} = \lambda - \lambda = 0$ and $Q(W) = -2\lambda = -\Lambda/3$; in the frozen-point scale it is the tractor $(1, 0, -\Lambda/6)$, the value at the origin $x=0$ (for $\Lambda\neq0$) of the $W = V/Q(V)$ of Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.stelle-west-vector-frozen-point}, whose $e_{a}\wedge W$ are the model connection's translation bivectors.

\emph{Step 2 (stabiliser and square).} $e_{0}$ and $W$ are orthogonal, so $B_{\Lambda} = e_{0}W = e_{0}\wedge W$ is a $2$-blade. Both factors are orthogonal to $I_{\Lambda}$ (for $e_{0}$ because $I_{\Lambda}$ lies in the added plane), so $I_{\Lambda}$ anticommutes with each and commutes with their product. For orthogonal vectors $(e_{0}W)^{2} = -Q(e_{0})\,Q(W) = -(1)(-\Lambda/3) = \Lambda/3$.

\emph{Step 3 (the Killing field).} For a null point $X$ the vector $\xi = X\cdot B_{\Lambda} = \tfrac12(XB_{\Lambda} - B_{\Lambda}X) = \ip{X}{e_{0}}W - \ip{X}{W}e_{0}$ satisfies $\ip{X}{\xi} = 0$, so it is tangent to the cone. Because $B_{\Lambda}$ commutes with $I_{\Lambda}$, its flow fixes $I_{\Lambda}$ and so preserves the scale $\sigma = \ip{X}{I_{\Lambda}}$ that fixes the metric $g = \sigma^{-2}\eta$ below; a flow that is conformal for $\eta$ and preserves $\sigma$ is an isometry of $g$, so $\xi$ is a Killing field and not only a conformal Killing field. Writing $\xi = \delta X + aX$ with $\delta X$ the variation of the embedding along the induced chart velocity $\delta x$, and using $Q(X) = 0$, $\ip{X}{\delta X} = 0$ and $Q(\delta X) = Q(\delta x)$, one gets $Q(\xi) = Q(\delta x)$. With $\ip{X}{e_{0}} = x_{0}$ and $\ip{X}{W} = 1 + \lambda Q(x)/2$,
\[
Q(\xi) = x_{0}^{2}Q(W) + \bigl(1 + \tfrac{\lambda}{2}Q(x)\bigr)^{2} = \bigl(1 + \tfrac{\Lambda}{12}Q(x)\bigr)^{2} - \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}x_{0}^{2} .
\]
The metric is $g = \sigma^{-2}\eta$ with $\sigma = \ip{X}{I_{\Lambda}} = 1 - \lambda Q(x)/2$ (Lemma \claimref{mass.de-sitter-scale-frozen-point}). On $x = re_{1}$, $Q(x) = -r^{2}$, $\sigma = 1 + \lambda r^{2}/2$, the sphere of chart radius $r$ has areal radius $R = r/\sigma$, and
\[
g(\xi,\xi) = \frac{(1 - \lambda r^{2}/2)^{2}}{(1 + \lambda r^{2}/2)^{2}} = 1 - \frac{2\lambda r^{2}}{(1 + \lambda r^{2}/2)^{2}} = 1 - 2\lambda R^{2} = 1 - \frac{\Lambda}{3}R^{2},
\]
the static form $f(R) = 1 - \Lambda R^{2}/3$, with $g(\xi,\xi) = 1$ at the origin.

\emph{Step 4 (horizon, surface gravity, period).} For $\Lambda > 0$, $f(R_{h}) = 0$ at $R_{h} = \sqrt{3/\Lambda}$. By Fact \claimref{singularity.imported-surface-gravity-redshifted-acceleration} the surface gravity of a static Killing horizon is the limit of the redshifted acceleration of static observers, $|f'(R)|/2$, so $\kappa_{\Lambda} = \Lambda R_{h}/3 = \sqrt{\Lambda/3}$ and $\kappa_{\Lambda}^{2} = \Lambda/3 = B_{\Lambda}^{2}$. With $H = \sqrt{\Lambda/3}$ and $e_{W} = W/H$, $Q(e_{W}) = -1$ and $u = e_{0}e_{W}$ squares to $+1$: $B_{\Lambda} = Hu$ is $H$ times a unit boost in the plane of $e_{0}$ and $e_{W}$. On the slice $x_{0} = 0$, $x = re_{1}$, the velocity of Step 3 is exactly $\delta x = -(1 - \lambda r^{2}/2)\,e_{0}$ (there $\ip{X}{e_{0}} = 0$ and $\xi$ has no component in the added plane), so it vanishes at $x_{0} = 0$, $r^{2} = 2/\lambda$, that is $Q(x) = -12/\Lambda$, where $\sigma = 2$ and $R = r/2 = R_{h}$. Off the slice, matching the $\nO$, vector and $\nInf$ parts of $\xi = x_{0}W - (1 + \lambda Q(x)/2)e_{0}$ against $\delta X + aX$ with $\delta X = \delta x - \ip{x}{\delta x}\nInf$ gives $a = -\lambda x_{0}$ and
\[
\delta x = -\bigl(1 + \tfrac{\lambda}{2}Q(x)\bigr)e_{0} + \lambda x_{0}\, x .
\]
Writing $x = x_{0}e_{0} + y$ with $y$ spatial, for $\Lambda \neq 0$ this vanishes if and only if $\lambda x_{0}y = 0$ and $\lambda x_{0}^{2} = 1 + \lambda Q(x)/2$: either $x_{0} = 0$ and $Q(x) = -12/\Lambda$ (the bifurcation sphere above), or $y = 0$ and $x_{0}^{2} = 12/\Lambda$, the two points $x = \pm\sqrt{12/\Lambda}\,e_{0}$, where $\sigma = 1 - \lambda x_{0}^{2}/2 = 0$, outside the region the metric covers. Both need $\Lambda > 0$, and for $\Lambda = 0$, $\delta x = -e_{0}$ never vanishes. The velocity is quadratic in $x$, and at the bifurcation sphere its Jacobian is $\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} 0 & H \\ H & 0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ on the $(x_{0}, r)$ plane and zero on the sphere directions, eigenvalues $\pm H$, a coordinate-independent statement at a zero of a vector field. The argument of Proposition \claimref{singularity.euclidean-section-period} uses only $f(R_{h}) = 0$ and $f'(R_{h}) \neq 0$: in proper distance $\varrho$ from the horizon the $(\varrho, \tau)$ plane carries $d\varrho^{2} + \kappa_{\Lambda}^{2}\varrho^{2}d\tau^{2} + O(\varrho^{4})d\tau^{2}$, smooth at $\varrho = 0$ if and only if $\tau$ has period $2\pi/\kappa_{\Lambda}$.

\emph{Step 5 (the three signs).} Step 2 holds for every $\Lambda$. At $\Lambda = 0$, $W = \nInf$ and $B_{0} = e_{0}\nInf$, nonzero with square $-Q(e_{0})\,Q(\nInf) = 0$: a null rotation, the translation $e^{-tB_{0}/2}X(x)\,e^{tB_{0}/2} = X(x - te_{0})$ of the flat model (the flow of the Killing field $X \cdot B_{0}$), with no fixed set and no horizon. For $\Lambda < 0$, $B_{\Lambda}^{2} = \Lambda/3 < 0$ and $\exp(tB_{\Lambda}/2)$ is periodic in $t$ with period $4\pi/\sqrt{-\Lambda/3}$, its conjugation action with period $2\pi/\sqrt{-\Lambda/3}$; $f(R) = 1 + |\Lambda|R^{2}/3$ has no zero.

\emph{Step 6 (reversal).} Under $Q \mapsto -Q$ the norms of $I_{\Lambda}$, $e_{0}$ and $W$ change sign, while $(e_{0}W)^{2} = -Q(e_{0})\,Q(W)$ is a product of two of them and does not.
