synthesis.norm-released-locally-on-isotr.formal:
\emph{Setting.} Take the frozen-point MacDowell-Mansouri functional of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west} and Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector} for a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), with the norm $u = -Q(V) = 3/\Lambda > 0$ of the Stelle-West vector: density $k\,u\,\epsilon(F, F)$, $k$ a nonzero constant, where $F(b \wedge c) = R(b \wedge c) + u^{-1}\,\hb^{-1}(b) \wedge \hb^{-1}(c)$ is the Lorentz block on background bivectors (on physical bivectors $-(\mathcal{R}(B) - u^{-1}B)$ in the store's sign) and $\epsilon(F, F)$ is the sum over the $24$ orderings of the background frame, with the sign of the ordering, of the coefficient of $e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}$ in $F(e_{\mu} \wedge e_{\nu})\,F(e_{\rho} \wedge e_{\sigma})$. \emph{Releasing the norm locally} means: $u$ is a positive field on spacetime, varied at fixed $(\hb, \Omega)$, with no three-form and no constraint. Matter obeys hypothesis (Mat) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.promoted-norm-weyl-clock-flat-weight}(v): its action depends on the frame only through the derived metric and not on $u$ or on $\Omega$; so the frame equation is $\mathcal{G}(b) + 3u^{-1}\,b = -8\pi G\,T(b)$ with $u$ the local value, and the equations of $u$ and of $\Omega$ have no matter term. This fixes which frame matter sees as the norm varies: the derived metric of $\hb^{-1}$, with $u$ varied at fixed $(\hb, \Omega)$; every clause on matter below is for this choice. The functional is the bare one, the stored coefficients $c_{3} = c_{5} = 0$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.stelle-west-norm-is-no-local-output}. Write $\tilde\rho = 8\pi G\rho$, $\tilde p = 8\pi G p$ for a perfect fluid at rest in the frame below, $T(e_{0}) = \rho\,e_{0}$, $T(e_{i}) = -p\,e_{i}$.

\emph{The isotropic family.} With $t = e_{0} \cdot x$ and functions $n, s > 0$, $y$ and $u > 0$ of $t$ alone,
\[
\hb^{-1}(e_{0}) = n\,e_{0},\qquad \hb^{-1}(e_{i}) = s\,e_{i},\qquad \Omega(e_{0}) = 0,\qquad \Omega(e_{i}) = y\,e_{i}e_{0}\quad(i = 1, 2, 3),
\]
the homogeneous, isotropic, reflection-invariant gravitational fields with flat slices, torsion allowed ($n$ the lapse, $s$ the scale factor; the derived metric is $n^{2}dt^{2} - s^{2}dx^{2}$). A dot is $d/dt$, and $H = \dot s/(n s)$ is the expansion rate.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Kinematics; proved.)} The torsion is $D_{e_{0}}\hb^{-1}(e_{i}) - D_{e_{i}}\hb^{-1}(e_{0}) = (\dot s - n y)\,e_{i}$ and vanishes on spatial pairs, so the field is torsion-free exactly when $y = \dot s/n$. The curvature operator is diagonal, $\mathcal{R}(e_{0}e_{i}) = \alpha\,e_{0}e_{i}$ and $\mathcal{R}(e_{i}e_{j}) = \beta\,e_{i}e_{j}$ with
\[
\alpha = \frac{\dot y}{n s},\qquad \beta = \frac{y^{2}}{s^{2}},
\]
and $\mathcal{G}(e_{0}) = -3\beta\,e_{0}$, $\mathcal{G}(e_{i}) = -(2\alpha + \beta)\,e_{i}$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The four equations; proved.)} On the family, $u\,\epsilon(F, F) = 24\,L$ with
\[
L = n s^{3} u\,(\alpha - u^{-1})(\beta - u^{-1}) = u\,\dot y\,y^{2} - s^{2}\dot y - n s\,y^{2} + n s^{3}u^{-1},
\]
and the stationary points of the released functional with matter under (Mat) within the family are the solutions of
\[
3\beta = 3u^{-1} + \tilde\rho,\qquad 2\alpha + \beta = 3u^{-1} - \tilde p,\qquad \alpha\beta = u^{-2},\qquad 2s(\dot s - n y) = \dot u\,y^{2},
\]
the two frame equations, the equation of the norm, and the equation of $\Omega$. They are the full field equations on the family: every other component vanishes there by rotation and reflection covariance. The derivative $\dot u$ enters only the last: a varying norm is a source of torsion, and the three other equations are algebraic in $u$ and hold in the same form with torsion present. This, the connection equation and the solved dynamics of (iv) and (v) are what the clause adds to the stored results.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Elimination; proved, a corollary of the stored display.)} The two frame equations give $\alpha\beta - u^{-2} = \tfrac{1}{18}\bigl[3u^{-1}(\tilde\rho - 3\tilde p) - \tilde\rho(\tilde\rho + 3\tilde p)\bigr]$, which is $\tfrac{1}{24}$ of the density $E - \tfrac83\Lambda^{2} = \tfrac43[\Lambda(\tilde\rho - 3\tilde p) - \tilde\rho(\tilde\rho + 3\tilde p)]$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.promoted-norm-weyl-clock-flat-weight}(v) at $\Lambda = 3u^{-1}$. So the equation of the released norm is
\[
\Lambda\,(\tilde\rho - 3\tilde p) = \tilde\rho\,(\tilde\rho + 3\tilde p),\qquad \Lambda = 3u^{-1},
\]
pointwise in time. The identification is definitional: the stored theorem's clause (iii) defines the clock density as the derivative of the Lagrangian in $u$ at fixed frame and connection, and the release sets that derivative to zero. The stored display was computed on torsion-free solutions of constant norm; by (ii) it holds unchanged with the norm varying and the torsion solved.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Dust; proved.)} For $\tilde p = 0$ and $\tilde\rho = m s^{-3}$ with $m > 0$ constant, the solutions are exactly: $\Lambda = 3u^{-1} = \tilde\rho$ at every time; $\beta = \tfrac23\tilde\rho$, $\alpha = \tfrac16\tilde\rho$; $y = -2\dot s/n$ (so the torsion is $3\dot s\,e_{i}$, nonzero); and
\[
H^{2} = \tfrac16\tilde\rho = \tfrac{4\pi G}{3}\rho ,
\]
half the Friedmann value for the matter density alone (a quarter of the value $\tfrac13(\tilde\rho + \Lambda)$ for matter with the tracked term), with either sign of $H$. In proper time $s$ is proportional to the power $\tfrac23$ of the time from the singular point, the deceleration parameter is $\tfrac12$ at every time, and the cosmological term $\Lambda/8\pi G = \rho$ scales as $s^{-3}$: as a fluid it has equation of state $w = 0$, not $-1$. No solution with dust alone accelerates, and none has constant norm.
\item[(v)] \emph{(One barotropic fluid; proved; the value of $\Lambda$ a corollary of the stored display.)} For $\tilde p = w_{m}\tilde\rho$ with $\tilde\rho > 0$ the equation of (iii) gives $\Lambda = \tilde\rho\,(1 + 3w_{m})/(1 - 3w_{m})$ for $w_{m} \neq \tfrac13$, positive only for $-\tfrac13 < w_{m} < \tfrac13$, and has no solution for radiation, $w_{m} = \tfrac13$, where it reads $-2\tilde\rho^{2} = 0$. For $-\tfrac13 < w_{m} < \tfrac13$ and $\tilde\rho = m\,s^{-3(1 + w_{m})}$ the solutions are exactly $y = -2\dot s/\bigl(n(1 + 3w_{m})\bigr)$ with
\[
H^{2} = \frac{(1 + 3w_{m})^{2}}{6\,(1 - 3w_{m})}\,\tilde\rho ,
\]
and the deceleration parameter is $\tfrac12(1 + 3w_{m}) > 0$ at every time: no solution with one such fluid and $u > 0$ accelerates. Mixtures are not treated: the equation of (iii) with the total density and pressure is necessary, and no statement on their acceleration is made.
\item[(vi)] \emph{(Vacuum; proved.)} For $\tilde\rho = \tilde p = 0$ the equations give $\alpha = \beta = u^{-1}$, so $F = 0$, the equation of the norm holds identically, and for every positive function $u(t)$ the field with $y = \pm s\,u^{-1/2}$ and
\[
H = \pm u^{-1/2} + \frac{\dot u}{2 n u}
\]
is a solution. The norm is a free function and the expansion history is not determined; for constant $u$ this is the de Sitter field with every norm of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.stelle-west-norm-is-no-local-output}(iv)(a).
\item[(vii)] \emph{(The promoted norm, for comparison; recalled with one step added.)} Under the promotion of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-henneaux-teitelboim-promotion}, the three-form's equation is $d\lambda = 0$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.promoted-norm-one-global-pair}(ii)); under (Mat) the three-form term contains neither the frame nor matter, so the frame equation is that of the Setting with $3u^{-1}$ a constant $\Lambda$, whose term is the stress-energy $(\Lambda/8\pi G)\,b$ of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-condition}(i) with $p = -\rho$: $w = -1$ on every solution, the value of $\Lambda$ differing between solutions and not within one. The same holds if a function $g(\lambda)$ with $g' \neq 0$ is promoted, the equation being $g'(\lambda)\,d\lambda = 0$.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading (argued).} A text search of the store, not an audit of a cone, finds two ways of making the norm a variable. The promotion keeps $w = -1$ exactly by (vii); that the promoted norm supplies no scale-dependent source is Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-phase-spectrum-not-red}(iv), cited and not restated. The local release, the one in which the cosmological term can change in time, gives under (Mat), for the bare functional and on the isotropic family, no evolution of the kind the surveys test: with dust, or one barotropic fluid with $-\tfrac13 < w_{m} < \tfrac13$, the cosmological term is a fixed multiple of the matter density and the expansion decelerates; with radiation there is no solution; in vacuum nothing is predicted. Together with the exclusion of the Schwarzschild-de Sitter field (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.stelle-west-norm-is-no-local-output}(iv)), the local release is not a fallback for the prediction $w = -1$. The conclusions for matter hold for matter on the derived metric of $\hb^{-1}$ with $u$ varied at fixed $(\hb, \Omega)$; with matter on the frame $u^{-1/2}\hb^{-1}$ of the stored release the equation of the norm is the vanishing of the density $\epsilon(F, F)$ itself and the clauses on matter are not derived. The same search finds one stored structure with a late-time equation of state different from $-1$: the unadopted branch of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.unit-ball-clauses-hold-at-one-epoch-unless-hidden-direction-co-expands}(ii) with a static hidden direction, a dark-matter component with effective $w = -\tfrac14$ read from a dilution exponent (no pressure derived there); it is not a variable norm and is not treated here. Actions with derivative terms of the Stelle-West vector are not treated. The result is known for the minimal varying-$\Lambda$ theory in the literature named in the extraction note; what is added is its form in the store's setting and its identification with the stored clock density. Transport-absent.
synthesis.norm-released-locally-on-isotr.technical: The prediction $w = -1$ would be refuted by a confirmed evolution of the dark-energy density, so it matters whether any stored structure allows one. Of the two ways the store holds of making the norm a variable (a search of the store, not a proof that there are no others), the promoted norm does not: its multiplier is constant by its own equation, and under hypothesis (Mat) the frame equation is Einstein's with that constant. The other releases the norm $u = 3/\Lambda$ of the bare functional as a local field with no three-form, a construction known in the literature as the minimal varying-$\Lambda$ theory. On homogeneous, isotropic, reflection-invariant gravitational fields with flat slices, $\hb^{-1}(e_{0}) = n e_{0}$, $\hb^{-1}(e_{i}) = s e_{i}$, $\Omega(e_{i}) = y\,e_{i}e_{0}$, the functional reduces to $24k\,n s^{3}u(\alpha - 1/u)(\beta - 1/u)$ with $\alpha = \dot y/(ns)$ and $\beta = y^{2}/s^{2}$ the two curvature eigenvalues, and under (Mat) the field equations are $3\beta = 3/u + \tilde\rho$, $2\alpha + \beta = 3/u - \tilde p$, $\alpha\beta = 1/u^{2}$ and $2s(\dot s - ny) = \dot u\,y^{2}$. The rate of change of the norm enters only the last, where it sources torsion. Eliminating gives $\Lambda(\tilde\rho - 3\tilde p) = \tilde\rho(\tilde\rho + 3\tilde p)$, the stored clock density of the promoted norm set to zero. Under (Mat), with matter on the derived metric of $\hb^{-1}$, dust forces $\Lambda = 8\pi G\rho$ at all times with $H^{2} = \tfrac{4\pi G}{3}\rho$ and deceleration parameter $\tfrac12$; one barotropic fluid with $-\tfrac13 < w_{m} < \tfrac13$ has deceleration parameter $\tfrac12(1 + 3w_{m}) > 0$; radiation has no solution; in vacuum $u(t)$ is free and $H = \pm u^{-1/2} + \dot u/(2nu)$. So under (Mat), on this family and for one such fluid, the release gives no accelerating solution, and no prediction without matter; mixtures are not treated.
synthesis.norm-released-locally-on-isotr.lay: The framework predicts that dark energy never changes. If measurements showed it changing, could the framework bend? Its equations contain one quantity, a fixed length, that sets the strength of dark energy. The collection holds two ways of letting that length vary (found by a search of the collection, not a proof that there are no others). In one, the length becomes a quantity the equations hold constant, and dark energy still never changes. In the other, the length is allowed to vary freely from place to place and moment to moment. This result works out what that second way does, for the simplest form of the action, to a smooth, uniform, spatially flat universe, assuming matter responds to gravity in the ordinary way. The outcome was already known in the research literature for an equivalent theory; here it is derived in the framework's own language. With ordinary matter alone present, the dark energy is forced to equal the density of matter at every moment, so the expansion always slows down and never speeds up, contrary to what is observed; the same slowing holds for any single simple fluid the equations admit, and mixtures of several kinds of matter were not worked out. With only radiation present, the equations have no solution. With nothing present, the equations allow any expansion history at all, so they predict nothing. Under that assumption about matter, and for flat uniform universes of this kind filled with one kind of matter, freeing the length in the simplest form of the action does not give the framework a way to accommodate changing dark energy.

proofs.main:
All statements are in Gauge Theory Gravity: the gravitational field is the pair $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime, the products are those of $\Cl(1,3)$ with $e_{0}^{2} = 1$, $e_{i}^{2} = -1$, and $A \times B = \tfrac12(AB - BA)$.

\emph{(i)} Since the fields depend on $t$ alone and $\Omega(e_{0}) = 0$, the field strength of the Definition is $R(e_{0} \wedge e_{i}) = \partial_{t}\Omega(e_{i}) = \dot y\,e_{i}e_{0}$ and $R(e_{i} \wedge e_{j}) = \Omega(e_{i}) \times \Omega(e_{j}) = y^{2}\,(e_{i}e_{0}) \times (e_{j}e_{0}) = -y^{2}\,e_{i}e_{j}$ for $i \neq j$, because $(e_{i}e_{0})(e_{j}e_{0}) = -e_{i}e_{j}e_{0}^{2} = -e_{i}e_{j}$. The curvature operator is $\mathcal{R}(B) = -R(\hb(B))$; the physical bivectors $e_{0}e_{i}$ and $e_{i}e_{j}$ lie over the background bivectors $(ns)^{-1}e_{0} \wedge e_{i}$ and $s^{-2}e_{i} \wedge e_{j}$, so $\mathcal{R}(e_{0}e_{i}) = -(ns)^{-1}\dot y\,e_{i}e_{0} = \alpha\,e_{0}e_{i}$ and $\mathcal{R}(e_{i}e_{j}) = s^{-2}y^{2}\,e_{i}e_{j} = \beta\,e_{i}e_{j}$. Contracting with the reciprocal frame, $\mathcal{R}(e_{0}) = 3\alpha\,e_{0}$, $\mathcal{R}(e_{i}) = (\alpha + 2\beta)\,e_{i}$, the scalar is $6\alpha + 6\beta$, and $\mathcal{G}(b) = \mathcal{R}(b) - \tfrac12 b\,\mathcal{R}$ gives the two values stated. For the torsion, $D_{b}v = b \cdot \nabla v + \Omega(b) \times v$ on vectors: $D_{e_{0}}(s\,e_{i}) - D_{e_{i}}(n\,e_{0}) = \dot s\,e_{i} - n y\,(e_{i}e_{0}) \times e_{0} = (\dot s - n y)\,e_{i}$, since $(e_{i}e_{0}) \times e_{0} = e_{i}$; on spatial pairs $(e_{i}e_{0}) \times e_{j} = 0$ for $i \neq j$. The check computes $R$, the torsion, the eigenvalues and the Einstein map (contracted with the reciprocal frame) with the algebra's products at four sample jets $(n, s, y, \dot y, u)$ and three rates $(\dot s, \dot u)$.

\emph{(ii), the density.} The density is that of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west} in the frozen-point form of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}, with $\ell^{2} = u$. $F$ is diagonal with $F(e_{0} \wedge e_{i}) = -ns(\alpha - u^{-1})\,e_{0}e_{i}$ and $F(e_{i} \wedge e_{j}) = -s^{2}(\beta - u^{-1})\,e_{i}e_{j}$. The coefficient of $e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}$ in a product of two basis bivectors is nonzero only for complementary planes, and each of the $24$ orderings pairs a plane $e_{0}e_{i}$ with its complement; every ordering contributes $n s^{3}(\alpha - u^{-1})(\beta - u^{-1})$ with the sign of the ordering cancelling the sign of the pseudoscalar coefficient, so $u\,\epsilon(F, F) = 24\,n s^{3}u(\alpha - u^{-1})(\beta - u^{-1})$. Expanding with $\alpha = \dot y/(ns)$, $\beta = y^{2}/s^{2}$ gives the second form of $L$. The density is a polynomial of degree at most one in each of $\dot y$, $n$, $u$ and $u^{-1}$ jointly as displayed, and the check confirms the factor $24$ and the expansion by the algebra's products at four jets, and that the Lorentz block vanishes on the de Sitter values.

\emph{(ii), the reduction.} Let $G$ be the group generated by the rotations of the background about the $e_{0}$ axis, each combined with the same rotor acting as a rotation gauge transformation, by one reflection $e_{1} \mapsto -e_{1}$ combined in the same way, and by the spatial translations. The functional (the density is a scalar density built from $\epsilon$ and is unchanged when the orientation of the background and that of the frame are reversed together) and the matter action are invariant under $G$, and the family, with matter at rest, is fixed by $G$ pointwise in field space. The Euler-Lagrange expression of each field is then a $G$-covariant object evaluated at a $G$-fixed configuration, hence $G$-invariant. For the frame, the expression is a linear map of vectors commuting with the rotations and the reflection: it is a multiple of the identity on the span of the $e_{i}$ and maps $e_{0}$ to a multiple of $e_{0}$, two components. For $\Omega$, the expression is a linear map from vectors to bivectors: on $e_{0}$ it would be an invariant bivector, which is zero (an invariant boost bivector $e_{i}e_{0}$ would give an invariant vector; an invariant spatial bivector does not exist); on the $e_{i}$ it is a combination of $e_{i} \mapsto e_{i}e_{0}$ and of $e_{i} \mapsto e_{j}e_{k}$ ($ijk$ cyclic), and the second is odd under the reflection, so one component remains. The remaining components are the derivatives of the reduced functional along $n$, $s$ and $y$, because a variation within the family is a variation of the full fields. The equation of $u$ is pointwise and has no derivative of $u$, since $u$ enters the density algebraically. So the full equations on the family are the four Euler-Lagrange equations of $24k\,L$ plus matter.

\emph{(ii), the equations.} From the second form of $L$: $\partial L/\partial u = \dot y\,y^{2} - n s^{3}u^{-2} = n s^{3}(\alpha\beta - u^{-2})$; $\partial L/\partial n = -s\,y^{2} + s^{3}u^{-1} = s^{3}(u^{-1} - \beta)$; $\partial L/\partial s = -2s\dot y - n y^{2} + 3n s^{2}u^{-1} = n s^{2}(3u^{-1} - 2\alpha - \beta)$; and, with $\partial L/\partial\dot y = u\,y^{2} - s^{2}$,
\[
\frac{\partial L}{\partial y} - \frac{d}{dt}\frac{\partial L}{\partial\dot y} = 2u\,\dot y\,y - 2n s\,y - \dot u\,y^{2} - 2u\,y\,\dot y + 2s\dot s = 2s(\dot s - n y) - \dot u\,y^{2}.
\]
In vacuum the $n$ and $s$ equations are $-3\beta + 3u^{-1} = 0$ and $-(2\alpha + \beta) + 3u^{-1} = 0$, the components of $\mathcal{G}(b) + 3u^{-1}b = 0$ on $e_{0}$ and $e_{i}$ by (i), in agreement with the frame equation of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west} at $\Lambda = 3u^{-1}$. Under (Mat) the matter action does not contain $u$ or $\Omega$ and its frame derivative is the stress-energy of the Definition's field equation, $\mathcal{G}(b) + 3u^{-1}b = -8\pi G\,T(b)$; with $T(e_{0}) = \rho\,e_{0}$, $T(e_{i}) = -p\,e_{i}$ this is $3\beta = 3u^{-1} + \tilde\rho$ and $2\alpha + \beta = 3u^{-1} - \tilde p$. The $u$ and $y$ equations are unchanged. As a second derivation of the last equation: in the forms of the Fact the $\Omega$-equation of $k\,u\,\epsilon_{abcd}F^{ab} \wedge F^{cd}$ is $\epsilon_{abcd}\bigl(du \wedge R^{cd} - 2\,T^{c} \wedge e^{d}\bigr) = 0$ (the two terms in $u^{-1}du \wedge e^{c} \wedge e^{d}$ cancel), whose one nonzero component on the family is $\dot u\,\beta = 2(\dot s - n y)/s$ in units $n = 1$, the same equation. The check differentiates $L$ exactly with dual numbers over the rationals at four jets and three rates and compares with the four displayed expressions.

\emph{(iii)} From the frame equations $\beta = u^{-1} + \tfrac13\tilde\rho$ and $\alpha = u^{-1} - \tfrac16(\tilde\rho + 3\tilde p)$, so $\alpha\beta - u^{-2} = u^{-1}\bigl(\tfrac13\tilde\rho - \tfrac16(\tilde\rho + 3\tilde p)\bigr) - \tfrac1{18}\tilde\rho(\tilde\rho + 3\tilde p) = \tfrac1{18}\bigl[3u^{-1}(\tilde\rho - 3\tilde p) - \tilde\rho(\tilde\rho + 3\tilde p)\bigr]$; with $\Lambda = 3u^{-1}$ this is $\tfrac{1}{24}\cdot\tfrac43[\Lambda(\tilde\rho - 3\tilde p) - \tilde\rho(\tilde\rho + 3\tilde p)]$, the display of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.promoted-norm-weyl-clock-flat-weight}(v). The identity is polynomial of degree two in $(u^{-1}, \tilde\rho, \tilde p)$ and is checked at sixteen points. That the released norm's equation is that density set to zero is definitional (clause (iii) of that theorem defines the density as $\partial L/\partial u$ at fixed frame and connection); the content is that by (ii) the frame equations have the same algebraic form with torsion and a varying norm. The check tests this where it can fail: at four jets with nonzero torsion it reads $\tilde\rho$ and $\tilde p$ off the frame equation with the Einstein map contracted in the algebra, and confirms that the derivative of the density in $u$ is $n s^{3}/24$ times the stored polynomial, while the torsion-free spatial eigenvalue of the same metric gives a different density.

\emph{(iv)} With $\tilde p = 0$ and $\tilde\rho > 0$ the equation of (iii) is $\tilde\rho\,(3u^{-1} - \tilde\rho) = 0$, so $3u^{-1} = \tilde\rho$, and then $\beta = \tfrac23\tilde\rho$, $\alpha = \tfrac16\tilde\rho$. With $\tilde\rho = m s^{-3}$ and $c^{2} = \tfrac23 m$, $\beta = y^{2}/s^{2}$ gives $y = \varepsilon\,c\,s^{-1/2}$ with $\varepsilon = \pm1$ (constant by continuity, $y \neq 0$), so $\dot y = -\tfrac12\varepsilon\,c\,s^{-3/2}\dot s$, and $\alpha = \dot y/(ns) = \tfrac16 m s^{-3}$ gives $\dot s/n = -\varepsilon\,\tfrac{m}{3c}\,s^{-1/2} = -\tfrac12\varepsilon\,c\,s^{-1/2} = -\tfrac12 y$, using $m/(3c) = c/2$. Hence $y = -2\dot s/n$, $H^{2} = y^{2}/(4s^{2}) = \tfrac14\beta = \tfrac16\tilde\rho$, and the torsion coefficient is $\dot s - n y = 3\dot s$. The fourth equation then holds identically: $u = 3s^{3}/m$ gives $\dot u\,y^{2} = (9 s^{2}\dot s/m)(c^{2}/s) = 6 s\,\dot s$, and $2s(\dot s - n y) = 6 s\,\dot s$. In proper time $\tau$ ($d\tau = n\,dt$), $ds/d\tau = \pm\tfrac12 c\,s^{-1/2}$, so $s^{3/2}$ is linear in $\tau$, $d^{2}s/d\tau^{2} = -\tfrac18 c^{2}s^{-2}$ and the deceleration parameter $-s\,(d^{2}s/d\tau^{2})/(ds/d\tau)^{2}$ is $\tfrac12$. The cosmological term $\Lambda/8\pi G = \rho$ is proportional to $s^{-3}$, the scaling of a fluid with $w = 0$. Since these are all the solutions, none accelerates and none has $\dot u = 0$. The check evaluates the closed form and its derivatives at three rational points of the curve (where $s$ is a square), confirms all four equations, the rate, the deceleration parameter, and that the torsion-free connection, a rescaled norm and the Friedmann rate fail.

\emph{(v)} Substitute $\tilde p = w_{m}\tilde\rho$ in (iii): $\Lambda(1 - 3w_{m}) = \tilde\rho(1 + 3w_{m})$. At $w_{m} = \tfrac13$ the left side vanishes and the right side is $2\tilde\rho \neq 0$. For $-\tfrac13 < w_{m} < \tfrac13$ write $\kappa = 1 + 3w_{m} > 0$ and $\nu = 1 - 3w_{m} > 0$. Then $u^{-1} = \tfrac13\tilde\rho\,\kappa/\nu$, $\beta = u^{-1} + \tfrac13\tilde\rho = \tfrac{2}{3\nu}\tilde\rho$ and $\alpha = u^{-1} - \tfrac16\kappa\tilde\rho = \tfrac{\kappa^{2}}{6\nu}\tilde\rho$. With $\tilde\rho = m\,s^{-3(1 + w_{m})}$ (conservation of the fluid on the derived metric, which (Mat) gives) and $c^{2} = 2m/(3\nu)$, $y = \varepsilon\,c\,s^{-\kappa/2}$, so $\dot y = -\tfrac12\kappa\,(\dot s/s)\,y$ and $\alpha = \dot y/(ns) = -\tfrac12\kappa\,H\,y/s$; with $\alpha = \tfrac14\kappa^{2}\beta = \tfrac14\kappa^{2}y^{2}/s^{2}$ this is $H = -\tfrac12\kappa\,y/s$, that is $y = -2\dot s/(n\kappa)$ and $H^{2} = \tfrac14\kappa^{2}\beta = \kappa^{2}\tilde\rho/(6\nu)$. The fourth equation holds identically: $\dot u = 3(1 + w_{m})\,(\dot s/s)\,u$ and $u\,y^{2} = s^{2}\beta u = 2s^{2}/\kappa$ give $\dot u\,y^{2} = 6(1 + w_{m})\,s\dot s/\kappa$, and $2s(\dot s - ny) = 2s\dot s\,(1 + 2/\kappa) = 6(1 + w_{m})\,s\dot s/\kappa$. In proper time $ds/d\tau$ is proportional to $s^{-\kappa/2}$, so $d^{2}s/d\tau^{2} = -\tfrac12\kappa\,(ds/d\tau)^{2}/s$ and the deceleration parameter is $\tfrac12\kappa$. Dust is $\kappa = \nu = 1$. The frame and norm equations are necessary for any matter content of the family; nothing further is claimed for mixtures. The check confirms the four equations, the rate, the connection coefficient and the deceleration parameter on the closed form at four equations of state, three amplitudes and two lapses.

\emph{(vi)} With $\tilde\rho = \tilde p = 0$ the frame equations give $\beta = u^{-1}$ and $\alpha = u^{-1}$, so $F = 0$ and $\alpha\beta = u^{-2}$ holds. Then $y = \pm s\,u^{-1/2}$, and $\alpha = \dot y/(ns) = u^{-1}$ reads $\pm\bigl(\dot s\,u^{-1/2} - \tfrac12 s\,\dot u\,u^{-3/2}\bigr) = n s\,u^{-1}$, that is $H = \pm u^{-1/2} + \dot u/(2nu)$; the fourth equation, $2s(\dot s - n y) = \dot u\,s^{2}u^{-1}$, is the same relation. For any positive $u(t)$ this is a first-order linear equation for $s$, which has solutions. The check confirms the four equations and $F = 0$ at four samples with arbitrary $\dot u$.

\emph{(vii)} The promotion is that of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-henneaux-teitelboim-promotion}. The equation $d\lambda = 0$ is Theorem \claimref{synthesis.promoted-norm-one-global-pair}(ii). The added term $c\int\lambda\,dT$ contains neither $\hb$ nor matter fields, and under (Mat) matter does not contain $\lambda$ or $T$, so the frame equation is that of the Setting with $3u^{-1} = \Lambda$ constant; its term $\Lambda\,b$, moved to the matter side of $\mathcal{G}(b) = -8\pi G\,(T(b) + T^{\Lambda}(b))$, is the stress-energy $T^{\Lambda}(b) = (\Lambda/8\pi G)\,b$ of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-condition}(i), with $p = -\rho$. For a promoted function $g(\lambda)$ the variation of $T$ gives $d\,g(\lambda) = g'(\lambda)\,d\lambda = 0$.

\emph{Reading.} The reading collects (iv) to (vii) with Theorem \claimref{synthesis.stelle-west-norm-is-no-local-output}(iv). It is argued, not a theorem: it concerns the bare functional under (Mat) on the isotropic family, and in vacuum the stored release (the Stelle-West vector varied at fixed ambient connection) has the same stationary points as the release at fixed $(\hb, \Omega)$ used here, the two differing by the pointwise change of variable $\hb^{-1} \mapsto u^{-1/2}\hb^{-1}$; with matter, (Mat) names $\hb^{-1}$ as the frame matter sees; with matter on $u^{-1/2}\hb^{-1}$ instead, the Lagrangian is $u$ times a function free of $u$ and the equation of the norm is the vanishing of $\epsilon(F, F)$, for which the clauses on matter are not derived here. That the promoted norm supplies no scale-dependent source is Theorem \claimref{synthesis.frozen-phase-spectrum-not-red}(iv). The count of stored ways of making the norm a variable is a text search; it also finds the branch of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.unit-ball-clauses-hold-at-one-epoch-unless-hidden-direction-co-expands}(ii) with a static hidden direction, an effective $w = -\tfrac14$ for a dark-matter component, which is not a variable norm.

synthesis.number-n-free-at-fixed-d-term-.formal:
Take the setting of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.d-term-level-free-at-fixed-n}: the D-term action of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus} on the null-lift locus $L_{H} = \{Q(c) = -H^{2}\}$, $H^{2} = \Lambda/3 = Q(I_{\Lambda})$ for the frozen point $I_{\Lambda}$, with the added invariant $\kappa\mathsf{N}^{2}$, $\kappa \ge 0$; the lift family $c_{\lambda}$ with $\mathsf{N}(\lambda) = \tfrac12(H^{4}/\lambda^{2} + \lambda^{2})$ and $m(\lambda) = \tfrac12(H^{4}/\lambda^{2} - \lambda^{2})$; the level $\xi$; Newton's constant $G = M_{P}^{-2}$ and $N = M_{P}/H$. Fix $G$, the couplings $g$, $g'$, $\kappa$ and a level $\xi > 0$, and put $m^{*} = g'^{2}\xi/(g^{2} + g'^{2} + 8\kappa)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(A vacuum at the same level for every $N$; a corollary of the stored results.)} For every $H > 0$ the frame $\lambda_{H}$ with $\lambda_{H}^{2} = \sqrt{m^{*2} + H^{4}} - m^{*}$ satisfies $0 < \lambda_{H} < H$, $m(\lambda_{H}) = m^{*}$ and $\mathsf{N}(\lambda_{H}) = \sqrt{m^{*2} + H^{4}}$, and by part (i) of that theorem $c_{\lambda_{H}}$ is a charge-preserving critical point of the potential on $L_{H}$ at the level $\xi$, with every tree mass squared a positive multiple of $\mathsf{N}$ that depends on $g$, $g'$, $\kappa$ only. So every pair $(N, \xi G)$ of positive numbers is realised by a model with the given couplings, and the ratios of tree masses are the same in all of them.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Two exact models.)} With $G = 1008^{-2}$, $g = \tfrac23$, $g' = \tfrac12$, $\kappa = \tfrac15$ and $\xi = \tfrac{171808}{9}$, so $m^{*} = 2080$: the model $A$ with $H = 48$, $\lambda = 32$ and the model $B$ with $H = 63$, $\lambda = 49$ have $N = 21$ and $N = 16$, $\mathsf{N} = 3104$ and $4481$, the same ratios $M_{W}^{2}/M_{Z}^{2} = \tfrac{16}{25}$, $m_{h}^{2}/M_{Z}^{2} = \tfrac{413}{125}$, $m_{\pm}^{2}/M_{Z}^{2} = \tfrac{368}{125}$, and different $(v/M_{P})^{2} = 2G\mathsf{N}$, with $\mathsf{N}_{B}^{2} - \mathsf{N}_{A}^{2} = H_{B}^{4} - H_{A}^{4}$. At $N = 10^{61}$ against $2 \times 10^{61}$ with $v/M_{P} = 2 \times 10^{-17}$ the relative change of $(v/M_{P})^{4}$ is below $10^{-176}$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The stored relations containing $N$ that the search found hold in every model of (i); that there are no others is argued, on a pattern search.)} $G\Lambda = 3N^{-2}$, $(H/M_{P})^{2} = N^{-2}$ and, for each tree mass $\mu$, the Casimir value $(\mu/M_{P})^{2}N^{2} = \mu^{2}/H^{2}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.smallness-monomials-exact-hierarchy-casimir}) are identities in $N$; the horizon entropy $\pi N^{2}$ and the mode count $4\pi\kappa_{c}N^{2}$ (Theorems \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-entropy-pi-n-squared}, \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-mode-count}) are functions of $N$ that no stored relation fixes by another route (the Euler term's shift of the horizon entropy under Wald entropy, $-\pi N^{2}$, is a second stored expression and again an identity in $N$; the count is a density times an area, and no stored statement asserts that it is an integer; were integrality imposed, $N^{2}$ would be confined to a discrete set and still not fixed); $Gv^{2}N^{2} = (v/H)^{2}$ is an identity and $\mathsf{N}^{2} = m^{*2} + H^{4}$ is the stored dependence of the weak scale on $H$ at fixed level (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.constant-d-term-level-fixes-weak-scale-against-planck-under-promotion}); the discrete invariants of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number}(1) do not contain $I_{\Lambda}$. Under the Henneaux-Teitelboim promotion the models of (i) with one $\xi G$ are solutions of one theory, $N$ being constant on each and taking every positive value (Theorems \claimref{synthesis.promoted-norm-one-global-pair}, \claimref{synthesis.einstein-route-makes-n-initial-data}); under the action as written they are the members of the family of theories indexed by $\Lambda$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws}).
\item[(iv)] \emph{(A remark on scale-free functions of the frozen point.)} Let $(V, Q)$ be the ambient real quadratic space and $\Phi$ a function on $\{I \in V : Q(I) > 0\}$ with $\Phi(\gamma I) = \Phi(I)$ for every isometry $\gamma$ of $(V, Q)$ and $\Phi(sI) = \Phi(I)$ for every $s > 0$. Then $\Phi$ is constant. At fixed $M_{P}$, $N = M_{P}/\sqrt{Q(I)}$ is invariant under isometries and homogeneous of degree $-1$, so it takes every positive value and is not a function of such $\Phi$; that much is the proved clause of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number}(1) and clause (ii) of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws}, and what is added here is only that $\Phi$ is constant. Under the reading of "a construction from the conformal class and the pair structure alone" as a construction of this kind, a function of the frozen point alone, invariant under all isometries and under rescaling, the observation-level reading in that theorem is immediate; a construction that uses other fixed data (the null pairs, a chart) is not of this kind, and the stored reading in its general wording is not upgraded. The clause covers only constructions that do not contain $G$: it says nothing about a relation between $Q(I)$ and the Planck scale, which is the business of (i) to (iii). The change of $N$ in (i) is a change of the datum $\Lambda$ at fixed $G$ and is not a symmetry: a dilation acting on every scale ($G \to G/s^{2}$, $H \to sH$, $m^{*} \to s^{2}m^{*}$) fixes $N$ and $\xi G$.
\end{enumerate}
The models use the branch $W = \kappa\mathsf{N}^{2}$, whose charged pair the record excludes, as in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.d-term-level-free-at-fixed-n}: they are models of the premise set and the stored relations at their pinned versions, not of the record. What is held fixed is $\xi G$, not $v/M_{P}$, which depends on $N$ through $\mathsf{N}^{2} = m^{*2} + H^{4}$. What is proved is (i), (ii), the listed identities of (iii) and (iv). The headline is argued, on a pattern search: given the stored relations found by the search described in the extraction note, none fixes $N$ at fixed $\xi G$, and with that theorem the two registered inputs are jointly free in these models; a derivation of $N$ would have to supply a relation, not an identity, between $Q(I_{\Lambda})$ in Planck units and numbers the premises fix, and the search found none.
synthesis.number-n-free-at-fixed-d-term-.technical:
Given the stored rung-field action on the null-lift locus with the second invariant $\kappa\mathsf{N}^{2}$, a fixed D-term level in Planck units and fixed couplings, there is a stable vacuum for every value of the cosmological constant, at the frame where the hypercharge moment equals the level's value; so the number $N = M_{P}/H$ can be moved freely while the level, the couplings and every ratio of tree masses stay put. Two exact models, with $N = 21$ and $N = 16$, are exhibited. The stored relations that contain $N$ are either identities in $N$, definitions of quantities that scale with $N$ (the horizon entropy and mode count), or the stored weak dependence of the weak scale on $H$ at fixed level, and each holds in both models. Under the promoted action the models are solutions of one theory; under the action as written they are members of the family of theories indexed by $\Lambda$.

Clause (iv) is a remark: under a narrow definition (a function of the frozen point alone) the observation-level reading of the trichotomy result, that no kinematic construction can fix $N$, is immediate; the stored reading in its general wording is not upgraded. A function of the frozen point that is invariant under the isometries of the ambient form and under positive rescaling is constant on frozen points of positive norm, because two reflections and a rescaling carry any one to any other, while $N$ has degree $-1$. That "no other stored relation contains $N$" is argued from a pattern search of the whole store and the joint past cone of the results that mention $N$ (519 entities, 40 postulates), not from a formal audit of every derivation. The models are not models of the record: the simple second invariant has a charged pair that collider data exclude.
synthesis.number-n-free-at-fixed-d-term-.lay: The theory has one enormous number it does not explain, the ratio of the Planck mass to the scale set by the cosmological constant, and records it as an input. This result checks that nothing the theory has stored secretly fixes it. Assuming the theory's stored equations for its Higgs-like field, it builds two exact versions of the theory that agree in the strength of gravity, in every coupling and in the constant that sets the weak scale, and differ only in the cosmological constant; both satisfy every stored formula found by the search in which the big number appears, and in both every particle mass ratio is the same. These are toy models, not our universe: the big number is 21 in one and 16 in the other, and the simple potential used has a charged particle pair that collider data exclude. Under a narrow definition of a construction that uses only the shape of the theory's basic geometric data (a function of the frozen point alone, unchanged by all isometries and by rescaling) the stored reading that such a construction cannot produce the number becomes immediate; the stored reading in its general wording is not upgraded. So, as an argued conclusion given what the search found, the big number is a free input, independently of the weak scale's own free input. The search for stored formulas was done by pattern and reading, which is why that part is labelled as argued.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i).} With $x = \lambda^{2}$, $m(\lambda) = m^{*}$ reads $x^{2} + 2m^{*}x - H^{4} = 0$, whose positive root is $x = \sqrt{m^{*2} + H^{4}} - m^{*}$; $x < H^{2}$ because $\sqrt{m^{*2} + H^{4}} < m^{*} + H^{2}$ for $m^{*} > 0$, so $0 < \lambda_{H} < H$ and in particular $\lambda_{H} \neq H$. On the family $\mathsf{N}^{2} - m^{2} = H^{4}$, so $\mathsf{N}(\lambda_{H}) = \sqrt{m^{*2} + H^{4}}$. Theorem \claimref{synthesis.d-term-level-free-at-fixed-n}(i) states that for every $\lambda > 0$, $\lambda \neq H$, the level $m(\lambda)(g^{2} + g'^{2} + 8\kappa)/g'^{2}$ makes $c_{\lambda}$ a charge-preserving critical point on the locus, with $M_{W}^{2} = \tfrac12 g^{2}\mathsf{N}$, $M_{Z}^{2} = \tfrac12(g^{2} + g'^{2})\mathsf{N}$, $m_{h}^{2} = M_{Z}^{2} + 4\kappa\mathsf{N}$, $m_{\pm}^{2} = M_{W}^{2} + 4\kappa\mathsf{N}$; at $\lambda = \lambda_{H}$ that level is $\xi$ by the definition of $m^{*}$. Given $N > 0$ put $H = M_{P}/N$. The script recomputes criticality along the family for both models: with the stored boundary form $V_{D} = \tfrac12\bigl(\tfrac14 g^{2}m^{2} + g'^{2}(\tfrac{m}{2} - \zeta)^{2}\bigr)$, $\xi = 2\zeta$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus}), the derivative of $V_{D} + \kappa\mathsf{N}^{2}$ in $\lambda$ is $m'(\lambda)\bigl(\tfrac14(g^{2} + g'^{2} + 8\kappa)m - \tfrac12 g'^{2}\zeta\bigr)$, using $\mathsf{N}\mathsf{N}' = mm'$, zero exactly at $m = m^{*}$, and the second derivative is positive there.

\emph{(ii).} $(72, 32)$ and $(81, 49)$ are two pairs $(H^{2}/\lambda, \lambda)$ with the same difference of squares $4160 = 2m$; their products are $48^{2}$ and $63^{2}$. Then $\xi = 2080 \cdot \tfrac{413}{45} \cdot 4 \cdot \tfrac14$, that is $2080(g^{2} + g'^{2} + 8\kappa)/g'^{2} = \tfrac{171808}{9}$, $N^{2} = 1/(GH^{2}) = 441$ and $256$, and $\mathsf{N} = 3104$, $4481$. The mass ratios follow from (i). For the realistic sizes, in Planck units $m^{*} = 2 \times 10^{-34}$ and $H^{4} = N^{-4}$: $\mathsf{N}^{2}$ changes by $10^{-244}(1 - \tfrac{1}{16})$, a relative change of $(v/M_{P})^{4} = 4G^{2}\mathsf{N}^{2}$ of about $2.3 \times 10^{-177}$.

\emph{(iii).} The relations are those of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.smallness-monomials-exact-hierarchy-casimir} (the monomials and the Casimir value), Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-entropy-pi-n-squared} (the entropy) and Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-mode-count} (the count). Each line is a substitution, computed in both models: $G\Lambda = 3GH^{2} = 3N^{-2}$; $A_{\Lambda} = 4\pi/H^{2}$ so $A_{\Lambda}/4G = \pi N^{2}$, and the count is $\kappa_{c}A_{\Lambda}/G$; $\mu^{2}/H^{2} = (\mu^{2}G)N^{2}$; $Gv^{2}N^{2} = v^{2}/H^{2}$. The entropy and the count are defined from $N$; the stored results give them no expression in terms of numbers that the premises fix (the residue $\kappa_{c}$ is a density per Planck area, and the area is $4\pi N^{2}$); the one second expression the search found, the Euler term's shift $-3\pi\chi/(2\Lambda G) = -\pi N^{2}$ at $\chi = 2$ under Wald entropy, is again an identity in $N$ (computed). These lines are identities and hold for any $H$; the line that could fail is the stored weak-scale relation at fixed level, $(v/M_{P})^{4} = 4G^{2}(m^{*2} + H^{4}) = 4c^{2}(\xi G)^{2} + 4N^{-4}$ with $c = g'^{2}/(g^{2} + g'^{2} + 8\kappa)$, which the script checks from each model's own frame and couplings. That the promoted solution space contains every positive $\Lambda$ with the level a constant of the action is Theorem \claimref{synthesis.promoted-norm-one-global-pair} with Theorem \claimref{synthesis.constant-d-term-level-fixes-weak-scale-against-planck-under-promotion}; the Clausius route gives the same solution space (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-route-makes-n-initial-data}); the family of theories is Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws}. The frozen point of each model is the chart vector $I_{\Lambda} = n_{\infty} + (\Lambda/6)n_{0}$ of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-frozen-point-dictionary}, with $Q(I_{\Lambda}) = H^{2}$ (computed).

\emph{(iv).} Let $I, I'$ have positive norm and put $s = \sqrt{Q(I')/Q(I)}$, so that $a = sI$ and $b = I'$ have the same nonzero norm. Since $Q(a - b) + Q(a + b) = 4Q(a) \neq 0$, one of $a - b$, $a + b$ is not null. If $Q(a - b) \neq 0$, the reflection in $a - b$ is an isometry carrying $a$ to $b$. Otherwise the reflection in $a + b$ carries $a$ to $-b$ and the reflection in $b$ carries $-b$ to $b$. So $\Phi(I') = \Phi(sI) = \Phi(I)$. That $N$ is not a function of such $\Phi$ needs no isometry: $\Phi(sI) = \Phi(I)$ and $N(sI) = N(I)/s$, the proved clause of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number}(1), recorded against the stored definition of kinematic in Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws}(ii); the two reflections add only the constancy of $\Phi$. $Q(\gamma I) = Q(I)$ and $Q(sI) = s^{2}Q(I)$ give the statement on $N$. The discrete invariants listed in Theorem \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number}(1) are constants and so of this kind. The script exhibits the isometry for the two models as a versor of $\Cl(2,4)$: $U = (37e_{+} - 5e_{-})e_{+}$ fixes the spacetime vectors and carries $I_{\Lambda_{A}}$ to $\tfrac{16}{21}I_{\Lambda_{B}}$, and likewise for two further pairs of norms.

\emph{The conclusion.} The models of (i) satisfy the stored relations of (iii) for every $N$; the search described in the extraction note (lists in the file it names) found no stored relation containing $N$ outside those, which is an argument and not an audit of every derivation, the conjectured readings and the excluded hypotheses named there. The joint freedom is (i) as stated, which contains the two frames of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.d-term-level-free-at-fixed-n}(ii) as the case of fixed $H$.

synthesis.number-n-registered-free-input.formal:
\emph{Premise (N), the large number as a registered input.} Let $I$ be the frozen point and $\Lambda := 3Q(I)$, so that $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}); under the field-space premise $Q(I) = 2\rho$ is constant and $\Lambda = 6\rho$ (Premise \claimref{synthesis.field-space-premise-parallel-frozen-point}, which leaves $\rho$ to this input). Write $H^{2} = \Lambda/3$ and $N = M_{P}/H$, so that $G\Lambda = 3N^{-2}$ with $G = M_{P}^{-2}$. The premise: \emph{$N$ is a free number of the series}, not computed from the transport structure, from another premise of the register, or from a dynamics with no further free dimensionless constant, and not a function of the D-term level $\xi G$ (Premise \claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-second-free-number}). Its value, about $10^{61}$, is taken from the record (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-frozen-point-dictionary-external}).

\emph{What kind of number it is}, as \claimref{programme.n-parameter-of-the-laws} states it (a conjectured placement) and not decided further here: under the action as written, with $\Lambda$ fixed before variation, $N$ is a parameter of the laws (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws}); under the Henneaux-Teitelboim promotion of the frozen point's norm to the value of a Lagrange-multiplier field with $d\Lambda = 0$ as an equation of motion (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-henneaux-teitelboim-promotion}), which the series adopts, $N$ is initial data of the descent, dated to the origin, constant on each solution and taking every positive value across the solution space (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.promoted-norm-one-global-pair}); on the Clausius route alone it is initial data even without the promotion (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.einstein-route-makes-n-initial-data}(i)), and the promotion is that route's own variational form. In both readings $\Lambda$ is fixed by the frozen point, $\Lambda = 3Q(I)$, and $N$ is the registered input that sets it. Registering $N$ does not choose between the two readings.

\emph{What it is for.} Every hierarchy the series reads through the frozen point's norm runs through $N$: the value of $\Lambda$, the norm $\rho$ that the field-space premise leaves open, the rung unit $v/H = (v/M_{P})N$ against the law $v/M_{P}$ (Premise \claimref{synthesis.rung-unit-second-free-number}), and the dating's statement that $N$ was fixed at the origin (\claimref{standard-model.dating-descent}). Results that use a value of $\Lambda$ or of $N$ use this input; no assumes edge to it is drawn here.

\emph{What it does not give.} It does not explain why $N$ is large or $\Lambda$ small, which is declared outside the series (\claimref{programme.n-parameter-of-the-laws}); the one measure the promotion names is flat in whichever function of the norm is promoted (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.promoted-norm-one-global-pair}). It does not fix Newton's constant, which is a unit here.

\emph{Refutation condition.} The premise is false if $N$ (equivalently $G\Lambda$) is derived: computed from the transport structure, from another premise of the register, or from a dynamics with no further free dimensionless constant; or if it is shown to be a function of another registered number, such as $\xi G$; or if $\Lambda$, read as $3Q(I)$, is shown not to be one constant (a confirmed $w \neq -1$ with dark energy read as the frozen point's norm, the condition (a) of Premise \claimref{synthesis.field-space-premise-parallel-frozen-point}), so that there is no single $N$ to register. Confirmed means the rule registered on the prediction \claimref{pred.dark-energy-w-minus-one}: two independent surveys each excluding the point $(w_{0}, w_{a}) = (-1, 0)$ of the form $w(a) = w_{0} + w_{a}(1 - a)$ at five standard deviations, each survey allowed the shared CMB prior, by the collaboration's published frequentist distance, Bayesian evidence recorded beside it; a model-independent exclusion of $w = -1$ at any epoch counts by the same rule; the rule is conservative. The series has no fallback for $w \neq -1$ (argued: a search of the store, not a proof): the promoted norm keeps $w = -1$ and the norm released locally tracks one fluid and decelerates (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.norm-released-locally-on-isotropic-fields-tracks-dust-and-never-accelerates}, within its scope), and the one stored structure with a late-time equation of state different from $-1$, the unadopted branch of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.unit-ball-clauses-hold-at-one-epoch-unless-hidden-direction-co-expands}(ii) with effective $w = -\tfrac14$, is a dark-matter component with $w_{a} > 0$ and no crossing of $-1$, not a variable norm.
synthesis.number-n-registered-free-input.technical: The series reads the cosmological constant as the norm of the frozen point, $\Lambda = 3Q(I)$, and the large number $N = M_{P}/H$, with $H^{2} = \Lambda/3$, as the one number that sets it; until now that number was carried only by a conjectured programme entity. This premise registers it, as the D-term level of the weak scale is registered: $N$, equivalently $G\Lambda = 3N^{-2}$, is not derived from the transport structure, from another premise, or from a dynamics without a further free constant, and is not a function of the D-term level; its value, about $10^{61}$, comes from the record. What kind of number it is stays as the programme entity states: a parameter of the laws under the action as written, and initial data of the descent, fixed at the origin, under the Henneaux-Teitelboim promotion the series adopts, which is also the Clausius route's own variational form. It sets the value of $\Lambda$, the norm the field-space premise leaves open, and the rung unit $v/H$ against the law $v/M_{P}$. It does not explain why $N$ is large. It would be refuted by a derivation of $N$, by showing it is a function of another registered number, or by a confirmed change of dark energy with time, read as the frozen point's norm (confirmed by the registered rule: two independent surveys each excluding $(w_{0}, w_{a}) = (-1, 0)$ at five standard deviations, a conservative rule; the series has no fallback, as far as a search of the store shows).
synthesis.number-n-registered-free-input.lay: In this framework one huge number, N, the ratio of the Planck mass to the scale set by the cosmological constant, about ten to the sixty-one, lies behind most of its puzzles about scales. Nothing in the framework produces it: its value is taken from observation. This entry records it as one of the basic numbers put in by hand, beside the one that sets the weak scale. Whether it counts as a constant of the laws or as a fact about the universe's history depends on how the gravitational action is written; the framework adopts the version in which it is a fact fixed at the start, without settling why it is so large. The entry would be overturned if anyone derived N, showed it follows from another basic number, or found that dark energy changes with time (by a rule fixed in advance: two independent surveys, each at five standard deviations).

synthesis.pati-salam-chain-defects-canno.formal:
Work on the stored chain: $G = SU(4) \times SU(2)_{L} \times SU(2)_{R}$, simply connected (the store's $\mathrm{Spin}(6) \times \mathrm{Spin}(4)$), broken in one step at $M_{I} = 1.95 \times 10^{10}$ GeV to the Standard Model by the $\nu^{c}\nu^{c}$ component of the $(10,1,3)$ (Theorem \claimref{standard-model.majorana-element}), with $v_{R} = M_{I}/g_{R}$, $g_{R} = 0.469$ (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.what-angle-asks-neutrino-sector}); let $H$ be the stabiliser of that vacuum and $H_{0} = SU(3) \times SU(2)_{L} \times U(1)_{Y}$, $Y = T_{3R} + \tfrac12(B - L)$, its identity component. Let $M_{r} = 2.435 \times 10^{18}$ GeV be the reduced Planck mass and $A_{s} = 2.1 \times 10^{-9}$ the measured amplitude (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-planck-2018-lcdm-parameters}).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{($\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ strings.)} The matter parity $m = (-1_{4}, 1, 1) = \exp(3\pi I_{4}(B - L))$ on the $16$ (numbers, and the entries of the defining representations of the factors, are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, conventions U1), which is the rotor $-1$ of $\mathrm{Spin}(6) = SU(4)$ (the $2\pi$ rotor, the kernel element of Proposition \claimref{std-algebra.spin-double-cover}; its image in $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ is the rotor $-1$ there), lies in $H$ (it fixes every vector and so every tensor, and the $(10,1,3)$ is a tensor: self-dual $3$-vectors of the six-dimensional factor and self-dual bivectors of the four-dimensional one) and not in $H_{0}$: every central element of $G$ in $H_{0}$ has equal $SU(4)$ and $SU(2)_{R}$ scalars, and $m$ does not. Hence $\pi_{1}(G/H) = \pi_{0}(H)$ contains $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$: the chain has topologically stable $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ strings at the scale $v_{R}$, besides the monopoles of $\pi_{2}(G/H) = \pi_{1}(H_{0}) \supseteq \mathbb{Z}$ (the hypercharge circle is a noncontractible loop of $H_{0}$ that closes in the simply connected $G$).
\item[(ii)] \emph{(No formation after the descent.)} Under Premise \claimref{neutrino.r-descent-reheats-below-lower-heavy} on the untuned fit (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.untuned-fit-caps-lightest-heavy-neutrino}) the descent reheats below $7.3 \times 10^{8}$ GeV $< 0.0176\,v_{R}$, so unless the restoration temperature of the chain lies below $0.0176\,v_{R}$ the descended bath never restores Pati-Salam, and the chain's monopoles and strings exist after the descent only as part of the deposit. The later transitions form no topologically stable defect: the electroweak vacuum manifold is the three-sphere and the strong interaction breaks no gauge symmetry.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(A deposited network is negligible.)} A deposited $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ string network reaches scaling with $G\mu = \epsilon\,\eta^{2}/(4M_{r}^{2})$; for $\epsilon \in [\tfrac12, 10]$ and $\eta \in [v_{R}/\sqrt2, \sqrt2\,v_{R}]$, $G\mu \in (1.8 \times 10^{-17}, 1.46 \times 10^{-15})$, central value $7.3 \times 10^{-17}$. Its share of the temperature power at $\ell = 10$ is $f_{10} = \kappa\,(G\mu)^{2}$ with $\kappa < 10^{13}$ for both string models, so, with the mirror copy doubling it, $f_{10} < 4.3 \times 10^{-17}$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Monopoles.)} Deposited monopoles are a pressureless gas with fluctuations of finite range, in the class of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.finite-range-descent-deposit-cannot-seed-cmb}, and are bounded in density by the flux limit of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-macro-monopole-flux-limit} (argued).
\end{enumerate}
So no topological defect network of the stored chain, formed after the descent or deposited by it, supplies more than $10^{-16}$ of the CMB temperature power at $\ell = 10$, an active source and not a primordial spectrum, so it is no source of the measured primordial spectrum; the third line of attack of the open problem is closed for the chain's defects. Sources outside the chain (global symmetries broken in the descended phase, sectors not in the store) are not covered.
synthesis.pati-salam-chain-defects-canno.technical: The series' grand-unified chain breaks $SU(4) \times SU(2)_{L} \times SU(2)_{R}$ to the Standard Model in one step with the $(10,1,3)$. Topological defects of a breaking $G \to H$ are read from the homotopy of $G/H$: monopoles from $\pi_{2}$, strings from $\pi_{1}$. The store already has the monopoles. The new point is that the breaking leaves matter parity $(-1)^{3(B-L)}$ unbroken, and that this element, $(-1_{4}, 1, 1)$, is not in the connected part $SU(3) \times SU(2)_{L} \times U(1)_{Y}$ of the unbroken group: on the connected part the central elements have the same sign on $SU(4)$ and $SU(2)_{R}$, and matter parity has opposite signs. So $\pi_{1}(G/H) = \pi_{0}(H) \supseteq \mathbb{Z}_{2}$ and the chain has stable $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ strings. Under Premise (R) the descent reheats below $7.3 \times 10^{8}$ GeV, under two percent of $v_{R}$, so, unless the chain's restoration temperature is below that, its symmetry is never restored after the descent and these defects can only be deposited; the electroweak and strong transitions make none. A deposited string network relaxes to scaling with tension set by $v_{R}$: $G\mu$ about $10^{-16}$, at most $1.5 \times 10^{-15}$, and its contribution to the CMB power is proportional to $(G\mu)^{2}$, below $10^{-16}$ of the measured temperature power at $\ell = 10$ even with the mirror copy. Deposited monopoles are a finite-range deposit, already covered. The open problem's third attack line, a defect or scaling network of the descended phase, is therefore closed for the defects of the stored chain.
synthesis.pati-salam-chain-defects-canno.lay: When a symmetry of the forces breaks as the universe cools, it can leave behind defects: point-like monopoles, or long thin strings of trapped energy. Moving strings were once a candidate source for the ripples in the cosmic microwave background. The framework's unified theory does produce stable strings, as well as the monopoles already known. But the strings carry a tension set by an energy scale far below the one that would matter, so a network of them would contribute less than a ten-million-billionth of the ripples' strength. And in the framework's account, unless the symmetry returns at an unusually low temperature, the universe never got hot enough after its origin to remake these defects at all. Defects of this theory cannot explain the primordial ripples.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} Write elements of the maximal torus of $G$ as phase tuples, in turns: four for $SU(4)$ on its $4$, two each for $SU(2)_{L}$ and $SU(2)_{R}$ on their doublets. The $(10,1,3)$ vacuum is its $\nu^{c}\nu^{c}$ component (Theorem \claimref{standard-model.majorana-element}): the weight $2e_{4}$ of the $10$ ($B - L = -2$) tensored with the weight $T_{3R} = +1$ of the $3$, so $Y = 0$ on it; a torus element fixes it exactly when the phase of that weight vanishes mod $1$. On the $4$, $B - L = \mathrm{diag}(\tfrac13, \tfrac13, \tfrac13, -1)$ (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pati-salam-representation-theory-survival}).

\emph{(i)} The element $m = (-1_{4}, 1, 1)$ has phases $\tfrac12$ on the $4$; its $SU(4)$ determinant phase is $2 \equiv 0$, so $m \in G$. Every weight of the $10$ is a sum of two weights of the $4$, so $m$ acts on the $10$ by $e^{2\pi I_{4}} = 1$ (numbers and matrix entries in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, as in the statement) and trivially on the whole $(10,1,3)$; in particular $m \in H$. On the $(4,2,1)$ and $(\bar4,1,2)$ it acts by $-1$, and $\tfrac32(B - L) \equiv \tfrac12$ on every entry of the $4$, so $m = \exp(3\pi I_{4}(B - L))$ there: matter parity. In Clifford form, $SU(4) = \mathrm{Spin}(6)$ and $-1_{4}$ is the rotor $-1$, the square of the rotor $e_{1}e_{2}$ of the rotation by $\pi$; by Proposition \claimref{std-algebra.spin-double-cover} it is the kernel of $\Ad$, so it fixes every vector, hence every multivector, and the $10 \oplus \overline{10}$ is the space of $3$-vectors of the six-dimensional factor (self-dual and anti-self-dual), while on spinors (the $4$ and $\bar 4$) it acts by $-1$; the check computes these in $\Cl(6,0)$. Under $\mathrm{Spin}(6) \times \mathrm{Spin}(4) \to \mathrm{Spin}(10)$ its image is the rotor $-1$ of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$. Of the centre $\{I_{4}^{a}1_{4}\}$ of $SU(4)$ only $a = 0, 2$ fix the vacuum (phase $a/2$ on it).

Suppose $m \in H_{0}$. A general element of $H_{0}$ is $h = (\mathrm{diag}(e^{I_{4}\theta/6}U_{3}, e^{-I_{4}\theta/2}),\, u_{L},\, \mathrm{diag}(e^{I_{4}\theta/2}, e^{-I_{4}\theta/2}))$ with $U_{3} \in SU(3)$, $u_{L} \in SU(2)_{L}$, $\theta \in \R$, since $\exp(I_{4}\theta Y)$ has these entries and $SU(3)$, $SU(2)_{L}$ and $U(1)_{Y}$ commute; $H_{0}$ is their product. Because $m$ is central in $G$, so would $h$ be. The $SU(2)_{R}$ entry $\mathrm{diag}(e^{I_{4}\theta/2}, e^{-I_{4}\theta/2})$ is a scalar only if $e^{I_{4}\theta} = 1$, that is $\theta = 2\pi t$ with $t \in \mathbb{Z}$, and then it is $(-1)^{t}$. The $SU(4)$ entry is a scalar $c$ only if $c = e^{-I_{4}\theta/2} = (-1)^{t}$ and $U_{3} = (-1)^{t}e^{-I_{4}\pi t/3}1_{3}$, a centre element of $SU(3)$ (determinant $(-1)^{3t}e^{-I_{4}\pi t} = (-1)^{4t} = 1$). So every central element of $G$ in $H_{0}$ has its $SU(4)$ scalar equal to its $SU(2)_{R}$ scalar, both $(-1)^{t}$. For $m$ these are $-1$ and $+1$: $m \notin H_{0}$. Since $G$ is connected and simply connected, the exact homotopy sequence of $H \to G \to G/H$ gives $\pi_{1}(G/H) \cong \pi_{0}(H) = H/H_{0}$ (standard, cited from memory), which contains the class of $m$, of order two ($m^{2} = 1$). The element $(-1_{4}, -1, -1)$ acts trivially on every field of the chain, so the gauge group that acts effectively is the quotient of $G$ by it; that element is central with $c_{4} = c_{R}$, hence lies in $H_{0}$, so the quotient has the same coset space $G/H$ and the same $\pi_{1}$. These are the $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ strings; the monopoles come from $\pi_{2}(G/H) = \pi_{1}(H_{0}) \supseteq \mathbb{Z}$: the loop $\exp(2\pi I_{4}t Y)$, $t \in [0, 6]$, closes (hypercharge period $6$ on the $16$) and generates an infinite cyclic subgroup of $\pi_{1}(U(1)_{Y})$ that survives in $\pi_{1}(H_{0})$ because $U(1)_{Y}$ is a central circle factor of $H_{0}$ up to a finite quotient. A control: $(-1_{4}, 1, -1_{R})$ is the element $t = 1$, $U_{3} = e^{2\pi I_{4}/3}1_{3}$ of $H_{0}$, so $m$ and $(1, 1, -1_{R})$ represent the same nontrivial class.

\emph{(ii)} By Proposition \claimref{standard-model.what-angle-asks-neutrino-sector}, $v_{R} = M_{I}/g_{R} = 1.95 \times 10^{10}/0.469 = 4.158 \times 10^{10}$ GeV. Under Premise \claimref{neutrino.r-descent-reheats-below-lower-heavy}, with the untuned fit's cap on the lightest heavy neutrino (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.untuned-fit-caps-lightest-heavy-neutrino}), $T_{\mathrm{desc}} < 7.3 \times 10^{8}$ GeV, which lies between $0.0175\,v_{R}$ and $0.0176\,v_{R}$. A gauge symmetry broken at the scale $v_{R}$ is restored above a temperature of order $v_{R}$ (the ratio is a ratio of couplings and is not computed in the store); unless that ratio is below $0.0176$, no temperature reached after the descent restores the symmetry, so no Kibble formation of the chain's defects occurs in the descended phase, and they are present only if the descent deposits them. The remaining breakings of the series form none: $(SU(2)_{L} \times U(1)_{Y})/U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$ is the three-sphere (cited from memory), with $\pi_{0} = \pi_{1} = \pi_{2} = 0$, and the strong interaction breaks no gauge symmetry.

\emph{(iii)} A string network of any initial density relaxes to the scaling regime, of order one string per Hubble volume, whose CMB imprint scales as $(G\mu)^{2}$ (cited from memory). For a string of the Nielsen-Olesen type $\mu = 2\pi\epsilon\,\eta^{2}$, with $\eta$ the vacuum value and $\epsilon$ a slowly varying function of the quartic-to-gauge coupling ratio, equal to one at the self-dual point and below $10$ over the range of interest (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-nielsen-olesen-string-tension}); with $G = 1/(8\pi M_{r}^{2})$, $G\mu = \epsilon\,\eta^{2}/(4M_{r}^{2})$. The $(10,1,3)$ vacuum value is $v_{R}$ up to the normalisation of the triplet, which is absorbed by $\eta \in [v_{R}/\sqrt2, \sqrt2\,v_{R}]$. With $(v_{R}/M_{r})^{2} = 2.9156 \times 10^{-16}$: $G\mu = 7.29 \times 10^{-17}$ at $\epsilon = 1$, $\eta = v_{R}$; $1.82 \times 10^{-17}$ at the lower corner; $1.457 \times 10^{-15}$ at the upper corner. The Planck string bounds (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-planck-2013-cosmic-string-bounds}) give $f_{10} < 0.015$ at $G\mu < 1.5 \times 10^{-7}$ for Nambu-Goto strings and $f_{10} < 0.028$ at $G\mu < 3.2 \times 10^{-7}$ for Abelian-Higgs strings, so $\kappa = f_{10}/(G\mu)^{2}$ is $6.7 \times 10^{11}$ and $2.7 \times 10^{11}$, both below $10^{13}$. The mirror sector, a reversal copy with the same chain and scales, at most doubles the power. Hence $f_{10} < 2 \times 10^{13} \times (1.457 \times 10^{-15})^{2} < 4.3 \times 10^{-17}$, and in units of the measured amplitude $A_{s} = 2.1 \times 10^{-9}$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-planck-2018-lcdm-parameters}) the product $f_{10}A_{s}$ is below $10^{-25}$. This is the string share of the temperature power at $\ell = 10$, an active source, not a primordial spectrum. A $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ string is its own antistring and reconnects, so its network scales like the ones the bounds were computed for; the bound uses only the $(G\mu)^{2}$ scaling and a coefficient $\kappa$ fifteen times above the larger of the two models.

\emph{(iv)} Monopoles deposited at any temperature in the window of (ii), below $0.0176\,v_{R}$ and so well below their mass of order $4\pi v_{R}/g_{R}$, are nonrelativistic and do not scale: their density contrast is the Poisson noise of a deposit whose correlations have finite range, the class bounded by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.finite-range-descent-deposit-cannot-seed-cmb}, and their density is capped by the flux limit of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-macro-monopole-flux-limit}. This clause is argued.

\emph{Scope.} The result covers the topological defects of the stored chain and of its mirror copy. Global symmetries broken in the descended phase (none is stored; the chain gauges $B - L$) and sectors outside the store are not covered. If the restoration temperature of the chain were below $0.0176\,v_{R}$, strings could form after the descent, and clause (iii) would still bound their power. \emph{A link (argued):} a deposit whose Pati-Salam orientation is uncorrelated beyond the descent's Hubble length leaves a scaling $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ network at $G\mu$ between about $2 \times 10^{-17}$ and $1.5 \times 10^{-15}$, near the reach of LISA for string backgrounds (of order $10^{-17}$, cited from memory), while an aligned deposit leaves none; this is the same long-range correlation of the deposit that a causal monopole bound on the descent history meets: a deposit whose orientation is uncorrelated beyond the descent's Hubble length leaves at least of order one monopole per Hubble volume as well.

synthesis.pre-descent-contracting-kasner.formal:
\emph{Premise (P1) of the Kasner exit, a contracting metric stage before the descent.} Before the descent there is a stage on which the gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) has an invertible region whose derived metric, near a wall at $\tau = 0$, is synchronous and diagonal, $d\tau^{2} - \sum_{j}\tau^{2p_{j}}(dx^{j})^{2}$ over the three observed directions and any hidden ones, with $\sum_{j}p_{j} = 1$ (the setting of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.kasner-approach-gives-horizon-exit-and-index-three}), and on which $\tau$ decreases toward the wall: the volume, proportional to $\tau$, contracts as the wall is approached. The fields whose exited spectra the stored Kasner results compute propagate on that region.

\emph{What it does not fix.} It fixes no Kasner exponents, no duration of the approach, no matter content and no state of the fields on the stage; in particular it does not say that the approach lasts until the observed modes have left the Hubble length, nor whether the approach reaches the wall or is ended before it by the descent. It says nothing about the descended phase; carrying the stage's state into the descended phase is the separate Premise \claimref{synthesis.pre-descent-state-carried-into-descended-phase-premise} (P2).

\emph{What it is for.} The one geometry in the store in which modes leave the Hubble length is a Kasner approach to a wall, and modes of every Bessel order leave it only while the approach contracts toward the wall (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.kasner-exit-needs-a-contracting-metric-stage-and-a-wall-matching}(i)). With the descent at the origin and the descended phase expanding monotonically from it, such an approach can only precede the descent; so the stored Kasner spectra (Theorems \claimref{synthesis.kasner-approach-gives-horizon-exit-and-index-three}, \claimref{synthesis.kasner-approach-coupled-modes-reach-measured-tilt-only-by-a-fitted-curvature-coupling}, \claimref{synthesis.kasner-hidden-scale-coupled-scalars-stay-blue}), read as a source of the primordial spectrum, need this stage. It is stated as hypothesis (P1) in the reading of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.kasner-exit-needs-a-contracting-metric-stage-and-a-wall-matching} and in the formal of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tree-level-curvature-couplings-stay-blue-at-the-isotropic-kasner-point}; neither has an assumes edge to this premise.

\emph{What it does not give.} It does not supply the tilt. At tree level every curvature coupling the series fixes (twelve values, the largest $\tfrac12$) leaves the exited spectrum blue at the Kasner points the store fixes, with index at least $3 - \sqrt{3}$ for a scalar with no hidden-scale weight and at least $3 - \sqrt{7}$ with the stored weights (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tree-level-curvature-couplings-stay-blue-at-the-isotropic-kasner-point}); the curvature coupling that matches the measured tilt (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.kasner-approach-coupled-modes-reach-measured-tilt-only-by-a-fitted-curvature-coupling}) stays a free parameter, not fixed by the series and not adopted. It does not supply the amplitude.

\emph{Tension, recorded and not resolved.} The dating reads pre-descent physics as pre-metric, the polynomial action and the $\theta$-remnants alone (\claimref{standard-model.dating-descent}, reading (iii), a conjecture at observation level); on that reading there is no derived metric before the descent, and this premise is denied. No proved result in the store denies it, as far as the store has been searched: gravity's polynomial action is defined across the singular locus (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.gravity-pre-metric-forces-degenerate-exactly}(2)). The two cannot both hold; which one gives way is not decided here.

\emph{Refutation condition.} The premise is false if either of the following is established: (a) the pre-metric reading of the dating is proved, that is, before the descent the gravitational field has no invertible region (no nondegenerate soldering, so no derived metric); (b) any other proved result of the series excludes a metric stage contracting toward a Kasner wall before the descent. It is idle, not refuted, if the descent is not at the origin or the descended phase does not expand monotonically from it, since then an exit stage need not precede the descent.
synthesis.pre-descent-contracting-kasner.technical: The only geometry in the store in which field modes are stretched beyond the Hubble length is an approach to a Kasner wall, and the stretching happens only while space contracts toward the wall. Since the series places the descent at the origin and the universe expands from it, such a stage, if it supplies anything, must come before the descent. This premise takes that stage as given: before the descent the gravitational field has an invertible region with a synchronous diagonal Kasner metric, exponents summing to one, contracting toward its wall. It fixes no exponents, duration, matter or state, and it does not say how the stage's state reaches the descended phase, which is the companion premise (P2). Even granted, it does not supply the tilt: at tree level the curvature couplings the series fixes leave the spectrum blue at the Kasner points the store fixes, so the coupling that would match the measured tilt remains a free parameter. It stands against the dating's conjectured reading of pre-descent physics as pre-metric, which denies it; no proved result does, and the tension is recorded, not resolved. It would be refuted by a proof that there is no derived metric before the descent, or by any other proved exclusion of such a stage.
synthesis.pre-descent-contracting-kasner.lay: In this framework the universe begins with an event called the descent, and nothing in it stretches the earliest ripples to cosmic size after that event. The one known way the framework could stretch them is a stage in which space is squeezed toward a singularity, and that squeezing would have to happen before the descent. This assumption says such a stage existed. It is put in by hand: the framework's own account of the descent suggests that before it there was no ordinary geometry at all, and the two views clash. Even with this assumption the fields the framework fixes give ripples tilted the wrong way, so it does not explain the measured tilt.

synthesis.pre-descent-state-carried-into.formal:
\emph{Premise (P2) of the Kasner exit, the state carried into the descended phase.} Assume Premise \claimref{synthesis.pre-descent-contracting-kasner-stage-premise} (P1). There is a rule, part of the laws, that takes the state of the fields on the contracting stage, including the modes that have left the Hubble length there, to a state of the same fields in the descended phase, so that the descended phase's state on scales outside its Hubble length is determined by the exited state. The rule acts in one of two cases:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] \emph{(Across the wall.)} If the approach reaches its wall, the rule is a matching across the wall into the descent. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.kasner-exit-needs-a-contracting-metric-stage-and-a-wall-matching}(iii) the wall is a curvature singularity at every stored Kasner point except the five-dimensional vacuum end $(0, 0, 0, 1)$, where the five-dimensional metric is flat and the hidden scale collapses while the Einstein-frame reduction is the isotropic disk point, singular in four dimensions; the frozen-point datum extends regularly across a singular wall in no chart (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-datum-kasner-wall}(i)).
\item[(b)] \emph{(Across the descent.)} If the descent ends the approach at finite $\tau$, after the modes have left the Hubble length, the rule is a matching across the descent itself.
\end{enumerate}
In either case, under Einstein's equations a turn from contraction to expansion needs a singularity or a violation of the null energy condition (the argued reading of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.kasner-exit-needs-a-contracting-metric-stage-and-a-wall-matching}), so a premise of this kind is needed whichever case holds.

\emph{What it does not fix.} The premise asserts that such a rule exists; it does not give its form. In particular it does not fix which quantity of the exited state is carried over unchanged, and so not how the exited spectrum of a field maps to the spectrum of the curvature perturbation in the descended phase; once a field's state is in the descended phase, its local conversion into the curvature perturbation is the subject of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.local-conversion-cannot-redden-a-gaussian-spectator}. It has no content without (P1).

\emph{What it is for.} With (P1) it is the second of the two hypotheses under which a Kasner approach can be a source of the primordial spectrum: on the expanding branch after a wall no mode exits and the state at the wall is initial data (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.kasner-exit-needs-a-contracting-metric-stage-and-a-wall-matching}(i), (ii)), so a spectrum exited before the descent reaches the record only if it is carried across. It is stated as hypothesis (P2) in the reading of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.kasner-exit-needs-a-contracting-metric-stage-and-a-wall-matching}, which has no assumes edge to it. At the five-dimensional Milne end the wall is the compactified Milne geometry of the ekpyrotic and cyclic models, whose matching is not settled there either (cited from memory).

\emph{What it does not give.} It does not supply the tilt: granting (P1) and (P2), at tree level every curvature coupling the series fixes (twelve values, the largest $\tfrac12$) leaves the exited spectrum blue at the Kasner points the store fixes (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tree-level-curvature-couplings-stay-blue-at-the-isotropic-kasner-point}), and the tilt-matching curvature coupling stays a free parameter.

\emph{Tension, recorded and not resolved.} The dating reads pre-descent physics as pre-metric (\claimref{standard-model.dating-descent}, reading (iii), a conjecture), which denies (P1) and so leaves this premise without a stage to carry from; reading (ii) takes the initial singularity to be a division event, with the classical era the descended phase. A rule that carries a metric state across the descent presupposes a metric stage before the classical era, which reading (iii) denies. Which gives way is not decided here.

\emph{Refutation condition.} The premise is false if, with (P1) granted, it is proved that no state of the descended phase depends on the exited modes of the contracting stage: for example, that the descent's map on states takes every state of the stage's fields to one independent of their exited modes, or that across a singular Kasner wall the series' field equations admit no continuation of data outside the Hubble length when the approach reaches the wall and the descent does not end it first. It falls with (P1) if (P1) is refuted.
synthesis.pre-descent-state-carried-into.technical: If a contracting Kasner stage before the descent is granted (premise (P1)), the modes it stretches beyond the Hubble length still have to reach the universe we observe, which expands from the descent. This premise takes as given a rule that carries the stage's state into the descended phase: a matching across the wall if the approach runs into it, which at every stored Kasner point except one five-dimensional end is a true curvature singularity, or a matching across the descent itself if the descent cuts the approach short after the modes have left. Under Einstein's equations a turn from contraction to expansion needs a singularity or a violation of the null energy condition, so some such rule is needed in either case. The premise says the rule exists, not what it is: it does not fix which quantity passes through unchanged, and so not which spectrum the descended phase inherits. Even with both premises granted the tree-level couplings the series fixes leave the spectrum blue, so the tilt is not supplied. It stands against the dating's conjectured pre-metric reading of pre-descent physics; the tension is recorded, not resolved. It would be refuted by a proof that the descended phase's state cannot depend on the exited modes, for example that the descent's map on states erases them.
synthesis.pre-descent-state-carried-into.lay: Suppose that before the framework's starting event, the descent, space was being squeezed toward a singularity, stretching the early ripples. Those ripples would still have to survive into the expanding universe we see, passing through either a true singularity or the descent itself. This assumption says that they do: some rule of nature carries them across. The framework does not say what the rule is, and its own account of the descent suggests there was no ordinary geometry before it, so the assumption sits uneasily with it. Even with this rule the fields the framework fixes give ripples tilted the wrong way.
