synthesis.promoted-norm-one-global-pair.formal:
\emph{Setting.} Promote the norm as in Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-henneaux-teitelboim-promotion}: in the three-argument functional of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation}, replace the number $\Lambda$ in the Stelle-West constraints $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$, $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$ by a positive function $\lambda$ on spacetime $M$, on which gravity is a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), and add $c\int_{M}\lambda\,dT$ with $c \ne 0$ a constant and $T$ a $3$-form field. Take $M = \R \times \Sigma$ with $\Sigma$ compact, connected and orientable.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Pointwise count.)} At each point the linearised constraints are three independent conditions on the thirteen components of $(\delta I, \delta V, \delta\lambda)$; the ten remaining directions are the nine images of the broken generators and the norm mode $n = (I/2\lambda, -V/2\lambda, 1)$ of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws}. Unitary gauge removes every fluctuation of $(I, V)$ except the multiple $\delta\lambda\,n$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(No local norm mode.)} Varying $T$ gives $d\lambda = 0$, so on connected $M$ the multiplier is a constant $\Lambda$ and the norm mode enters as one number $\delta\Lambda$, constant over spacetime. No local fluctuation of $(I, V, \lambda)$ survives unitary gauge: the local Goldstone count is nine broken generators against nine eaten directions, as without the promotion, and the graviton still carries no $(\delta I, \delta V, \delta\lambda)$ polarisation.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(One global pair.)} In $c\int\lambda\,dT$ the pullback $T_{\Sigma}$ of $T$ to a slice is conjugate to $\lambda$, and the components of $T$ along the time direction are multipliers for the constraint $d\lambda|_{\Sigma} = 0$, which generates $T_{\Sigma} \mapsto T_{\Sigma} + d\theta$. The reduced phase space of the $(\lambda, T)$ sector is $H^{0}(\Sigma) \times H^{3}(\Sigma) \cong \R^{2}$, paired by integration over $\Sigma$: exactly one canonical pair $(\Lambda, \tau)$, $\tau = \int_{\Sigma}T_{\Sigma}$, and no local degree of freedom.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Kind of number.)} The promoted functional has no parameter left in the norm, and for every $\Lambda > 0$ the solutions of the unpromoted equations with parameter $\Lambda$, together with a $T$ solving the $\lambda$-equation, are solutions of it. So $N = M_{P}\sqrt{3/\Lambda}$ is not constant on its solution space: in the sense of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-energy.four-ways-number-enters-theory-shape} it is (I), initial data, and not (P).
\item[(v)] \emph{(The measure the promotion names.)} The Liouville measure of the reduced pair is $|c|\,d\Lambda\,d\tau$, so the Liouville density per unit $\tau$ is constant in $\Lambda$ and its integral over $\Lambda > 0$ diverges. This is a density on the reduced phase space, not a normalised weight over histories: on a solution $\tau$ advances by an amount that depends on the solution. If instead a function $g$ of the norm is promoted, $c\int g(\lambda)\,dT$, the Liouville density per unit $\tau$ is $|c\,g'(\Lambda)|$: constant for the norm $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ that the Fact transcribes, $3|c|/\Lambda^{2}$ for $\ell^{2} = 3/\Lambda$. The promotion names a measure only together with the choice of $g$. With the transcribed choice, a cutoff $\Lambda \le \Lambda_{\max}$, and the convention that every value of $\Lambda$ is given the same $\tau$-range, the measure of $\Lambda \le \Lambda_{\mathrm{obs}}$ is the fraction $\Lambda_{\mathrm{obs}}/\Lambda_{\max}$, which equals $3/N^{2}$ for $\Lambda_{\max} = M_{P}^{2}$; without both assumptions no fraction is defined.
\end{enumerate}

\emph{Beyond one flat chart.} The compact spatial slice $\Sigma$ of $M = \R \times \Sigma$, on which the reduced phase space of (iii) is $H^{0}(\Sigma) \times H^{3}(\Sigma)$, is global and is not carried by a single gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime; the statements above that hold on the invertible region (the pointwise count (i) and the equation $d\lambda = 0$ of (ii)) are in GTG, and the compact slice is read on the manifold assembled from the derived metric's charts.
synthesis.promoted-norm-one-global-pair.technical: The decision left open is whether the cosmological constant is a parameter of the series' action or the value of a field whose constancy is an equation of motion. This result carries the second branch through. Its new content is the series' own count with the norm mode and the change in which kind of number $N$ is; the one global pair and the absence of local degrees of freedom are the Henneaux-Teitelboim reduction itself, applied here to the norm. Pointwise nothing changes: with the norm free there are ten constrained directions, nine of them gauge and the tenth the norm mode already found in the store. The promotion's own equation says the multiplier is constant, so the norm mode is a single number for the whole universe, not a field: no new local degree of freedom appears and the graviton count is untouched. The 3-form that carries the promotion has no local degrees of freedom either; on a closed slice it leaves exactly one number, its integral, the cosmic time conjugate to the cosmological constant. The cochain check exhibits this on lattice 3-tori, where the constraint leaves the constants and the gauge freedom leaves only the total. Under the promotion the number N therefore varies across the solutions of one theory, which is what initial data means in the series' classification. Finally, the only measure over the cosmological constant that the promotion supplies without a further choice is the Liouville measure of its one canonical pair. Its density per unit of the conjugate time is flat in whichever function of the norm is promoted, so it is fixed only with that choice; for the norm itself it is flat in the cosmological constant. Only with a cutoff at the Planck scale and the convention that every value gets the same range of conjugate time does this become a fraction, about $3/N^{2}$, for values as small as the observed one; on actual histories the conjugate time advances by a solution-dependent amount, so the convention is a choice. A computation filed alongside, synthesis.promoted-norm-weyl-clock-flat-weight, finds that the conjugate time advances by the Weyl-squared integral, and that under the no-boundary hypothesis the round four-sphere has weight one at every cosmological constant, so no factor of the action favours small values; with that, the smallness of the cosmological constant stays unexplained under the promotion. Reading, not proved here: since the conjugate time is global, the cosmological constant commutes with every local observable, so the I-state of the cosmological horizon lives in one sector of fixed cosmological constant, and a state with a definite cosmic time spreads over sectors and is KMS at no single temperature. Its compact spatial slice, on which the one global pair lives, is global: no single gravitational field on flat spacetime carries it, so that part is read on several charts of flat spacetime, each carrying its own gravitational field, glued on overlaps by displacement and rotation gauge transformations.
synthesis.promoted-norm-one-global-pair.lay: The series has a choice to make about the cosmological constant: is it a fixed setting of the laws, or a quantity that happens to have the value it has in our universe, as a starting condition would? The standard way to make it the second is to let it be a field and add an equation saying the field cannot vary. This result works out what that choice adds to the series. Nothing local: there is still no new particle or wave, and the count of the series' hidden directions is unchanged. What it adds is a single pair of numbers for the whole universe, the cosmological constant and a cosmic clock reading that goes with it. With that choice, the number N that sets the scale of the universe becomes a starting condition rather than a law. The natural way of weighing the possible values that the choice supplies treats every value equally per unit of the cosmic clock, so it does not explain why the observed value is so small; and even that weighing depends on which version of the quantity is made into a field.

proofs.main:
Gravity is in Gauge Theory Gravity (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}): $I$, $V$ and the canonical tractor are vectors of the conformal model $\Cl(2,4)$ at each point, the ambient gauge transformations act on them by bivectors through the commutator, $\delta I = B\cdot I$, and differential forms on spacetime are multivector fields: the $3$-form $T$ is a trivector field, $dT = 
abla\wedge T$ is a pseudoscalar field, and $\int\lambda\,dT = \int\lambda\,\langle(
abla\wedge T)I^{-1}angle\,d^{4}x$.

\emph{(i).} With $\lambda$ a field, the constraints $Q(I) = \lambda/3$, $I\cdot V = 0$, $Q(V) = -3/\lambda$ linearise to $2\,\delta I\cdot I - \delta\lambda/3 = 0$, $\delta V\cdot I + V\cdot\delta I = 0$ and $2\,\delta V\cdot V - 3\,\delta\lambda/\lambda^{2} = 0$, the free case of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws}: three independent conditions on thirteen components, a ten-dimensional constrained space, inside which the images $(B\cdot I, B\cdot V, 0)$ of the fifteen bivectors $B$ of $\Cl(2,4)$ span nine dimensions (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation}: bivectors do not change a norm, and the stabiliser of $(I,V)$ is the six-dimensional Lorentz algebra of $\{I,V\}^{\perp}$) and the norm mode $n$ is constrained and not a gauge direction, so the two together span the constrained space. Gauge transformations act on $(
abla, I, V)$ and leave $\lambda$ and $T$ alone, so after removing the gauge part the remaining fluctuation of $(I, V, \lambda)$ at each point is $\delta\lambda(x)\,n(x)$. The GTG check takes $I = 
Inf + 	frac{\Lambda}{6}
O$ and $V = 
O - 	frac{3}{\Lambda}I$ in $\Cl(2,4)$, the bivector action by the commutator, and finds the ranks $3$, $9$, $10$ exactly at $\Lambda = 3$, $12$, $	frac34$ and $-6$; the earlier check does the same in components of $\R^{2,4}$.

\emph{(ii).} The added term is the only one containing $T$, and $
abla\wedge(\lambda\,\delta T) = 
abla\lambda\wedge\delta T + \lambda\,
abla\wedge\delta T$ gives $\delta_{T}\,c\int\lambda\,\langle(
abla\wedge T)I^{-1}angle = -c\int\langle(
abla\lambda\wedge\delta T)I^{-1}angle$ up to a boundary term, for every compactly supported trivector field $\delta T$; the map $\delta T \mapsto \langle(g\wedge\delta T)I^{-1}angle$ vanishes on all trivectors only for $g = 0$ (the GTG check finds it of rank one for timelike, spacelike and null $g$ and zero for $g = 0$), so $
abla\lambda = 0$, the equation $d\lambda = 0$. On connected $M$, $\lambda = \Lambda$ is constant and $\delta\lambda = \delta\Lambda$ is a constant, so by (i) the only non-gauge fluctuation of $(I, V, \lambda)$ is the global one, $\delta\Lambda\,n$, the tangent at $s = 1$ of the family $(sI, V/s, s^{2}\Lambda)$ up to the factor $1/(2\Lambda)$. Every local fluctuation of $(I, V)$ is therefore gauge, as in Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation}, and its conclusion for the graviton holds unchanged.

\emph{(iii).} This clause is global (beyond one flat chart: the compact slice $\Sigma$ and its de Rham cohomology), so it is read on the manifold assembled from the derived metric's charts, in the language of forms. On $M = \R 	imes \Sigma$ write $T = T_{\Sigma} + dt \wedge T_{0}$ with $T_{\Sigma}$ a $3$-form and $T_{0}$ a $2$-form on the slices. Then $dT = dt \wedge (\partial_{t}T_{\Sigma} - d_{\Sigma}T_{0})$ and, integrating by parts on the compact slices, $c\int\lambda\,dT = c\int dt\int_{\Sigma} igl(\lambda\,\partial_{t}T_{\Sigma} - d_{\Sigma}\lambda \wedge T_{0} igr)$ up to a sign fixed by orientation. So $T_{\Sigma}$ is the momentum conjugate to $\lambda$ (with symplectic form $c\,\delta\lambda \wedge \delta T_{\Sigma}$ integrated over $\Sigma$), and $T_{0}$ is a multiplier for $d_{\Sigma}\lambda = 0$. These constraints are first class (they involve $\lambda$ alone) and the smeared constraint $\int_{\Sigma}d_{\Sigma}\lambda \wedge 	heta$ generates $T_{\Sigma} \mapsto T_{\Sigma} \pm d_{\Sigma}	heta$. The reduced space is the constraint surface, $\lambda$ constant on $\Sigma$, that is $H^{0}(\Sigma)$, times the quotient of $3$-forms by exact ones, $H^{3}(\Sigma)$; for $\Sigma$ compact, connected and orientable both are one-dimensional, and the pairing $\int_{\Sigma}\lambda\,T_{\Sigma} = \Lambda	au$ between them is nondegenerate (Poincar'e duality). So the sector reduces to one canonical pair. That the remaining gravitational part depends on $\lambda$ does not change this: it contributes to the evolution of $	au$, not to the constraints. This is the Henneaux-Teitelboim reduction of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-henneaux-teitelboim-promotion}, here applied to the norm. The check builds the cubical cochain complex of the periodic lattice $(\mathbb{Z}/L)^{3}$, $L = 2, 3$, verifies $\delta^{2} = 0$ and the Betti numbers $1, 3, 3, 1$ of the $3$-torus, and that the sum over cubes vanishes on every coboundary, so that the constants and the total are the surviving pair.

\emph{(v).} The reduced symplectic form is $c\,d\Lambda \wedge d	au$, whose Liouville measure is $|c|\,d\Lambda\,d	au$: its density per unit $	au$ is constant in $\Lambda$, and $\int_{0}^{\infty}d\Lambda$ diverges. Turning this into a relative weight over $\Lambda$ needs a convention for the $	au$-range attached to each value; $	au$ is non-compact and on a solution advances by a solution-dependent amount, so the equal-range convention used for the fraction below is an assumption, not a consequence. Promoting $g(\lambda)$ instead replaces $\lambda$ by $g(\lambda)$ in (iii), so the symplectic form becomes $c\,g'(\Lambda)\,d\Lambda \wedge d	au$: density $|c|/3$ for $g = \lambda/3$, $3|c|/\Lambda^{2}$ for $g = 3/\lambda$. With the flat density, equal $	au$-ranges and support $(0, \Lambda_{\max}]$ the measure of $(0, \Lambda_{\mathrm{obs}}]$ is the fraction $\Lambda_{\mathrm{obs}}/\Lambda_{\max}$, and $N^{2} = 3M_{P}^{2}/\Lambda$ turns it into $3/N^{2}$ for $\Lambda_{\max} = M_{P}^{2}$. The check verifies the two derivatives through exact difference quotients and the last identity at rational points.

\emph{(iv).} Varying $
abla$, $I$ and $V$ in the promoted functional at constant $\lambda = \Lambda$ gives the equations of the unpromoted functional at parameter $\Lambda$, since the added term contains none of them; varying $\lambda$ gives $c\,dT = -\partial\mathcal{L}/\partial\lambda$, a $4$-form equation on $M = \R 	imes \Sigma$, which is solvable because a noncompact connected $4$-manifold has $H^{4}(M) = 0$. So each solution of the unpromoted equations at parameter $\Lambda$, which by Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws}(i) has $N = M_{P}\sqrt{3/\Lambda}$, extends to a solution of the promoted functional, and these solution spaces for different $\Lambda$ all lie in the one solution space of the promoted functional. On it $N$ takes different values, so it is not constant there; the promoted theory is a single functional, so by Definition \claimref{obj.dark-energy.four-ways-number-enters-theory-shape} $N$ is (I) and not (P) or (D).

synthesis.promoted-norm-weyl-clock-flat-.formal:
\emph{Setting.} Take the MacDowell-Mansouri functional of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west} for a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on the Wick-rotated, Euclidean, flat background (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), in Euclidean signature, $S = k\,\ell^{2}\int\epsilon_{abcd}F^{ab}\wedge F^{cd}$ with Lorentz block $F^{ab} = R^{ab} - \ell^{-2}e^{a}\wedge e^{b}$ (the Euclidean form of the de Sitter branch, for which the round $\Sph^{4}$ of radius $\ell$ has $F = 0$), torsion zero, $\Lambda = 3/\ell^{2} > 0$, and $N^{2} = \ell^{2}/G = 3/(G\Lambda)$, the number of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-entropy-pi-n-squared}. Write $W$ for the Weyl tensor, the trace-free part $\mathcal{W}$ of the curvature operator, and $|W|^{2} = W_{abcd}W^{abcd} = 2\langle\mathcal{W}(a \wedge b)\,\mathcal{W}(\partial_b \wedge \partial_a)\rangle$; $\mathrm{vol}$ is $\det(\hb)^{-1}d^{4}x$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Normalisation.)} Matching the Einstein-Cartan term to the Euclidean Einstein-Hilbert action $-\tfrac{1}{16\pi G}\int R$ fixes $k = 1/(64\pi G)$; the cosmological term is then exactly $\tfrac{2\Lambda}{16\pi G}\int\mathrm{vol}$ with $\Lambda = 3/\ell^{2}$, and the Gauss-Bonnet coefficient is $\ell^{2}/(64\pi G) = 3/(64\pi G\Lambda)$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Instanton actions.)} On every Einstein metric with $\Ric = \Lambda g$ the integrand is pointwise $\epsilon_{abcd}F^{ab}\wedge F^{cd} = |W|^{2}\,\mathrm{vol}$, the volume and curvature terms cancelling identically. Hence on every closed Einstein $4$-manifold $M$
\[
I_{\mathrm{MM}}[M] \;=\; \frac{\ell^{2}}{64\pi G}\int_{M}|W|^{2}\,\mathrm{vol} \;=\; I_{\mathrm{EH}}[M] + \frac{\chi(M)}{2}\,\pi N^{2} \;\ge\; 0,
\]
with equality exactly when the Weyl part vanishes on $M$ (locally conformally flat derived metric). For the round $\Sph^{4}$, $\Sph^{2}\times\Sph^{2}$ and $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$: $I_{\mathrm{MM}} = 0$, $\tfrac43\pi N^{2}$, $\tfrac34\pi N^{2}$, against $I_{\mathrm{EH}} = -\pi N^{2}$, $-\tfrac23\pi N^{2}$, $-\tfrac34\pi N^{2}$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The conjugate time.)} Under the promotion of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-henneaux-teitelboim-promotion}, with the norm mode of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws} as the multiplier field, and with \emph{the norm} meaning $u = \ell^{2} = -Q(V)$, the variable conjugate to $u$ advances between two slices by the integral over the region between them of the density $k\bigl(E - 24u^{-2}\bigr)\mathrm{vol}$, $E$ the Gauss-Bonnet integrand, which is the derivative of the Lagrangian in $u$ at fixed frame and connection. On every torsion-free vacuum solution this is $k|W|^{2}\mathrm{vol}$. For any other choice $g(u)$ of the promoted variable (for instance $\Lambda = 3/u$, or the norm $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$) the conjugate variable advances by the same integral divided by $g'(u)$, so for $\Lambda$ by $-3/\Lambda^{2}$ times that; there is a conjugate time for each choice of variable, all proportional on each solution. The value does not depend on which frame normalisation is held fixed as the norm varies: the two choices differ by a multiple of the trace of the full frame equation (with the matter term when matter is present), which vanishes on shell.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Vacuum: where it runs.)} On solutions of the functional as written (vacuum), the conjugate time does not advance on any region where the Weyl part of the field strength vanishes, and such a region is locally the de Sitter field (Einstein with $\mathcal{W} = 0$ is constant curvature), the de Sitter slicings of FLRW form included. Near a Kasner wall with $p_{1}p_{2}p_{3} \neq 0$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-datum-kasner-wall}) its density is $k$ times the Kretschmann density at leading order, $\tfrac{64}{27}\,k\,\tau^{-3}$ for the Schwarzschild exponents, so it diverges as $\tau^{-2}$ toward the wall.
\item[(v)] \emph{(With matter.)} Add a matter action that depends on the frame only through the metric and on matter fields, and not on $u$ or on the connection (hypothesis (Mat)), with torsion zero. The density is still $k(E - 24u^{-2})\mathrm{vol}$. In Lorentzian signature $(3,1)$, with the curvature convention in which de Sitter space has $R_{abcd} = H^{2}(g_{ac}g_{bd} - g_{ad}g_{bc})$, on every solution, where $\Ric - \tfrac12 s\,g + \Lambda g = 8\pi G\,T$ holds, with $t = g^{ab}T_{ab}$ and $T^{\mathrm{tf}}$ the trace-free part of $T$,
\[
E - \tfrac83\Lambda^{2} \;=\; |W|^{2} - 2(8\pi G)^{2}|T^{\mathrm{tf}}|^{2} - \tfrac43\Lambda\,(8\pi G\,t) + \tfrac16(8\pi G\,t)^{2}.
\]
On the flat FLRW gravitational field on flat spacetime ($\hb^{-1}(e_t) = e_t$, $\hb^{-1}(e_i) = a(t)\,e_i$) with a perfect fluid of density $\rho$ and pressure $p$, writing $\tilde\rho = 8\pi G\rho$ and $\tilde p = 8\pi G p$,
\[
E - \tfrac83\Lambda^{2} \;=\; \tfrac43\bigl[\Lambda(\tilde\rho - 3\tilde p) - \tilde\rho(\tilde\rho + 3\tilde p)\bigr],
\]
which is $-\tfrac83\tilde\rho^{2}$ for radiation and $\tfrac43\tilde\rho(\Lambda - \tilde\rho)$ for dust, vanishing for dust only at $8\pi G\rho = \Lambda$. So the conjugate time advances on every FLRW cosmology with radiation or dust; standing still is a property of vacuum. Where $W = 0$, $(3k/\Lambda^{2})(E - \tfrac83\Lambda^{2}) = -t/(2\Lambda) + O(G)$; the time conjugate to $\Lambda$ advances by $(3k/\Lambda^{2})\int(E - \tfrac83\Lambda^{2})\mathrm{vol}$ up to the overall sign set by the signature convention of the action, so to first order in $G$ it counts, for dust, $\rho/(2\Lambda)$ per unit four-volume: rest mass times proper time over $2\Lambda$.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading, conditional on the no-boundary hypothesis (H).} (H) If the relative weight of the values of the promoted $\Lambda$ is the semiclassical factor $e^{-I}$ of closed Einstein instantons, then by (ii) the round $\Sph^{4}$ contributes weight $1$ at every $\Lambda$ and every other Einstein instanton contributes less, the less the smaller $\Lambda$; the factor $e^{\pi N^{2}}$ of the Einstein-Hilbert argument for small $\Lambda$ is cancelled exactly by the Gauss-Bonnet term. Under (H) the series' action therefore supplies no factor favouring small $\Lambda$, and a measure over the promoted $\Lambda$ has to be supplied as a datum of its own.

\emph{Beyond one flat chart.} The closed Einstein four-manifolds of (ii) and of the reading (H) ($\Sph^{4}$, $\Sph^{2}\times\Sph^{2}$, $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$, with their Euler characteristic $\chi(M)$) are global and are not carried by a single gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime; the statements above that hold on the invertible region are in GTG, and the closed instantons are read on the manifold assembled from the derived metric's charts.
synthesis.promoted-norm-weyl-clock-flat-.technical: The frozen-point action is the MacDowell-Mansouri form: Einstein-Hilbert plus a cosmological term plus a Gauss-Bonnet term whose coefficient is fixed at $\ell^{2}/(64\pi G)$. On any Einstein space the three combine into the Weyl-squared integral times that coefficient, so the Euclidean action of an Einstein instanton is non-negative and vanishes exactly for those with vanishing Weyl part, the round four-sphere among them; by Gauss-Bonnet it equals the Einstein-Hilbert value plus half the Euler characteristic times $\pi N^{2}$. The instanton identity itself is known for the Euler-regularised form of this action in the anti-de Sitter case (Miskovic and Olea, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-miskovic-olea-identity}, where the action is on shell equivalent to conformal gravity); what is new here is its reading for the promoted norm and the exact cancellation of the Baum-Hawking factor. If the norm $\ell^{2}$ (or any function of it, which only rescales the result by a derivative) is promoted to a multiplier field as Henneaux and Teitelboim do for $\Lambda$, its conjugate cosmic time is the derivative of the action in the norm, the integral of $k(E - 24\ell^{-4})$ with $E$ the Gauss-Bonnet integrand. On vacuum solutions this is the Weyl-squared integral: it stands still on de Sitter space and diverges at a Kasner wall. With matter coupled through the metric it is not: the trace and the trace-free part of the stress tensor enter, and on a flat FLRW universe with a perfect fluid the density is $\tfrac43 k[\Lambda(\tilde\rho - 3\tilde p) - \tilde\rho(\tilde\rho + 3\tilde p)]$ with $\tilde\rho = 8\pi G\rho$, $\tilde p = 8\pi G p$; it is negative throughout a radiation era, changes sign for dust at $8\pi G\rho = \Lambda$, and to first order in matter the time conjugate to $\Lambda$ counts rest mass times proper time over $2\Lambda$. The clock therefore runs on every universe with dust or radiation; it stands still only in vacuum. It is not monotone (it reverses sign for dust at $8\pi G\rho = \Lambda$), so it is a record of the history, not a time coordinate ordering it. The clock depends on which action is promoted: for the Einstein-Hilbert action it counts four-volume over $8\pi G$, for the series' action the Euler-density excess, which to first order in matter is $\rho/(2\rho_{\Lambda})$ times the four-volume clock, $\rho_{\Lambda} = \Lambda/8\pi G$; the companion result filed alongside, synthesis.einstein-route-makes-n-initial-data, shows that on the Clausius route alone $\Lambda$ is an integration constant and $N$ initial data with no promotion, so what the promotion adds over that route is this clock and the Liouville density. Assuming the no-boundary weighting, the series' action gives every value of $\Lambda$ weight one through the four-sphere and penalises the others, so it contains nothing that favours a small $\Lambda$: the standard Baum-Hawking factor comes from the Einstein-Hilbert action and is cancelled here. Its closed Einstein instantons and their Euler characteristic are global: no single gravitational field on flat spacetime carries them, so that part is read on several charts of flat spacetime (charts of Euclidean $\R^{4}$), each carrying its own gravitational field, glued on overlaps by displacement and rotation gauge transformations; the clock's density is local and lives on a flat chart. Because the clock's advance on a history depends on the solution (in vacuum it is the Weyl-squared integral; with matter it is dominated by the matter's stress), a density over $\Lambda$ that assumes equal ranges of the conjugate time for every $\Lambda$ (as in the phase-space count filed alongside, synthesis.promoted-norm-one-global-pair) carries that assumption as an extra input.
synthesis.promoted-norm-weyl-clock-flat-.lay: The framework's action for gravity differs from Einstein's by a term that only depends on the overall shape of space. One proposal for the cosmological constant is to make it a quantity that can differ between possible universes, paired with a cosmic clock. The first part of this result, the value of the action on these spaces, is already known in the literature on this form of the action; what is added is what it means for that proposal. It computes what the clock is for the framework's action: in empty space it only ticks where space is tidally distorted, so it stands still in a universe holding nothing but the cosmological constant, and near the crushing singularity inside a black hole it runs without bound. In a universe with matter and radiation, like ours, it does tick: fastest in the hot early universe, reversing direction once matter has thinned to the density of the cosmological constant. It also shows that, if one weighs possible universes in the usual way, this action gives no preference to a small cosmological constant, unlike Einstein's action; any explanation of the small observed value would have to come from somewhere else.
flags: beyond one flat chart: the closed Einstein instantons S^4, S^2 x S^2, CP^2 and their Euler characteristic

proofs.main:
Everything is computed in Gauge Theory Gravity (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}, clauses (i), (iv) and (v)), on the flat Euclidean background $\Cl(4,0)$ for (i) to (iii) and on $\Cl(1,3)$ for (iv) and (v); the closed manifolds of (ii) lie beyond one flat chart, and only their pointwise densities are computed on a chart. \emph{Notation.} For curvature operators $X, Y$ (linear maps on bivectors, such as the field strength $\mathcal{R}(B) = -R(\hb(B))$) put
\[
\mathcal{Q}(X, Y) \;=\; 2\,\langle X(a\wedge b)\,I^{-1}\,Y(I\,\partial_{b}\wedge\partial_{a})\rangle ,
\]
symmetric and bilinear; $\epsilon_{abcd}X^{ab}\wedge Y^{cd} = \mathcal{Q}(X, Y)\,\mathrm{vol}$ for the corresponding two-forms in Euclidean signature, and $\mathcal{Q}(X) := \mathcal{Q}(X, X)$ is the Gauss-Bonnet integrand $E(X)$ (dictionary row 13 in the $I^{-1}$ form, which is correct in both signatures). Let $D$ be the curvature operator of the unit four-sphere; in the store's sign on $\Cl(4,0)$ it is $D(B) = -B$ (the check solves the round $\Sph^{4}$ as a gauge field and finds $\mathcal{R}(a) = -3a$), and put $s(X) := \tfrac12\mathcal{Q}(X, D)$, which is the scalar trace in the convention positive on spheres ($s(D) = 12$; $s = -\partial_{a}\cdot\mathcal{R}(a)$ here). Then $\mathcal{Q}(D) = 24$. With $F = \mathcal{R} - \ell^{-2}D$ the Lorentz block of the Euclidean de Sitter-branch curvature (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west}; the sign is the one for which the round $\Sph^{4}$ of radius $\ell$ has $F = 0$; the overall sign of $F$ does not enter $\mathcal{Q}(F)$), bilinearity gives
\begin{equation}
\mathcal{Q}(F) \;=\; E(\mathcal{R}) - 4\ell^{-2}s(\mathcal{R}) + 24\,\ell^{-4}. \tag{1}
\end{equation}
The check computes $\mathcal{Q}$ in $\Cl(4,0)$ from the field strengths of three solved gauge fields and finds $\mathcal{Q}(D) = 24$, $\mathcal{Q}(\mathcal{R}, D) = 2s(\mathcal{R})$ and $\mathcal{Q}(\mathcal{R}) = E(\mathcal{R})$.

\emph{(i)} By (1), $S = k\ell^{2}\int\mathcal{Q}(F)\,\mathrm{vol} = k\ell^{2}\int E - 4k\int s + 24k\ell^{-2}\int\mathrm{vol}$, the three terms of the Fact's decomposition. Matching $-4k\int s$ to $-\tfrac{1}{16\pi G}\int s$ gives $k = 1/(64\pi G)$, and then $24k\ell^{-2} = 3/(8\pi G\ell^{2})$, which equals $2\Lambda/(16\pi G)$ exactly when $\Lambda = 3/\ell^{2}$, the value the Fact's field equations carry; the Gauss-Bonnet coefficient is $k\ell^{2} = \ell^{2}/(64\pi G) = 3/(64\pi G\Lambda)$.

\emph{(ii)} Let the field be Einstein, $\mathcal{R}(a) = -\Lambda a$ on $\Cl(4,0)$ in the store's sign ($\Ric = \Lambda g$ in the convention positive on spheres). The decomposition of the curvature operator into its Weyl and scalar parts (the trace-free Ricci part vanishing) gives $\mathcal{R} = \mathcal{W} + \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}D$, so $F = \mathcal{W} + (\tfrac{\Lambda}{3} - \ell^{-2})D = \mathcal{W}$. The Weyl operator commutes with the duality, $\mathcal{W}(IB) = I\mathcal{W}(B)$ (dictionary row 5), so
\[
\mathcal{Q}(F) = 2\langle\mathcal{W}(a\wedge b)\,I^{-1}I\,\mathcal{W}(\partial_{b}\wedge\partial_{a})\rangle = 2\langle\mathcal{W}(a\wedge b)\,\mathcal{W}(\partial_{b}\wedge\partial_{a})\rangle = |W|^{2} .
\]
Integrating, $I_{\mathrm{MM}}[M] = k\ell^{2}\int_{M}|W|^{2}\mathrm{vol} \ge 0$, with equality exactly when $\mathcal{W} \equiv 0$, which in dimension four is local conformal flatness. For the second form: $E(\mathcal{R}) = \mathcal{Q}(\mathcal{W}) + \tfrac{2\Lambda}{3}\mathcal{Q}(\mathcal{W}, D) + \tfrac{\Lambda^{2}}{9}\mathcal{Q}(D) = |W|^{2} + \tfrac83\Lambda^{2}$, since $\mathcal{Q}(\mathcal{W}, D) = 2s(\mathcal{W}) = 0$ ($\mathcal{W}$ is trace-free), and the Chern-Gauss-Bonnet theorem $\int_{M}E = 32\pi^{2}\chi(M)$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-chern-gauss-bonnet}(b)) gives
\[
I_{\mathrm{EH}} + \frac{\chi}{2}\pi N^{2} \;=\; -\frac{\Lambda\,\mathrm{Vol}}{8\pi G} + k\ell^{2}\int\Bigl(|W|^{2} + \tfrac83\Lambda^{2}\Bigr) \;=\; k\ell^{2}\int|W|^{2} + \Bigl(-\frac{\Lambda}{8\pi G} + \frac{3}{64\pi G\Lambda}\cdot\frac{8\Lambda^{2}}{3}\Bigr)\mathrm{Vol} \;=\; I_{\mathrm{MM}},
\]
using $I_{\mathrm{EH}} = -\tfrac{1}{16\pi G}\int(s - 2\Lambda) = -\Lambda\mathrm{Vol}/(8\pi G)$ on an Einstein space and $k\ell^{2}\cdot 32\pi^{2}\chi = \pi\ell^{2}\chi/(2G) = \tfrac{\chi}{2}\pi N^{2}$ with $N^{2} = \ell^{2}/G$ (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-entropy-pi-n-squared}: $N = M_{P}/H$, $H^{2} = \Lambda/3$). In units of $\pi N^{2}$, $I_{\mathrm{EH}} = -\Lambda^{2}\mathrm{Vol}/(24\pi^{2})$ and $I_{\mathrm{MM}} = \mathrm{Vol}\,|W|^{2}/(64\pi^{2})$, both rational once $\mathrm{Vol}/\pi^{2}$ is. The instantons are homogeneous, so $E$ and $|W|^{2}$ are constant on each and the Chern-Gauss-Bonnet theorem gives $\mathrm{Vol} = 32\pi^{2}\chi/E$; then $I_{\mathrm{MM}}/\pi N^{2} = \chi|W|^{2}/(2E)$ and $I_{\mathrm{EH}}/\pi N^{2} = -4\chi\Lambda^{2}/(3E)$, all scale invariant. The check builds each as a gauge field on $\Cl(4,0)$ and solves its rotation-gauge field from the torsion equation: the round $\Sph^{4}$ in the stereographic gauge $\hb^{-1}(e_{i}) = \tfrac{2}{1 + Q(x)}\,e_{i}$; $\Sph^{2}\times\Sph^{2}$ with one stereographic factor on $(e_{1}, e_{2})$ and one on $(e_{3}, e_{4})$; and $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ (Fubini-Study) in the gauge $f^{0} = \nabla r/(1 + r^{2})$, $f^{1,2} = r\sigma_{1,2}/(2\sqrt{1 + r^{2}})$, $f^{3} = r\sigma_{3}/(2(1 + r^{2}))$ with the left-invariant fields $\sigma_{l}$ of $SU(2)$ as in the Taub-NUT result, at a point where every value is rational. From the field strengths it finds the three fields Einstein ($\Lambda = 3, 1, 6$ in these normalisations), $\mathcal{Q}(F) = |W|^{2} = 0, \tfrac{16}{3}, 96$, $E = 24, 8, 192$ with $E = |W|^{2} + \tfrac83\Lambda^{2}$, and so, with $\chi = 2, 4, 3$, $I_{\mathrm{MM}}/\pi N^{2} = 0$, $\tfrac43$, $\tfrac34$ and $I_{\mathrm{EH}}/\pi N^{2} = -1$, $-\tfrac23$, $-\tfrac34$; the volumes this implies, $\tfrac83\pi^{2}$, $16\pi^{2}$ and $\tfrac12\pi^{2}$, are the standard ones (cited from memory). The pointwise identity $\mathcal{Q}(\mathcal{R} - \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}D) = |W|^{2}$ is also checked, in components, on a generic rational Weyl tensor (the Weyl part of a combination of Kulkarni-Nomizu products) at three values of $\Lambda$, both signs included.

\emph{(iii)} The promotion (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-henneaux-teitelboim-promotion}) replaces the fixed number $\ell^{2}$ by a field $\lambda$ and adds $-\int\lambda\,d\mathcal{T}$ with $\mathcal{T}$ a trivector field and $d\mathcal{T} = \nabla\wedge\mathcal{T}$ (a three-form in components); varying $\mathcal{T}$ gives $\nabla\lambda = 0$, which is the equation the norm mode of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws} lacked, and varying $\lambda$ gives $d\mathcal{T} = \partial L/\partial\lambda$, so $\mathcal{T}$ advances between two slices by the integral of $\partial L/\partial\lambda$ over the region between them. At fixed connection and frame, by (1) with $u = \ell^{2}$, $L = k\bigl(uE - 4s + 24u^{-1}\bigr)\mathrm{vol}$ and
\[
\frac{\partial L}{\partial u} \;=\; k\bigl(E - 24u^{-2}\bigr)\mathrm{vol} \;=\; k\bigl(\mathcal{Q}(F) + 4u^{-1}\,s(F)\bigr)\mathrm{vol},
\]
the second form by (1) and $s(F) = s(R) - 12u^{-1}$ (the identity is checked in exact arithmetic at two values of $u$ on a curvature tensor that is not Einstein). The frame equation of the Fact is, on $\Cl(4,0)$, the trivector-valued $2\,\partial_{b}\wedge F(I(a\wedge b)) = 2(\mathcal{G}(a) - \Lambda a)I = 0$ ($\epsilon_{abcd}\,e^{b}\wedge F^{cd} = 0$ in components), by $\partial_{b}\wedge\mathcal{R}(I(a\wedge b)) = \mathcal{G}(a)I$, $\partial_{b}\wedge(I(a\wedge b)) = -3aI$ and $F = \mathcal{R} - \ell^{-2}D = \mathcal{R} + \ell^{-2}\,\mathrm{id}$ (on $\Cl(1,3)$, where the de Sitter operator is $+\tfrac{\Lambda}{3}\,\mathrm{id}$, the same computation gives $2(\mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a)I$); the check evaluates the trivector on the three instantons and finds it zero. Traced with the frame it gives $\partial_{a}\cdot\mathcal{G}(a) - 4\Lambda = s(\mathcal{R}) - 4\Lambda = 0$, so $s(\mathcal{R}) = 12u^{-1}$ and $\mathcal{Q}(F, D) = 2s(F) = 0$ on shell, so the density is $k\,\mathcal{Q}(F) = k|W|^{2}$ by (ii), torsion-free solutions being Einstein with $\Lambda = 3/\ell^{2}$. If instead a rescaled frame $\hat e = e/f(u)$ is held fixed, the derivative changes by $\int (\delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}/\delta e^{a})\wedge f'(u)\hat e^{a}$, with $S_{\mathrm{tot}}$ the whole action (the matter action included when there is one), a multiple of the trace of the full frame equation, which vanishes on shell. The density $k(E - 24u^{-2})$ itself is obtained at fixed frame and connection and uses no field equation; only its reduction to $k\,\mathcal{Q}(F)$, and then to $k|W|^{2}$, uses the vacuum equations, through $s(F) = 0$ and $F = W$. For any other promoted variable $g(u)$ the term $-\int g\,d\mathcal{T}_{g}$ gives $d\mathcal{T}_{g} = \partial L/\partial g = (\partial L/\partial u)/g'(u)$, so its conjugate advances by the same integral divided by $g'(u)$; for $\Lambda = 3/u$ this is $(du/d\Lambda) = -3/\Lambda^{2}$ times it, and for the norm $Q(I) = \Lambda/3 = 1/u$ it is $-u^{2}$ times it. No choice is singled out; on each solution the conjugate times are proportional. In Lorentzian signature the same algebra holds with $\epsilon_{abcd}\epsilon^{efgh} = -\delta^{efgh}_{abcd}$, so the density is a multiple of $W_{abcd}W^{abcd}\sqrt{|g|}$.

\emph{(iv)} On a vacuum solution the density is $k|W|^{2}$ by (iii), so it vanishes on regions where the Weyl part of the field strength vanishes. A vacuum solution is Einstein with $\Lambda = 3/\ell^{2}$, and Einstein with $W = 0$ means the whole curvature is the de Sitter operator $\mathcal{R}(B) = \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}B$ of the store's sign on $\Cl(1,3)$ (not $\tfrac{\Lambda}{3}D$: $D = -\mathrm{id}$ is the Euclidean sphere's operator, and $-\tfrac{\Lambda}{3}\,\mathrm{id}$ on $\Cl(1,3)$ is anti-de Sitter), constant curvature, so such a region is locally de Sitter; the de Sitter slicings of FLRW form are among them. (Every FLRW field has vanishing Weyl part, its derived metric being conformally flat: in the comoving orthonormal frame its curvature has $R_{0i0j} = A\,\delta_{ij}$ and $R_{ijkl} = B\,D_{ijkl}$, so the electric and magnetic parts of $W$ are $SO(3)$-invariant symmetric trace-free tensors and vanish; the earlier check computes the Lorentzian Weyl tensor at three rational points $(a, \dot a, \ddot a, k)$ and finds it zero, and the GTG check finds the Weyl operator of the flat FLRW gauge field $\hb^{-1}(e_{i}) = a\,e_{i}$ zero at five instants. But an FLRW metric that is not de Sitter is not a vacuum solution, and on it the density is not $k|W|^{2}$: see (v).) On the leading Kasner term of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-datum-kasner-wall} the metric is Ricci-flat, so $W$ is the whole curvature and $|W|^{2}$ is the Kretschmann scalar $\bigl(4\sum_{i}p_{i}^{2}(p_{i} - 1)^{2} + 4\sum_{i<j}p_{i}^{2}p_{j}^{2}\bigr)\tau^{-4}$, which for $(\tfrac23, \tfrac23, -\tfrac13)$ is $\tfrac{64}{27}\tau^{-4}$, as that Proposition records (the GTG check computes $2\langle\mathcal{W}(a\wedge b)\mathcal{W}(\partial_{b}\wedge\partial_{a})\rangle$ from the Kasner gauge field $\hb^{-1}(e_{i}) = \tau^{p_{i}}e_{i}$ at $\tau = 1, 2, \tfrac13$ and finds it Ricci-flat with this value); with $\det(\hb)^{-1} = \tau^{p_{1}+p_{2}+p_{3}} = \tau$ the density is $\tfrac{64}{27}k\,\tau^{-3}$ and its integral from $\tau$ to a fixed $\tau_{0}$ grows as $\tau^{-2}$. The $\Lambda$-corrections are of relative order $\Lambda\tau^{2}$ by that Proposition and do not change the divergence. Under the Fact's identity $F = W$ on Einstein solutions this is exact, not only at leading order, wherever the solution is Einstein with the promoted $\Lambda$.

\emph{(v)} Under (Mat) the matter action does not depend on $u$ at fixed frame, connection and matter fields, so the variation in the multiplier gives the density $k(E - 24u^{-2})\mathrm{vol}$ of (iii) unchanged. The field equations of the functional plus the matter action are the Fact's equations with the matter source, Einstein's equations with $\Lambda = 3/\ell^{2}$ and stress tensor $T$ (the Gauss-Bonnet term contributes nothing to the Fact's Euler-Lagrange equations, which are linear in the source). Frame normalisation: in Lorentzian signature the functional is $-k(uE - 4s + 24u^{-1})\sqrt{|g|}$ plus the matter Lagrangian, the sign fixed by matching $4ks = s/(16\pi G)$ to the Einstein-Hilbert term; at fixed frame its $u$-derivative is $-k(E - 24u^{-2})\sqrt{|g|}$; holding the unit frame, $g = u\hat g$, the gravitational part gives $-k\,\mathcal{Q}(F)\sqrt{|g|}$ and the matter part gives $t\sqrt{|g|}/(2u)$, from $T^{ab} = (2/\sqrt{|g|})\,\partial(\sqrt{|g|}L_{m})/\partial g_{ab}$; the difference is $-(\sqrt{|g|}/u)\bigl(4k\,s(F) + t/2\bigr)$, which vanishes because $s(F) = s - 12u^{-1} = -8\pi G\,t$ is the trace of Einstein's equations. The check verifies the equality, and that the gravitational part alone differs from it whenever $t \neq 0$, at three FLRW points (units $8\pi G = 1$, $k = 1/8$).

In four dimensions the curvature decomposes into Weyl, trace-free Ricci and scalar parts, the Weyl tensor plus the Kulkarni-Nomizu products of $\Ric^{\mathrm{tf}}$ with $g$ and of $g$ with itself, the three parts orthogonal, and $E = |W|^{2} - 2|\Ric^{\mathrm{tf}}|^{2} + \tfrac16 s^{2}$, with norms taken with the Lorentzian metric (the check verifies this on a generic Lorentzian algebraic curvature tensor). Einstein's equations give, from their trace and trace-free parts, $s = 4\Lambda - 8\pi G\,t$ and $\Ric^{\mathrm{tf}} = 8\pi G\,T^{\mathrm{tf}}$, and $\tfrac16 s^{2} - \tfrac83\Lambda^{2} = -\tfrac43\Lambda(8\pi G\,t) + \tfrac16(8\pi G\,t)^{2}$, which is the first display; the check verifies it on the generic tensor with $T$ defined by Einstein's equations at three values of $\Lambda$. For flat FLRW, in the comoving orthonormal frame, $R_{0i0j} = -q\,\delta_{ij}$ and $R_{ijkl} = h\,D_{ijkl}$ with $h = H^{2}$ and $q = \ddot a/a$; then $|R|^{2} = 12(q^{2} + h^{2})$, $\Ric_{00} = -3q$, $\Ric_{ii} = q + 2h$, $s = 6(q + h)$, and $E = 36(q + h)^{2} - 4\bigl(9q^{2} + 3(q + 2h)^{2}\bigr) + 12(q^{2} + h^{2}) = 24hq$. Einstein's equations with $T = \mathrm{diag}(\rho, p, p, p)$ are the Friedmann equations $h = (\Lambda + \tilde\rho)/3$, $q = \Lambda/3 - (\tilde\rho + 3\tilde p)/6$, and
\[
24hq - \tfrac83\Lambda^{2} = \tfrac{4}{3}\bigl[(\Lambda + \tilde\rho)(2\Lambda - \tilde\rho - 3\tilde p) - 2\Lambda^{2}\bigr] = \tfrac43\bigl[\Lambda(\tilde\rho - 3\tilde p) - \tilde\rho(\tilde\rho + 3\tilde p)\bigr].
\]
In GTG the same values come from the flat FLRW gauge field with $\dot a/a = H$, $\ddot a/a = q$: the GTG check computes its field strength at five rational $(\Lambda, \tilde\rho, \tilde p)$ with $H^{2} = (\Lambda + \tilde\rho)/3$ and $q$ from the second Friedmann equation, finds the store-sign field equation $\mathcal{G}(a) + \Lambda a = -\tilde T(a)$ with $\tilde T(a) = (\tilde\rho + \tilde p)(a\cdot e_{0})e_{0} - \tilde p\,a$, $E = 24hq = \mathcal{Q}(\mathcal{R})$ and the display. The earlier check computes $E$ from the tensor, verifies both Einstein components from the same tensor, and verifies the display on the $3 \times 3 \times 3$ grid $\{\tfrac12, 3, -2\}^{3}$ of $(\Lambda, \tilde\rho, \tilde p)$; both sides have degree at most two in each variable, so agreement on three values per variable is the polynomial identity. Radiation ($\tilde p = \tilde\rho/3$) gives $-\tfrac83\tilde\rho^{2}$, and dust gives $\tfrac43\tilde\rho(\Lambda - \tilde\rho)$, positive for $0 < \tilde\rho < \Lambda$ and negative for $\tilde\rho > \Lambda$. Finally $(3k/\Lambda^{2})\bigl(-\tfrac43\Lambda\cdot 8\pi G\,t\bigr) = -t/(2\Lambda)$ with $k = 1/(64\pi G)$, and the remaining terms carry a further factor $G$; for dust $t = -\rho$, and $\int\rho\,\sqrt{|g|}\,d^{4}x$ is the sum over the dust's worldlines of rest mass times proper time.

\emph{Reading of (v) (argued, not part of the statement).} In a radiation era $\tilde\rho \propto a^{-4}$ and $H \propto a^{-2}$, so per comoving volume the advance between scale factors $a_{1} < a_{2}$ is proportional to $\int \tilde\rho^{2} a^{3}\,dt = \int \tilde\rho^{2}a^{2}H^{-1}\,da \propto \int a^{-4}\,da$, that is to $a_{1}^{-3} - a_{2}^{-3}$: the record is dominated by the earliest epoch. For dust after $8\pi G\rho = \Lambda$ the density changes sign, and as $\tilde\rho \to 0$ the advance per comoving volume tends to $\tfrac43 k\Lambda\,\tilde\rho\, a^{3}$ per unit cosmic time, a constant, since $\rho a^{3}$ is. The advance is therefore not monotone over a history with radiation and dust (negative before $8\pi G\rho_{m} \approx \Lambda$, positive after), so the conjugate variable is a record of the history and not a time coordinate that orders it. Against the Henneaux-Teitelboim clock of the Einstein-Hilbert action, which counts four-volume over $8\pi G$, the first-order term is that clock times $8\pi G\rho/(2\Lambda) = \rho/(2\rho_{\Lambda})$ with $\rho_{\Lambda} = \Lambda/8\pi G$.

\emph{The reading under (H).} If the weight of a value of the promoted $\Lambda$ is $e^{-I}$ summed over closed Einstein instantons, (ii) gives $e^{-I_{\mathrm{MM}}[\Sph^{4}]} = 1$ at every $\Lambda$ and $e^{-I_{\mathrm{MM}}[M]} = \exp\bigl(-\tfrac{3}{64\pi G\Lambda}\int|W|^{2}\bigr) < 1$ otherwise, with $\int|W|^{2}$ scale invariant, so these factors decrease as $\Lambda$ decreases. The Einstein-Hilbert weight of $\Sph^{4}$, $e^{\pi N^{2}}$, which is the factor used to argue for a vanishing cosmological constant (Baum, Hawking, Coleman; cited from memory), is multiplied here by $e^{-\pi N^{2}}$ from the Gauss-Bonnet term. So under (H) no factor of the action favours small $\Lambda$, and the measure is not supplied by the action. (H) itself, and the Euclidean continuation of the functional, are hypotheses of the reading, not results; the Euclidean value $I_{\mathrm{MM}}[\Sph^{4}] = 0$ is the Euclidean counterpart of the remark in Proposition \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-entropy-pi-n-squared} that the functional as written gives the horizon zero entropy.


\emph{Literature.} The identity $I_{\mathrm{MM}} = k\ell^{2}\int|W|^{2}$ on Einstein spaces is known for the Euler-regularised action of anti-de Sitter gravity, where it expresses the on-shell equivalence of that action with conformal gravity (O.~Miskovic and R.~Olea, ``Topological regularization and self-duality in four-dimensional anti-de Sitter gravity'', arXiv:0902.2082; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-miskovic-olea-identity}); the computation above is the de Sitter (Euclidean, positive $\Lambda$) form of the same algebra.

\emph{In components} (a labelled reading). In an orthonormal frame a curvature-type two-form is $X^{ab} = \tfrac12 X^{ab}{}_{ef}\,e^{e}\wedge e^{f}$, and in Euclidean signature $\epsilon_{abcd}\epsilon^{efgh} = \delta^{efgh}_{abcd}$ gives $\mathcal{Q}(X, Y) = \tfrac14\,\delta^{efgh}_{abcd}\,X^{ab}{}_{ef}\,Y^{cd}{}_{gh}$, with $E(X) = s(X)^{2} - 4|\Ric(X)|^{2} + |X|^{2}$, $D_{abcd} = \delta_{ac}\delta_{bd} - \delta_{ad}\delta_{bc}$ and $\delta^{efgh}_{abgh} = 2\delta^{ef}_{ab}$; in Lorentzian signature $\epsilon_{abcd}\epsilon^{efgh} = -\delta^{efgh}_{abcd}$, and the density is a multiple of $W_{abcd}W^{abcd}\sqrt{|g|}$. synthesis.quasi-free-deposit-has-white-e.formal:
Let $\CAR$ be the CAR algebra of the fermion modes on a slice, as in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.quasi-free-deposit-is-vacuum-plus-shot-noise}, and $\omega$ a homogeneous gauge-invariant quasi-free state (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-quasi-free-states-car-algebra}): its one-particle density is $E = \bigoplus_{p}E_{p}$, $0 \le E_{p} \le 1$, on the band space at momentum $p$, on which the one-particle Hamiltonian is $H_{p}$. For the cosine and sine moments $C$, $S$ of the energy density over a box of volume $V$ at wave vector $k$, with one-body form $\tfrac12(cH + Hc)$ as in clause (iv) of that theorem, put $S_{E}(k) = \lim_{V}(\mathrm{Var}\,C + \mathrm{Var}\,S)/V$, so that the contrast of the energy has spectrum $P_{\delta}(k) = S_{E}(k)/\bar\rho^{2}$. By clause (i) of that theorem,
\[
S_{E}(k) = \int\tr\bigl[\varepsilon_{k}(p)\,E_{p}\,\varepsilon_{k}(p)^{\dagger}\,(1 - E_{p + k})\bigr]\frac{d^{3}p}{(2\pi)^{3}}, \qquad \varepsilon_{k}(p) = \tfrac12(H_{p + k} + H_{p}),
\]
(averaged over $\pm k$ when the state is not symmetric under $k \mapsto -k$).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The white term.)} $S_{E}(0) = \int\tr[H_{p}E_{p}H_{p}(1 - E_{p})]\,d^{3}p/(2\pi)^{3} \ge 0$, and the integrand vanishes exactly when $H_{p}$ maps the range of $E_{p}$ into the eigenspace $E_{p} = 1$; where $H_{p}$ has no kernel, exactly when $E_{p}$ is a projection commuting with $H_{p}$. So $S_{E}(0) = 0$ if and only if the state is pure and stationary (up to zero modes of $H$); here stationary means $E_{p}H_{p} = H_{p}E_{p}$ for almost every $p$, invariance under the slice's one-particle dynamics generated by $H$, not under the cosmological evolution. The white term of the spectrum is $\lim_{k \to 0}S_{E}(k)$; it equals $S_{E}(0)$ when $E_{p}$ is continuous off a null set and the integrand is dominated, as for the filled ball of (iii), where the limit is zero linearly. The corresponding term of a momentum component is $\int p_{1}^{2}\tr[E_{p}(1 - E_{p})]\,d^{3}p/(2\pi)^{3}$, which vanishes exactly for pure states, stationary or not.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(One Weyl field, in $\Cl(3,0)$.)} Let the band space at $p$ be a minimal left ideal of $\Cl(3,0)$, with $H_{p}$ left multiplication by the vector $p$ (eigenvalues $\pm|p|$, spectral idempotents $P_{\pm}(p) = \tfrac12(1 \pm p/|p|)$), and $E_{p} = \tfrac12(\nu_{p} + \mu_{p})$ with a scalar $\nu_{p}$ and a vector $\mu_{p}$, $|\mu_{p}| \le \min(\nu_{p}, 2 - \nu_{p})$. Then
\[
\tr[H_{p}E_{p}H_{p}(1 - E_{p})] = \tfrac12\,p^{2}\bigl(\nu_{p}(2 - \nu_{p}) - \mu_{p}^{2}\bigr) + |p\wedge\mu_{p}|^{2}, \qquad \tr[E_{p}(1 - E_{p})] = \tfrac12\bigl(\nu_{p}(2 - \nu_{p}) - \mu_{p}^{2}\bigr),
\]
with $|p\wedge\mu|^{2} = p^{2}\mu^{2} - (p\cdot\mu)^{2}$. The first term is $p^{2}$ times $\sum n(1 - n)$ over the two eigen-occupations of $E_{p}$ and vanishes for pure states; the second is the squared bivector $p\wedge\mu_{p}$ and vanishes when $E_{p}$ commutes with $H_{p}$. Three classes: a stationary mixed state ($\mu \parallel p$, occupations $n$, $1 - n$ in $(0,1)$) has $2p^{2}n(1 - n)$ and momentum noise; a pure state of pairs ($\nu = 1$, $\mu = m$ a unit vector not parallel to $p$) has $|p\wedge m|^{2} = 4p^{2}n(1 - n)$, $n = \tfrac12(1 - m\cdot p/|p|)$, and no momentum noise; a pure stationary state ($E_{p} = P_{\pm}(p)$, $0$ or $1$) has neither.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The filled ball.)} For the Weyl field with the negative band filled and the positive band filled for $|p| \le k_{F}$, the excess of $S_{E}$ over the vacuum's (negative band filled; the difference of the two integrands is integrable) is, for $\ell = k/k_{F} \le 1$ ($k$ and $k_{F}$ in the same units), exactly
\[
S_{E}(k) - S_{E}^{\mathrm{vac}}(k) = \frac{k_{F}^{4}\,k}{8\pi^{2}}\Bigl(1 - \frac{\ell^{3}}{30} + \frac{\ell^{4}}{96}\Bigr),
\]
the sum of a particle-hole part $\tfrac{k_{F}^{5}}{4\pi^{2}}(\tfrac{\ell}{2} - \tfrac{\ell^{5}}{320})$ and minus the Pauli-blocked part $\tfrac{k_{F}^{5}}{4\pi^{2}}(\tfrac{\ell^{4}}{60} - \tfrac{\ell^{5}}{120})$ of the vacuum's pair term. With $\bar\rho = k_{F}^{4}/8\pi^{2}$ per field and $g$ independent fields filled alike, $\Delta^{2}_{\delta}(k) = k^{3}P_{\delta}/2\pi^{2} = \tfrac{4}{g}\ell^{4}(1 - \ell^{3}/30 + \ell^{4}/96)$. (For comparison, the number structure factor of one band with trivial overlap is $\tfrac34\ell - \tfrac1{16}\ell^{3}$ for $\ell \le 2$, and with the Weyl overlap its particle-hole part is $\tfrac34\ell - \tfrac{5}{32}\ell^{3}$ for $\ell \le 1$.)
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Index and amplitude on a slice of uniform expansion.)} Hypothesis (UE), a hypothesis of this clause and of (v) and (vi) and not a premise (the descent slice's expansion datum is left free): the descent slice expands uniformly, so that outside the descent's Hubble length the primordial curvature perturbation is $\zeta_{\infty} = \tfrac32X^{2}\delta$, $X = a_{d}H_{d}/k \gg 1$. This is the Poisson relation $(k/a)^{2}\psi = -4\pi G\rho\,\delta$ with the potential the curvature perturbation of the slice (reading (UE) of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.descent-slice-constraints-and-the-three-readings-of-a-white-deposit}, where the coefficient $\tfrac32$ is derived; only spectra enter below, so the sign convention of $\zeta$ plays no part). Named variant (UE$_{\Phi}$): the same potential read instead as the Bardeen potential of the growing solution, as in Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-string-gas-thermal-spectrum-and-conversion} with $\Phi = \tfrac23\mathcal{R}$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-large-scale-potential-and-sachs-wolfe-relations}); it gives $\zeta_{\infty} = \tfrac94X^{2}\delta$, every amplitude below multiplied by $\tfrac94$, and the same indices. Under (UE), $\Delta^{2}_{\zeta} = \tfrac94X^{4}\Delta^{2}_{\delta}$ and a contrast with $P_{\delta} \propto k^{s}$ gives $n_{s} - 1 = s - 1$: a state with white term gives $-1$, and the filled ball gives $\Delta^{2}_{\zeta} = \tfrac{9}{g}(H_{d}/k_{F})^{4}(1 - \ell^{3}/30 + \ell^{4}/96)$, so $n_{s} - 1 = -\tfrac{1}{10}\ell^{3} + O(\ell^{4})$ with $\ell = k/(a_{d}k_{F})$: $n_{s} = 1$ on observed scales, between $8.3$ and $8.4$ standard deviations from the measured $n_{s} - 1 = -0.0351 \pm 0.0042$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-planck-2018-lcdm-parameters}). If the filled fields carry the density, $3H_{d}^{2}\bar M_{P}^{2} = g k_{F}^{4}/8\pi^{2}$, the amplitude does not depend on $g$ or $k_{F}$:
\[
\Delta^{2}_{\zeta} = \frac{3H_{d}^{2}}{8\pi^{2}\bar M_{P}^{2}} = \frac{\rho}{8\pi^{2}\bar M_{P}^{4}} \qquad \bigl(\text{variant (UE}_{\Phi}\text{)}: \ \frac{27H_{d}^{2}}{32\pi^{2}\bar M_{P}^{2}}\bigr).
\]
Under (UE) it is between $3.5 \times 10^{-39}$ and $3.7 \times 10^{-39}$ at the energy density of a thermal bath at $7.3 \times 10^{8}$ GeV (the ceiling of the stored window; $g = 106.75$ there) and between $1.2 \times 10^{-26}$ and $1.3 \times 10^{-26}$ at that of $10^{12}$ GeV, more than $10^{17}$ below $A_{s}$; it equals $A_{s}$ at $\rho^{1/4}$ between $4.9 \times 10^{16}$ and $5.0 \times 10^{16}$ GeV ($H_{d}$ between $5.6 \times 10^{14}$ and $5.8 \times 10^{14}$ GeV), above the ceiling's energy scale by more than $2.7 \times 10^{7}$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Thermal smearing; computed in the proof.)} For the sea at temperature $T \ll k_{F}$ and $k \ll k_{F}$, $S_{E}(k) = S_{E}^{T = 0}(k)\,F(k/T)$ with $F(y) = 2\int_{0}^{1}\mu\operatorname{coth}(\tfrac12 y\mu)\,d\mu$: $F = 4/y + y/9 + \dots$ for $y \ll 1$ (white, $S_{E}(0) = 4\bar\rho T$) and $F = 1 + 2\pi^{2}/3y^{2}$ up to exponentially small terms for $y \gg 1$. Under (UE) the index is $-1$ for $k/a_{d} \ll 4T_{d}$ and $-2e/(1 + e)$, $e = 2\pi^{2}T_{d}^{2}a_{d}^{2}/3k^{2}$, above; the measured index is reached where $k/(a_{d}T_{d})$ is between $19.1$ and $19.3$, with running $dn_{s}/d\ln k = t(2 - t) = +0.06896799$ at $t = 0.0351$ (a white term added to a linear one, $S = S(0) + ck$, would give $t(1 - t) = +0.03386799$). So scale invariance on the observed band needs $a_{d}T_{d}$ well below the smallest observed wavenumber.
\item[(vi)] \emph{(The stored deposit; argued.)} Under the dynamics (L$_{E}$) permits, occupations are conserved (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.quadratic-flows-cannot-thermalise-descent}), so the entropy of a quasi-free deposit is the record's, and with entropy conserved from the descent (as in Proposition \claimref{synthesis.finite-range-descent-deposit-cannot-seed-cmb}(iii)) the stored thermal deposit has $k_{*}/(a_{d}T_{d}) < 2 \times 10^{-26}$ (the proof of clause (iv) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.quasi-free-deposit-is-vacuum-plus-shot-noise}): it is in the white regime of (v), $k_{*}/(4a_{d}T_{d}) < 5 \times 10^{-27}$, and a pure stationary deposit is excluded. A purification by partner modes on the slice removes the white term only if the joint state is pure and stationary, by (i): the partners degenerate with their modes in momentum and energy and each pair a superposition of one quantum in the mode or in the partner. Then the partners hold at least $1 - n_{p}$ quanta at every momentum the modes occupy, an energy density of at least $\int\omega_{p}(1 - n_{p})\,d^{3}p/(2\pi)^{3}$, which diverges for Fermi-Dirac occupations. The stored pair states, $c\ket{00} + s\ket{11}$ of a mode and a partner, are not stationary when both carry positive energy on the slice and keep a white term, $4\omega^{2}n(1 - n)$ per pair in the form of (ii). So for the stored deposit Hypothesis (UE) gives index $-1$, and the scale-invariant row of (iv) is a statement about a deposit that the stored state rules do not produce.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.quasi-free-deposit-has-white-e.technical:
The stored bound caps the long-range fluctuations of any quasi-free fermion deposit by its shot noise. Shot noise of the energy is white: its spectrum tends to a constant at long wavelengths. This result asks when that constant vanishes. The variance of the total energy in a large region is $\Tr(HEH(1 - E))$ per unit volume, and it has two sources that the Clifford form of a Weyl field separates: a term proportional to $n(1 - n)$, the mixedness of the occupations, and the squared bivector $p\wedge\mu$, which measures how far the state's polarisation $\mu$ is from the momentum, that is, how far the state is from stationary. Thermal deposits have the first; pure states of pairs, such as pair creation produces, have the second (and no momentum noise); only filled bands have neither.

For a filled ball the energy fluctuations at wave vector $k$ come from the shell of states that a shift by $k$ carries across the Fermi surface, a volume linear in $k$, and the bipolar integrals are polynomials: the excess over the vacuum is $\tfrac{k_{F}^{4}k}{8\pi^{2}}$ up to relative corrections $\ell^{3}/30$ from the Pauli blocking of vacuum pairs. A structure factor linear in $k$ is the hyperuniform class to which the scale-invariant spectrum belongs (literature, from memory): read on a slice of uniform expansion, Hypothesis (UE), it gives equal power per logarithmic interval, with no parameter. That is $n_{s} = 1$, the same value as the stored thermal reading with an area-law heat capacity, here from the algebra's own statistics; it misses the measured index by between $8.3$ and $8.4$ standard deviations. The amplitude is also parameter-free once the sea carries the density, $3H_{d}^{2}/8\pi^{2}\bar M_{P}^{2}$, and reaches the measured value only at an energy scale between $4.9 \times 10^{16}$ and $5.0 \times 10^{16}$ GeV, more than $2.7 \times 10^{7}$ above the energy scale of the stored window's ceiling. (UE) is one of the readings the series leaves open, not a premise; on a flat slice the same sea is blue.

The scale-invariant row needs the deposit to be pure on the observed scales themselves. At temperature $T$ the spectrum is white below $k \approx 4aT$; the measured tilt is crossed at $k/aT$ between $19.1$ and $19.3$ with a running of $t(2 - t) = 0.06896799$, a fit of one number with a large positive running. The stored deposit is thermal with the record's entropy, more than twenty-six orders inside the white regime, so under (UE) its index is $-1$ (argued, clause (vi)). The variance of the number in a sharp ball of radius $R$ grows as $R^{2}\ln R$; the logarithm belongs to the sharp boundary and not to the spectrum, which has no logarithm (argued). An occupied region whose boundary is not rectifiable would give a structure factor $\propto k^{3 - D}$, $D$ the box dimension of the boundary, and an index $2 - D$: the measured index for $D = 2.0351$, a fit of one number (argued).
synthesis.quasi-free-deposit-has-white-e.lay: Earlier work showed that the particles laid down at the universe's first event can only produce ripples as large as their own random counting noise. This result looks at the long-wavelength part of that noise. It shows that the noise in the energy has two independent causes, heat and the creation of particle pairs, and that it disappears at long wavelengths only for a perfectly cold, perfectly still sea of particles filling every state up to a maximum momentum. Such a sea has a particular property: read through one assumed link between matter and gravitational potential (one of the readings the series leaves open), it gives ripples of equal strength on every scale, with no adjustable number. That is close to what is observed, but not it: the observed ripples are slightly stronger on large scales, and the difference is more than eight times the measurement's uncertainty. The sea would also have to be far denser than the theory's first event allows, and it would have to be free of heat on the scale of the whole visible universe, whereas the event the theory describes is hot. For a hot deposit the same assumed link gives ripples that grow in proportion to the scale, which is not observed either.

u \pm |\mu|)$. The three classes follow: for $\mu = (2n - 1)p/|p|$, $
u = 1$, the first term is $	frac12p^{2}(1 - (2n - 1)^{2}) = 2p^{2}n(1 - n)$ and the second vanishes; for $
u = 1$ and a unit vector $m$ the first vanishes and $|p\wedge m|^{2} = p^{2}(1 - \cos^{2}\vartheta) = 4p^{2}n(1 - n)$ with $n = 	frac12(1 - \cos\vartheta)$ the weight of $P_{-}(p)$ in the state, a superposition of the two energy levels at each $p$, that is, of the filled level and a pair; for $E_{p} = P_{\pm}(p)$ both vanish. The check verifies the two identities and the three classes in $\Cl(3,0)$ with rational data.

\emph{(iii)} With $E_{p} = P_{-}(p) + 	heta(k_{F} - |p|)P_{+}(p)$, $1 - E_{p + k} = 	heta(|p + k| - k_{F})P_{+}(p + k)$. Put $r_{1} = |p|$, $r_{2} = |p + k|$, $\vartheta$ the angle between $p$ and $p + k$, and $\varepsilon = 	frac12(p + (p + k))$, a vector. Since $P_{+}(q)\,\varepsilon\,P_{\pm}(p) = 	frac12(r_{2} \pm r_{1})P_{+}(q)P_{\pm}(p)$ for $q = p + k$ and $	r[P_{+}(q)P_{\pm}(p)] = 	frac12(1 \pm \cos\vartheta)$, the integrand is $	frac14(r_{1} + r_{2})^{2}	frac12(1 + \cos\vartheta)$ on the lune $r_{1} \le k_{F} < r_{2}$ (particle to particle) plus $	frac14(r_{2} - r_{1})^{2}	frac12(1 - \cos\vartheta)$ on $r_{2} > k_{F}$ (sea to particle). The second, over all $p$, is the vacuum's integrand; the state's differs from it by minus its restriction to the blocked region $r_{2} \le k_{F}$, a bounded region. In bipolar coordinates $d^{3}p = (2\pi/k)\,r_{1}r_{2}\,dr_{1}dr_{2}$ on $|r_{1} - r_{2}| \le k \le r_{1} + r_{2}$, and $r_{1}r_{2}\cos\vartheta = 	frac12(r_{1}^{2} + r_{2}^{2} - k^{2})$, so both integrands are polynomials in $(r_{1}, r_{2})$: for $k \le k_{F}$ the lune is $k_{F} - k \le r_{1} \le k_{F}$, $k_{F} \le r_{2} \le r_{1} + k$, and the blocked region is $0 \le r_{2} \le k_{F}$, $|r_{2} - k| \le r_{1} \le r_{2} + k$. The integrals are $2\pi k_{F}^{5}(	frac{\ell}{2} - 	frac{\ell^{5}}{320})$ and $2\pi k_{F}^{5}(	frac{\ell^{4}}{60} - 	frac{\ell^{5}}{120})$; dividing by $(2\pi)^{3}$ and subtracting gives the display. (For the blocked part with $r_{2} \ge k$: $\int_{-k}^{k}t^{2}(k^{2} - t^{2})\,dt = 	frac{4}{15}k^{5}$ in $t = r_{1} - r_{2}$, which gives the leading $\ell^{4}/60$.) The mean density is $\int_{|p| \le k_{F}}|p|\,d^{3}p/(2\pi)^{3} = k_{F}^{4}/8\pi^{2}$. For $g$ independent fields the variances and the densities add, so $P_{\delta} = S_{E}/(g arho_{1}^{2})$ and $\Delta^{2}_{\delta} = 	frac{k^{3}}{2\pi^{2}}\cdot	frac{8\pi^{2}k}{g\,k_{F}^{4}}(\dots) = 	frac{4}{g}\ell^{4}(\dots)$. The check verifies the overlaps in $\Cl(3,0)$ on rational vectors of rational length and the integrals exactly at rational $k$, with the number structure factors quoted for comparison.

\emph{(iv)} Under (UE), $\Delta^{2}_{\zeta} = 	frac94X^{4}\Delta^{2}_{\delta}$ with $X = a_{d}H_{d}/k$, and $\Delta^{2}_{\delta} \propto k^{3 + s}$ gives $n_{s} - 1 = s - 1$. The coefficient: the energy constraint on a slice whose expansion is uniform is the Poisson relation, and with $4\pi Gho = 	frac32H^{2}$ it gives the slice a curvature perturbation $\psi = -	frac32X^{2}\delta$, which is the conserved amplitude up to sign and up to relative corrections of order $X^{-4}$ and a velocity term smaller by $1/X$ (derived in Proposition \claimref{synthesis.descent-slice-constraints-and-the-three-readings-of-a-white-deposit}(iii) and (iv); here it is the content of the hypothesis). In the variant (UE$_{\Phi}$) the same potential is read as the growing solution's Bardeen potential $\Phi$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-string-gas-thermal-spectrum-and-conversion}), and $\mathcal{R} = 	frac32\Phi$ in the radiation field (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-large-scale-potential-and-sachs-wolfe-relations}) gives the coefficient $	frac94$ in place of $	frac32$, so spectra larger by $(	frac32)^{2} = 	frac94$. For the ball, with physical $k_{F}$ and $\ell = k/(a_{d}k_{F})$, $X^{4}\ell^{4} = (H_{d}/k_{F})^{4}$, so $	frac94X^{4}\cdot	frac4g\ell^{4} = 	frac9g(H_{d}/k_{F})^{4}$, and $d\ln(1 - \ell^{3}/30 + \ell^{4}/96)/d\ln\ell = -\ell^{3}/10 + O(\ell^{4})$. On observed scales $\ell$ is of order $10^{-26}$ for a sea that carries the density and is followed by a radiation history (argued: $k_{F}$ is of the order of the temperature of a bath of the same density, for which $k_{*}/(a_{d}T_{d}) < 2 	imes 10^{-26}$ by the stored bracket), so the correction $\ell^{3}/10$ to the index is far below any measurable level. The measured index is $-0.0351 \pm 0.0042$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-planck-2018-lcdm-parameters}) and $0.0351/0.0042$ is between $8.3$ and $8.4$. With $ho = gk_{F}^{4}/8\pi^{2} = 3H_{d}^{2} ar M_{P}^{2}$, $	frac4g(H_{d}/k_{F})^{4} = 	frac4g H_{d}^{2}\cdot	frac{ho}{3 ar M_{P}^{2}}\cdot	frac{g}{8\pi^{2}ho} = H_{d}^{2}/(6\pi^{2} ar M_{P}^{2})$, and $	frac94$ of it is $3H_{d}^{2}/(8\pi^{2} ar M_{P}^{2}) = ho/(8\pi^{2} ar M_{P}^{4})$; the variant has $	frac94$ of that, $27H_{d}^{2}/(32\pi^{2} ar M_{P}^{2})$. Labelling a density by the temperature of a thermal bath of that density, $ho = 	frac{\pi^{2}}{30}g_{*}T^{4}$, gives $ho/(8\pi^{2} ar M_{P}^{4}) = 	frac{g_{*}}{240}(T/ ar M_{P})^{4}$, in which $\pi$ has cancelled; the check evaluates it at $7.3 	imes 10^{8}$ GeV and $10^{12}$ GeV with $g_{*} = 106.75$ and $ ar M_{P} = 2.435 	imes 10^{18}$ GeV, and brackets the density at which it equals $A_{s} = 2.1 	imes 10^{-9}$, $ho = 8\pi^{2}A_{s} ar M_{P}^{4}$, with $333/106 < \pi < 355/113$.

\emph{(v)} For $T \ll k_{F}$ and $k \ll k_{F}$ the occupations vary only near the Fermi surface, where the energies in $\varepsilon$ are $k_{F}$ and the overlap is $1$, so $S_{E} = k_{F}^{2}\int n_{p}(1 - n_{p + k})\,d^{3}p/(2\pi)^{3}$ with $n$ the Fermi-Dirac function of $|p| - k_{F}$. With $\mu$ the cosine of the angle between $p$ and $k$, $|p + k| - |p| = k\mu$, and $\int n(\epsilon)(1 - n(\epsilon + \Delta))\,d\epsilon = \Delta/(1 - e^{-\Delta/T})$, since $n(\epsilon)(1 - n(\epsilon + \Delta)) = [n(\epsilon) - n(\epsilon + \Delta)]/(1 - e^{-\Delta/T})$ (an identity of rational functions of $e^{\epsilon/T}$, in the check) and $\int[n(\epsilon) - n(\epsilon + \Delta)]\,d\epsilon = \Delta$. So $S_{E} = 	frac{k_{F}^{4}}{4\pi^{2}}\int_{-1}^{1}	frac{k\mu}{1 - e^{-k\mu/T}}\,d\mu = 	frac{k_{F}^{4}k}{4\pi^{2}}\int_{0}^{1}\mu\operatorname{coth}	frac{k\mu}{2T}\,d\mu$, which is $	frac{k_{F}^{4}k}{8\pi^{2}}F(k/T)$. For $y \ll 1$, $\operatorname{coth} z = 1/z + z/3 + \dots$ gives $F = 4/y + y/9$; so $S_{E}(0) = 	frac{k_{F}^{4}}{2\pi^{2}}T = 4 arho T$, in agreement with (i) ($\int\omega^{2}n(1 - n) = 4T arho$ for massless quanta). For $y \gg 1$, $F = 1 + 2\int_{0}^{1}\mu(\operatorname{coth}	frac{y\mu}{2} - 1)\,d\mu = 1 + 	frac{8}{y^{2}}\int_{0}^{y/2}z(\operatorname{coth} z - 1)\,dz$, and $\int_{0}^{\infty}z(\operatorname{coth} z - 1)\,dz = 2\sum_{n \ge 1}\int_{0}^{\infty}ze^{-2nz}dz = 	frac12\zeta(2) = \pi^{2}/12$, the remainder being exponentially small: $F = 1 + 2\pi^{2}/3y^{2}$. Under (UE) the index is $d\ln F/d\ln y$: $-1 + y^{2}/18$ at small $y$, and with $e = 2\pi^{2}/3y^{2}$, $de/d\ln y = -2e$, it is $-2e/(1 + e)$ at large $y$, with derivative $4e/(1 + e)^{2}$. Setting $-2e/(1 + e) = -t$ gives $e = t/(2 - t)$, $1 + e = 2/(2 - t)$ and running $t(2 - t)$; at $t = 0.0351$, $e = 0.01786$, $y = (2\pi^{2}/3e)^{1/2}$ between $19.1$ and $19.3$, where the exponential remainder is below $10^{-7}$. For $S = S(0) + ck$ the index is $-f$ with $f = S(0)/(S(0) + ck)$ and $df/d\ln k = -f(1 - f)$, running $f(1 - f)$.

\emph{(vi) (Argued.)} A quasi-free state's entropy is $-\Tr[E\ln E + (1 - E)\ln(1 - E)]$, a function of the spectrum of $E$, which quadratic flows and the number-diagonal generators that (L$_{E}$) permits conserve (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.quadratic-flows-cannot-thermalise-descent}(i), (ii)). So a deposit that becomes today's radiation under those dynamics has the record's entropy at the descent, and the stored relation $a_{d}T_{d}\,g_{s}^{1/3} = a_{0}T_{0}\,g_{s0}^{1/3}$ (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.finite-range-descent-deposit-cannot-seed-cmb}(iii)) with $k_{*}/(a_{0}T_{0}) < 1.37 	imes 10^{-27}$ and $g_{s} \le 10^{4}$ gives $k_{*}/(a_{d}T_{d}) < 14 	imes 1.37 	imes 10^{-27} < 2 	imes 10^{-26}$ (the bracket of the stored proof of clause (iv) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.quasi-free-deposit-is-vacuum-plus-shot-noise}). By (v) the white regime is $k/a_{d} \ll 4T_{d}$; at the pivot $k_{*}/(4a_{d}T_{d}) < 5 	imes 10^{-27}$ (the check recomputes $k_{*}/(a_{0}T_{0})$ from the record values and the factor $(g_{s}/g_{s0})^{1/3} < 14$), so the observed band is inside it by more than twenty-six orders. A purification of the occupations by partner modes on the slice is a pure quasi-free state of modes and partners together, and by (i) its white term vanishes exactly when its one-particle density is a projection commuting with the joint one-particle Hamiltonian. A homogeneous state mixes a mode only with partners at the same momentum, and a projection that commutes with the Hamiltonian mixes only levels of equal energy; so the partners are degenerate with their modes, the joint density at $p$ is a projection $E_{p}$ of rank $r_{p} \ge 1$ on the degenerate band space wherever the mode's occupation $n_{p} = \langle 1|E_{p}|1angle$ is strictly between $0$ and $1$, and the partners' occupations sum to $r_{p} - n_{p} \ge 1 - n_{p}$. Their energy density is then at least $\int\omega_{p}(1 - n_{p})\,d^{3}p/(2\pi)^{3}$ over the momenta the modes occupy, which diverges for Fermi-Dirac occupations (positive at every momentum). The pair states of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.quadratic-flows-cannot-thermalise-descent}(iii), $c\ket{00} + s\ket{11}$, superpose levels whose energies differ by the sum of the two one-particle energies; with both positive on the slice the state is not stationary, and in the Weyl form of (ii) its white term is $4p^{2}n(1 - n)$ per momentum, twice the mixed state's $2p^{2}n(1 - n)$.
\end{proof}
