synthesis.sparse-fermion-deposit-reaches.formal:
\emph{Setting.} Units $\hbar = c = 1$. As in Proposition \claimref{synthesis.quasi-free-deposit-is-vacuum-plus-shot-noise}(iv), let the deposit on the descent slice be a homogeneous gauge-invariant quasi-free state of fermion modes with one-particle energies $\omega_{p} \ge |p|$ (one energy for the $g$ internal states at each momentum), let $x_{p} = \Tr X_{p}$ be its density of quanta at momentum $p$ above the descended vacuum ($X_{E} = (E - E_{0})^{2} + E(1 - E) = \bigoplus_{p}X_{p}$, the trace over the $g$ internal states at each momentum), and let $\rho_{F} = \int\omega_{p}x_{p}\,d^{3}p/(2\pi)^{3} = f\rho$ be the energy density it carries, a share $f \le 1$ of the total density $\rho$ at the descent. All quantities are physical ones at the descent: $k_{d} = k/a_{d}$ is the physical wavenumber of the comoving mode $k$, $X = H_{d}/k_{d} = a_{d}H_{d}/k$, the descended field is the spatially flat radiation-dominated one with $H_{d}^{2} = \tfrac{8\pi G}{3}\rho$, and $M_{H} = \tfrac{4\pi}{3}\rho H_{d}^{-3} = 1/(2GH_{d})$ is the Hubble mass. Write $\omega_{\max}$ for the supremum of $\omega_{p}$ over the support of $x_{p}$, and
\[
s(k_{d}) = \frac{3k_{d}^{3}}{2\pi^{2}\rho^{2}}\int(\omega_{p} + k_{d})^{2}x_{p}\,\frac{d^{3}p}{(2\pi)^{3}}
\]
for the shot term of the cited clause, for the deposit's contribution $\delta$ to the contrast of the total density: $\Delta_{\delta}^{2}(k)^{1/2} \le \Delta_{\delta,\mathrm{vac}}^{2}(k)^{1/2} + s(k_{d})^{1/2}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The exclusion principle counts the soft quanta.)} $0 \le X_{p} \le 1$, so $x_{p} \le g$; the quanta with $\omega_{p} < k_{d}$ number at most $gk_{d}^{3}/6\pi^{2}$ per unit volume; and
\[
\int(\omega_{p} + k_{d})^{2}x_{p}\,\frac{d^{3}p}{(2\pi)^{3}} \;\le\; (\omega_{\max} + k_{d})\Bigl(2\rho_{F} + \frac{gk_{d}^{4}}{6\pi^{2}}\Bigr).
\]
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The shot term in Hubble masses.)} With $\eta = gk_{d}^{4}/(6\pi^{2}\rho) = 4gGH_{d}^{2}/(9\pi X^{4})$,
\[
s(k_{d}) \;\le\; \frac{2(2f + \eta)}{\pi}\,\frac{1}{X^{3}}\,\frac{\omega_{\max} + k_{d}}{M_{H}}.
\]
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Momentum noise.)} Let $v$ be the longitudinal part of the deposit's momentum density divided by $\rho + p = \tfrac43\rho$, its longitudinal velocity relative to the slice normal. Its shot term obeys the same bound as the energy's: $\Delta_{v}^{2}(k)^{1/2} \le \Delta_{v,\mathrm{vac}}^{2}(k)^{1/2} + \tfrac34 s(k_{d})^{1/2}$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(What an amplitude needs.)} Let the conserved curvature perturbation outside the Hubble length be $\mathcal{R} = \alpha\,\delta + \beta\,v$, with coefficients depending on $X$ alone, $v$ being the velocity of (iii); only $|\alpha|$ and $|\beta|$ enter, so the sign convention of $\mathcal{R}$ plays no part here ($\mathcal{R}$ is minus the $\zeta_{\infty}$ of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.descent-slice-constraints-and-the-three-readings-of-a-white-deposit}). Then $\Delta_{\mathcal{R}}^{2}(k)^{1/2} \le |\alpha|\,\Delta_{\delta,\mathrm{vac}}^{2}(k)^{1/2} + |\beta|\,\Delta_{v,\mathrm{vac}}^{2}(k)^{1/2} + D(k)$ with $D = (|\alpha| + \tfrac34|\beta|)\,s^{1/2}$ the part the deposit's quanta can carry. Three readings of the descent slice in the radiation era, with the coefficients of that Proposition to leading order in $1/X$, each a hypothesis here and none adopted: (FR) flat slice with the deposit at rest on it, $v = 0$ on the slice: $|\alpha| = \tfrac14$, $D = \tfrac14 s^{1/2}$; (FM) flat slice with the deposit's own longitudinal momentum noise: $|\alpha| = \tfrac14$, $|\beta| = 2X$, $D = \tfrac14(1 + 6X)s^{1/2}$; (UE) slice of uniform expansion: $|\alpha| = \tfrac32X^{2}$, $|\beta| = 2X$ (the velocity enters with $2X$ on every slice and is subleading here by $1/X$), $D = \tfrac32X^{2}(1 + 1/X)s^{1/2}$. By (ii), $D(k)^{2} \ge A$ requires
\[
\frac{\omega_{\max} + k_{d}}{M_{H}} \;\ge\; \frac{8\pi AX^{3}}{2f + \eta}\ \ \text{(FR)}, \qquad \frac{8\pi AX^{3}}{(2f + \eta)(1 + 6X)^{2}}\ \ \text{(FM)}, \qquad \frac{2\pi A}{9(2f + \eta)X(1 + 1/X)^{2}}\ \ \text{(UE)}.
\]
\item[(v)] \emph{(Numbers.)} Take $k = a_{0}H_{0}$, the largest observed scale, and $A = 2.0 \times 10^{-9}$, the lower record value of $A_{s}$ at the pivot (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-planck-2018-lcdm-parameters}), which the measured red spectrum exceeds at larger scales, and the stored $X > 4.96 \times 10^{7}$ at $T_{d} = 1$ MeV and $X > 7.27 \times 10^{22}$ at $T_{d} = 10^{12}$ GeV (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.finite-range-descent-deposit-cannot-seed-cmb}(iii), with its $g_{*} = 10.75$ and $106.75$ and the reduced Planck mass $\bar M_{P} = 2.435 \times 10^{18}$ GeV); $f \le 1$ and $\eta < 10^{-20}$. Under (FR) some quantum has $\omega_{\max} > 3.0 \times 10^{15}\,M_{H}$ at $1$ MeV and $> 9.6 \times 10^{60}\,M_{H}$ at $10^{12}$ GeV; equivalently a white contrast reaching $16A$ at $X$ is $16AX^{3} > 3.9 \times 10^{15}$ at the descent's Hubble scale. Under (FM) $\omega_{\max} > 0.034\,M_{H}$ at $1$ MeV and $> 5.0 \times 10^{13}\,M_{H}$ at $10^{12}$ GeV, which with $M_{H}/\bar M_{P} = 4\sqrt{90/g_{*}}\,(\bar M_{P}/T_{d})^{2}$ is more than $2.3 \times 10^{42}$ and $1.1 \times 10^{27}$ reduced Planck masses; the (FM) bound in Hubble masses increases with $X$, and in Planck masses it is least at the top of the window (argued between the two ends, where no stored bracket of $X$ is available: it is proportional to $a_{d}$). The bounds are stated for $f \le 1$; a smaller share raises them, in proportion to $1/f$ once $\eta$ is neglected. Under (UE) the condition is weak: at the pivot at $T_{d} = 10^{12}$ GeV ($X > 3.2 \times 10^{20}$, $A \le 2.2 \times 10^{-9}$, $f = 1$) it reads $\omega_{\max} + k_{d} \ge c\,M_{H}$ with $c < 2.5 \times 10^{-30}$, while $T_{d} > 10^{-20}\,M_{H}$ there, so quanta of thermal energy meet it with more than nine orders to spare (the factor $(1 + 1/X)^{-2}$ only lowers the threshold).
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the number of quanta of a deposit that does not conserve entropy is fixed by the energy budget of the descent, not by the record of the entropy: a quasi-free fermion deposit whose shot noise reaches the measured amplitude at the present Hubble scale under a flat-slice reading contains a quantum of more than $1.1 \times 10^{27}$ reduced Planck masses under (FM), at both ends of the window and for every share of the density, and a quantum of more than $3.0 \times 10^{15}$ Hubble masses under (FR). \emph{Hypothesis (QP).} The quanta of the deposit have energies below the Planck mass. (QP) is a hypothesis of this result only; it is not a stored premise and is not part of Premise (HD). Its motivation (argued): a quantum with $G\omega^{2} \gg 1$ has a gravitational radius far above its wavelength and is not a quantum of a test field on a Robertson-Walker collar of the descent, and under (FR) the contrast would in addition be far above one at the Hubble scale. \emph{Given (QP)}, a sparse or energetically broad quasi-free fermion deposit does not carry the measured amplitude under (FR) or under (FM): attack item 3 of the open problem is closed under the two flat-slice readings. Under (UE) it is open: the count excludes nothing there, and a deposit is bounded by the shape of its spectrum on the observed band, which this result does not address. No reading of the slice is adopted.
synthesis.sparse-fermion-deposit-reaches.technical: The stored shot-noise bound removes dense quasi-free deposits and leaves sparse or energetically broad ones, because the bound scales inversely with the number of quanta and the record of the entropy does not fix that number for a deposit that reaches today's radiation by producing entropy. The number is fixed another way. The total density at the descent is known from the Friedmann relation at the reheating temperature, so a deposit with few quanta has much energy in each. The stored shot term is an integral of $(\omega + k_{d})^{2}$ over the quanta. It is at most the largest quantum energy times the integral of $\omega + k_{d}$, and the second integral is the energy density plus $k_{d}$ times the number density; the exclusion principle bounds the number of quanta softer than $k_{d}$ by the number of modes in the momentum ball of radius $k_{d}$, which is negligible, and the harder ones contribute at most the energy density again. Dividing by the square of the density and using the Friedmann relation turns the bound into the energy of the hardest quantum in Hubble masses, divided by the cube of the factor by which the mode lies outside the Hubble length. The same holds for the momentum density, whose one-body form obeys the same inequality mode by mode. How much shot noise an amplitude needs depends on how the contrast converts into the curvature perturbation, which depends on the descent slice; the series leaves the slice free, so three readings are carried as hypotheses, with the coefficients of the result on the slice's constraints (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.descent-slice-constraints-and-the-three-readings-of-a-white-deposit}). On a flat slice with the deposit at rest the curvature perturbation is a quarter of the contrast, and the measured amplitude at the present Hubble scale needs a quantum of more than $10^{15}$ Hubble masses: the white contrast would be far above one at the descent's Hubble scale, which is the stored finite-range obstruction seen from the side of the quanta. On a flat slice with the deposit's own momentum noise the conversion gains a factor of the order of the distance outside the Hubble length, and the largest quantum needed is a few percent of a Hubble mass at $1$ MeV, rising with the temperature in Hubble masses and above $10^{27}$ reduced Planck masses at the top of the window, where it is least: a lump of the mass scale of the Hubble volume. Given the hypothesis (QP) that the deposit's quanta lie below the Planck mass, both flat-slice readings are closed. On a slice of uniform expansion the conversion gains the fourth power in the spectrum, the condition falls far below thermal energies at the top of the window, and the count is no obstruction: under (UE) the item stays open, and that reading has to be confronted through the shape of the spectrum instead.
synthesis.sparse-fermion-deposit-reaches.lay: One loophole in the earlier result was a deposit with very few particles: few particles means large random variation from place to place, perhaps as large as the measured ripples. But the total energy of the newborn universe is known, so few particles means that some of them carry an enormous energy. Working this out, a deposit sparse enough to make the measured ripples would need some particles weighing more than a billion billion billion Planck masses: a sizeable fraction of, or more than, the mass inside the Hubble region at that time. Such objects would behave as black holes rather than particles (argued). So, if one assumes that the particles of the deposit are lighter than the Planck mass, the loophole closes, provided the ripples are read off the deposit with space taken to be flat region by region. There is another way of reading them, in which the geometry of space rather than the expansion rate takes up the unevenness of the deposit; in that reading the argument does not close the loophole, which stays open, and the question becomes whether the pattern has the right dependence on scale. The theory does not say which reading holds.

proofs.main:
(i) $X_{E} = (E - E_{0})^{2} + E(1 - E)$ is the system block of $(\widetilde E - \widetilde E_{0})^{2}$ for a purification (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.quasi-free-deposit-is-vacuum-plus-shot-noise}(ii)); the difference of two projectors has norm at most one, so $0 \le X_{E} \le 1$, and on the $g$-dimensional internal space at momentum $p$ this gives $x_{p} = \Tr X_{p} \le g$. Since $\omega_{p} \ge |p|$, the quanta with $\omega_{p} < k_{d}$ have $|p| < k_{d}$, and their density is at most $g\int_{|p| < k_{d}}d^{3}p/(2\pi)^{3} = gk_{d}^{3}/6\pi^{2}$. Write $\bar n = \int x_{p}$ for the density of quanta. On the support of $x$, $(\omega_{p} + k_{d})^{2} \le (\omega_{\max} + k_{d})(\omega_{p} + k_{d})$, so the integral is at most $(\omega_{\max} + k_{d})(\rho_{F} + k_{d}\bar n)$; and $k_{d}\bar n \le k_{d}\cdot gk_{d}^{3}/6\pi^{2} + \rho_{F}$, the first term from the quanta with $\omega_{p} < k_{d}$ and the second because $k_{d} x_{p} \le \omega_{p}x_{p}$ on the others. The factor $2$ is attained by quanta all at $\omega = k_{d}$. The check verifies $0 \le X_{E} \le 1$ and the trace formula on rational samples with non-commuting $E$ and $E_{0}$ (signatures by exact congruence), and the three inequalities on a cubic momentum grid for five occupation profiles, three masses and four values of $k_{d}$.

(ii) Insert (i) in the definition of $s$ with $\rho_{F} = f\rho$: $s \le \tfrac{3k_{d}^{3}}{2\pi^{2}\rho}(\omega_{\max} + k_{d})(2f + \eta)$. With $k_{d} = H_{d}/X$ and $M_{H} = 4\pi\rho/(3H_{d}^{3})$, $k_{d}^{3}/\rho = 4\pi/(3X^{3}M_{H})$, which gives the display; and $k_{d}^{4}/\rho = H_{d}^{4}/(X^{4}\rho) = 8\pi GH_{d}^{2}/(3X^{4})$ gives $\eta$. The check verifies both as rational identities with $\pi$ replaced by three rational values. Since $GH_{d}^{2} = (H_{d}/\bar M_{P})^{2}/8\pi$ is far below one in the window and $X > 10^{7}$, $\eta < 10^{-20}$ for any $g \le 10^{4}$.

(iii) The longitudinal part of the momentum density is that of the canonical one, since the symmetric momentum density differs from it by the curl of the spin density. Its cosine moment is the one-body observable with $f_{P} = \tfrac12(c\,p_{L} + p_{L}\,c)$, $c$ the multiplication by $\cos(\vec k\cdot\vec x)$ and $p_{L}$ the momentum along $\vec k$. As for the energy in the cited clause (iv), $f_{P}^{2} \le \tfrac12(c\,p_{L}^{2}\,c + p_{L}^{2})$, whose momentum-diagonal part is $\tfrac12\bigl(\tfrac14((p_{L} + k_{d})^{2} + (p_{L} - k_{d})^{2}) + p_{L}^{2}\bigr) = \tfrac34p_{L}^{2} + \tfrac14k_{d}^{2} \le \tfrac34(\omega_{p} + k_{d})^{2}$ because $|p_{L}| \le |p| \le \omega_{p}$. This is the bound the cited proof uses for the energy moment, so the cited clause (ii) gives the same shot term for the moments of the momentum density as for those of the energy density; dividing by $(\rho + p)^{2} = \tfrac{16}{9}\rho^{2}$ in place of $\rho^{2}$ gives the factor $\tfrac34$ in the amplitude.

(iv) The spectrum of a sum is bounded by the triangle inequality for standard deviations of the cosine and sine moments, as in the cited proof, so $\Delta_{\mathcal{R}}^{1/2} \le |\alpha|\Delta_{\delta}^{1/2} + |\beta|\Delta_{v}^{1/2}$, and the cited bound and (iii) give the display with $D = (|\alpha| + \tfrac34|\beta|)s^{1/2}$. For (FM), $\tfrac14 + 2X\cdot\tfrac34 = \tfrac14(1 + 6X)$. Solving $D^{2} \ge A$ with (ii): $s \ge 16A$ and $s \ge 16A/(1 + 6X)^{2}$ for (FR) and (FM), and $s \le \tfrac{2(2f + \eta)}{\pi X^{3}}(\omega_{\max} + k_{d})/M_{H}$ gives the first two thresholds. For (UE), $\tfrac32X^{2} + \tfrac34\cdot2X = \tfrac32X^{2}(1 + 1/X)$, and $s \ge 4A/(9X^{4}(1 + 1/X)^{2})$ gives the third. The coefficients $|\alpha|$ and $|\beta|$ of the three readings are those of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.descent-slice-constraints-and-the-three-readings-of-a-white-deposit} (its growing-mode amplitude in the radiation era, to leading order outside the Hubble length: a quarter of the contrast on a flat slice, $\tfrac32X^{2}$ times it on a slice of uniform expansion, and $2X$ times the velocity on every slice); they are not re-derived here, and which reading holds is a hypothesis.

(v) With $f \le 1$ the denominators are at most $2 + 10^{-20}$. The check evaluates the thresholds with $\pi > 333/106$ and $A = 2.0 \times 10^{-9}$ (the lower record value, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-planck-2018-lcdm-parameters}) at the stored lower bounds of $X = a_{d}H_{d}/a_{0}H_{0}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.finite-range-descent-deposit-cannot-seed-cmb}(iii)): (FR) $3.0 \times 10^{15} < 8\pi AX^{3}/(2 + \eta) < 3.1 \times 10^{15}$ at $1$ MeV and above $9.6 \times 10^{60}$ at $10^{12}$ GeV; (FM) between $0.034$ and $0.035$ at $1$ MeV, above $5.0 \times 10^{13}$ at $10^{12}$ GeV, and increasing on a grid of $X$ between. $M_{H} = 1/(2GH_{d}) = 4\pi\bar M_{P}^{2}/H_{d}$ and $H_{d} = \pi\sqrt{g_{*}/90}\,T_{d}^{2}/\bar M_{P}$ (the cited theorem's form) give $(M_{H}/\bar M_{P})^{2} = 1440\,(\bar M_{P}/T_{d})^{4}/g_{*}$, more than $(6 \times 10^{43})^{2}$ at $1$ MeV and $(2 \times 10^{13})^{2}$ at $10^{12}$ GeV, and the products exceed $2.3 \times 10^{42}$ and $1.1 \times 10^{27}$. In reduced Planck masses the (FM) threshold is $\tfrac{8\pi A}{2f + \eta}\tfrac{X^{2}}{(1 + 6X)^{2}}\cdot XM_{H}$ with $XM_{H} = 4\pi\bar M_{P}^{2}a_{d}/k$, and $a_{d}$ decreases as $T_{d}$ rises (entropy conservation, as in the cited theorem) while $X^{2}/(1 + 6X)^{2}$ is within $10^{-7}$ of $\tfrac{1}{36}$ throughout, so the value at $10^{12}$ GeV is the least in the window. Under (FR) a white contrast with $\Delta_{\delta}^{2} = 16A$ at $X$ has $\Delta_{\delta}^{2} = 16AX^{3}$ at $k_{d} = H_{d}$. Under (UE), with $\pi < 22/7$, $A \le 2.2 \times 10^{-9}$, $f = 1$ and the stored $X > 3.2 \times 10^{20}$ at the pivot for $T_{d} = 10^{12}$ GeV, the threshold without the factor $(1 + 1/X)^{-2}$ is below $2.5 \times 10^{-30}$, and that factor is below one; and $(T_{d}/M_{H})^{2} = (T_{d}/\bar M_{P})^{2}(\bar M_{P}/M_{H})^{2} > 10^{-40}$ there, so $T_{d}/M_{H}$ exceeds the threshold by more than $10^{9}$.

The consequence combines (iv) and (v): they bound $\omega_{\max}$, the largest energy on the support of the occupation profile, so they show that some quantum lies above the threshold. The closing under (FR) and (FM) is conditional on Hypothesis (QP), which is stated in the result and is not among the stored premises; its motivation, that a single quantum with $G\omega^{2} \gg 1$ has a gravitational radius far above its wavelength and is not a quantum of a test field on the collar, is argued.

synthesis.sudden-descent-feature-not-til.formal:
Work in the frozen phase in its flat slicing, the setting of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.frozen-phase-spectrum-not-red} (de Sitter space $\eta/(Hx_0)^2$ of Lemma \claimref{mass.de-sitter-scale-frozen-point}, conformal time $\eta = x_0 < 0$, scale factor $a = -1/(H\eta)$), and model the descent as an event at conformal time $\eta_d < 0$: before it the field has no propagating modes, and at it a massless scalar $\phi$ (the massless point of the series' weight dictionary, weight $0$) is set, mode by mode, to the instantaneous vacuum of $\chi = a\phi$, namely $\chi = (2k)^{-1/2}$, $\chi' = -I_{4}k(2k)^{-1/2}$ (numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$). Write $x = k|\eta_d|$ and let $\Delta^{2}(k)$ be the late-time ($\eta \to 0$) dimensionless spectrum of $\phi$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Exact spectrum.)} $\Delta^{2}(k) = (H/2\pi)^{2}F(x)$ with
\[
F(x) \;=\; 1 + \frac{1}{2x^{4}} + \frac{1}{x^{2}}\Bigl[\Bigl(1 - \frac{1}{2x^{2}}\Bigr)\cos 2x - \frac{1}{x}\sin 2x\Bigr],
\]
the Bogoliubov coefficients relative to the Bunch-Davies modes being $\alpha = e^{-I_{4} x}A$, $\beta = -e^{I_{4} x}B$ with $A = 1 - I_{4}/x - 1/(2x^{2})$, $B = 1/(2x^{2})$, and $|\alpha|^{2} - |\beta|^{2} = 1$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Modes outside at the descent.)} $F(x) = \tfrac49 x^{2} - \tfrac1{15}x^{4} + \tfrac{8}{1575}x^{6} + O(x^{8})$, so for $k|\eta_d| \ll 1$ the local index is $n_s - 1 \to +2$: large scales are suppressed, a blue cutoff.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Modes inside at the descent.)} $(|A| - B)^{2} \le F(x) \le (|A| + B)^{2}$ with $|A|^{2} = 1 + 1/(4x^{4})$, so $F \to 1$ with oscillations of envelope $x^{-2}$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Every window.)} For every $x_1 > 0$, $\ln F(x_1) - \ln F(e^{7}x_1) < 7 \times 0.0267$, the smallest red drop the measured $n_s = 0.9649 \pm 0.0042$ \cite{Planck2018} allows at two standard deviations over seven e-folds of $k$ (the measured range $\ell \approx 2$ to $2500$ spans about $7.1$ e-folds). So no window of that width has a mean index inside the measured band.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, under this model, a sudden descent imprints a feature at $k \sim 1/|\eta_d|$ (suppression of modes outside at the descent, a decaying ringing, flatness for modes well inside) and no window of the measured width carries the measured red index: the first escape named in Proposition \claimref{synthesis.frozen-phase-spectrum-not-red}, dilatation breaking by the descent's state, is not supplied by a single descent event with an instantaneous-vacuum start. Other initial states at the descent are not covered.

\emph{Note (the start state is not Hadamard; added 1 November).} The model's instantaneous-vacuum start is not a Hadamard state: at the descent it falls below the Bunch-Davies state by $1/(2k^{3}\eta_{d}^{2})$ per mode in $\langle\chi^{2}\rangle$, with $|\beta_{k}|^{2} = 1/(4k^{4}\eta_{d}^{4})$, and the mode sums diverge logarithmically, so its two-point function does not differ by a smooth kernel from that of an infrared-regularised Bunch-Davies comparison state, which is Hadamard (taken as given there, with the smooth-difference property of scalar Hadamard states) (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.massive-dirac-instantaneous-vacuum-and-non-smooth-descents-are-not-hadamard}(iv)). The model therefore describes a state that the Hadamard deposit premise, Premise \claimref{synthesis.hadamard-deposit-premise}, excludes. The late-time spectrum computed above, and the conclusion that this start supplies a feature and not a tilt, are unaffected.
synthesis.sudden-descent-feature-not-til.technical:
Model the descent as an instant $\eta_d$ in the frozen phase's flat slicing at which a massless scalar starts in the instantaneous vacuum. Matching to the Bunch-Davies modes gives Bogoliubov coefficients with $|\alpha|^{2} - |\beta|^{2} = 1$ and the late-time spectrum $(H/2\pi)^{2}F(k|\eta_d|)$, with $F$ in closed form. Modes already outside the horizon at the descent are suppressed, $F \approx \tfrac49 x^{2}$, a blue cutoff with local index $+2$; modes well inside approach the flat spectrum with oscillations of relative size $x^{-2}$, bounded between $(|A| - B)^{2}$ and $(|A| + B)^{2}$.

The measured index, $n_s = 0.9649 \pm 0.0042$, needs $\ln\Delta^{2}$ to fall by at least $7 \times 0.0267$ across the seven e-folds of the measured window. Exact rational enclosures of $F$ (a Taylor bound below $x = 1$, a gridded bound with Taylor-enclosed $\cos$ and $\sin$ on $[1, 3]$, the envelope bounds above $3$) show that no window of seven e-folds has that drop. A single descent event with an instantaneous-vacuum start thus leaves a feature, not a tilt. Read as a pointer, not proved here: if the descent's state is to break the dilatation and produce the measured red tilt, the breaking would have to last while the whole observed window is set, about seven e-folds of the frozen phase if horizon exit sets the modes; other initial states are not computed. The computation is standard de Sitter field theory; the series supplies the frozen-phase setting and the claim that the descent sources the earliest correlations.
synthesis.sudden-descent-feature-not-til.lay: An earlier result showed that if the universe's descent into its present phase respected that phase's stretching symmetry, it could not produce the slight tilt measured in the early universe's ripples: the symmetry has to be broken. The simplest way to break it is for the descent to happen at one moment, which sets a scale. This result computes what such a sudden start does to a simple field: ripples much larger than the scale set by the moment are suppressed, ripples much smaller come out with the flat, untilted pattern, and in between the pattern rings and then settles. Nowhere does it produce the gentle, steady tilt seen across the observed range of sizes. So a sudden start of this simple kind is ruled out as the source of the tilt; the natural reading, not proved here, is that a descent producing the tilt would have to be a drawn-out process, lasting while all the observed sizes were being imprinted.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} By Lemma \claimref{mass.de-sitter-scale-frozen-point} and part (i) of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.frozen-phase-spectrum-not-red}, the frozen phase in flat slicing is $g = \eta/(Hx_0)^{2}$, and in the usual sign conventions the metric is $a^{2}(d\eta^{2} - d\vec x^{2})$ with $a = -1/(H\eta)$, $\eta = x_0 < 0$, the late-time boundary being $\eta \to 0$. A massless minimally coupled scalar (weight $0$ in the dictionary $m^{2} = -w(w + 3)H^{2}$ used there) with $\chi = a\phi$ obeys $\chi'' + (k^{2} - a''/a)\chi = 0$ with $a''/a = 2/\eta^{2}$; in $z = k\eta$ this is $\chi_{zz} + (1 - 2/z^{2})\chi = 0$. The Bunch-Davies solution is $u(z) = e^{-I_{4} z}(1 - I_{4}/z)$ (times $(2k)^{-1/2}$), standard in de Sitter field theory (Birrell and Davies, cited from memory); the script verifies that it solves the equation, as an identity in $z$, and that $u\bar u' - u'\bar u = 2I_{4}$.

\emph{(i)} Write $\chi = \alpha u + \beta\bar u$ (units $(2k)^{-1/2} = 1$) and impose $\chi = 1$, $\chi_z = -I_{4}$ at $z_d = k\eta_d = -x$. With $W = 2I_{4}$, $\alpha = (\bar u'(z_d) + I_{4}\bar u(z_d))/W$ and $\beta = -(u'(z_d) + I_{4} u(z_d))/W$. Since $u' = e^{-I_{4} z}(-I_{4} - 1/z + I_{4}/z^{2})$, $u' + I_{4} u = e^{-I_{4} z}\,I_{4}/z^{2}$ and $\bar u' + I_{4}\bar u = e^{I_{4} z}(2I_{4} - 2/z - I_{4}/z^{2})$, so $\alpha = e^{I_{4} z_d}(1 + I_{4}/z_d - 1/(2z_d^{2}))$ and $\beta = -e^{-I_{4} z_d}/(2z_d^{2})$; at $z_d = -x$ these are the displayed $\alpha = e^{-I_{4} x}A$, $\beta = -e^{I_{4} x}B$. Then $|\alpha|^{2} - |\beta|^{2} = |A|^{2} - B^{2} = 1 + 1/(4x^{4}) - 1/(4x^{4}) = 1$. As $\eta \to 0$, $u \to -I_{4}/z$ and $\bar u \to I_{4}/z$ at leading order, so $\chi \to (-I_{4}/z)(\alpha - \beta)$ and $|\phi|^{2} = |\chi|^{2}/a^{2}$ is $|\alpha - \beta|^{2}$ times its Bunch-Davies value, whose dimensionless spectrum is $(H/2\pi)^{2}$. Finally $|\alpha - \beta|^{2} = |A + e^{2I_{4} x}B|^{2} = |A|^{2} + B^{2} + 2B\,\mathrm{Re}(\bar A e^{2I_{4} x})$, and $\mathrm{Re}(\bar Ae^{2I_{4} x}) = (1 - 1/(2x^{2}))\cos 2x - x^{-1}\sin 2x$, which gives $F$. The script stores every expression as $e^{\mp I_{4} z}$ times a Laurent polynomial in $z^{-1}$ with Gaussian-rational coefficients and differentiates exactly; it checks the mode equation, the Wronskian, the coefficients $A$ and $B$, the normalisation, and the closed form of $F$ as an identity in independent $(x, \cos 2x, \sin 2x)$ on rational points of the circle (only $|e^{2I_{4} x}| = 1$ is used).

\emph{(ii)} $x^{4}F(x) = x^{4} + \tfrac12 + (x^{2} - \tfrac12)\cos 2x - x\sin 2x$; inserting the Taylor series of $\cos 2x$ and $\sin 2x$ with their rational coefficients, the coefficients of $x^{0}, \dots, x^{5}$ cancel and those of $x^{6}, x^{8}, x^{10}$ are $\tfrac49, -\tfrac1{15}, \tfrac{8}{1575}$ (computed exactly by the script). So $F = \tfrac49 x^{2}(1 - \tfrac{3}{20}x^{2} + O(x^{4}))$ and $d\ln F/d\ln x \to 2$.

\emph{(iii)} $F = |A + \omega B|^{2}$ with $|\omega| = 1$ lies between $(|A| - B)^{2}$ and $(|A| + B)^{2}$. Using $1 \le |A| \le 1 + 1/(8x^{4})$ (from $\sqrt{1 + t} \le 1 + t/2$), $F(x_1) \le (1 + 1/(8x_1^{4}) + 1/(2x_1^{2}))^{2}$, decreasing in $x_1$, and $F(x_2) \ge (1 - 1/(2x_2^{2}))^{2}$. A constant index $n_s$ over $[x_1, x_2]$, $x_2 = e^{7}x_1$, needs $F(x_1)/F(x_2) = e^{7(1 - n_s)} \ge e^{7 \times 0.0267}$ at the weakest tilt of the two-standard-deviation band ($1 - n_s \ge 0.0351 - 0.0084$), and $e^{y} \ge 1 + y + y^{2}/2$. At $x_1 = 3$, $x_2 \ge 1096 \cdot 3$ ($e^{7} > 1096$ from a partial sum of the exponential series), the upper bound of the ratio is about $1.118$ against the lower bound $1.205$ of the required factor; the script checks this inequality exactly, and that the same bound at $x_1 = 2$ would not suffice, so the cut at $3$ is where the exact argument stops. The window width is the measured multipole range $2 \lesssim \ell \lesssim 2500$, $\ln 1250 \approx 7.13$ (Planck 2018, cited as in Proposition \claimref{synthesis.frozen-phase-spectrum-not-red}); the measured index and its error are those used there.

\emph{(iv)} Every window, exactly. A constant index $n_s$ in the band on $[x_1, x_2]$, $x_2 = e^{7}x_1 > 1096x_1$, needs $F(x_1)/F(x_2) \ge e^{7 \times 0.0267} \ge 1 + y + y^{2}/2 =: R$, $y = 7 \times 0.0267$. Three exact enclosures of $F$ suffice. (a) On $(0, 1]$: $x^{4}F = \sum_n s_nx^{n}$ with $s_0 = \dots = s_5 = 0$, $s_6 = \tfrac49$, and $|s_n| \le 3 \cdot 2^{n}/(n-2)!$ (each of the three contributions to the coefficient of $x^{n}$ in $(x^{2} - \tfrac12)\cos 2x - x\sin 2x$ is at most $2^{n}/(n-2)!$), so $F(x) \le Sx^{2}$ and $F(x) \ge (\tfrac49 - T)x^{2}$ with $S = \sum_{n \ge 6}|s_n| < 0.53$ and $T = \sum_{n \ge 7}|s_n|$, $\tfrac49 - T > 0.37$ (partial sums to $n = 30$ plus the geometric tail bound, ratio at most $1/15$). (b) On $[1, 3]$: write $F = 1 + 1/(2x^{4}) + G/x^{2}$ with $G = (1 - 1/(2x^{2}))\cos 2x - x^{-1}\sin 2x$, $|G'| \le 6$ for $x \ge 1$; on the cells $[x_0, x_0 + \tfrac1{100}]$, with $\cos 2x_0$, $\sin 2x_0$ enclosed by degree-$40$ Taylor sums and the Lagrange remainder, $0.30 < F < 1.16$. (c) On $[3, \infty)$ the envelope bounds of (iii). Then: for $x_1 \ge 1$, $F(x_1) < 1.16$ and $F(x_2) \ge (1 - 1/(2 \cdot 1096^{2}))^{2}$; for $x_1 \le 1$ and $x_2 \ge 3$, $F(x_1) \le S$ and $F(x_2) \ge (1 - \tfrac1{18})^{2}$; for $x_1 \le 1 \le x_2 \le 3$, $x_1 \le 3/1096$ and $F(x_1) \le Sx_1^{2}$ against $F(x_2) > 0.30$; for $x_2 \le 1$, $F(x_1)/F(x_2) \le S/((\tfrac49 - T)1096^{2})$. In every case the ratio is below $R$; the script checks each inequality in exact rationals.

Corroboration, numerical, double precision, not part of the check: on a logarithmic grid of $12000$ starting points $x_1 \in [0.05, 5 \times 10^{4}]$, the mean index $\ln(F(x_1)/F(e^{7}x_1))/7$ is at most $0.0175$ (at $x_1 \approx 2.745$); $F$ has its global maximum $1.1302$ at $x \approx 2.7435$; least-squares fits of $\ln F$ against $\ln x$ on $401$ points per window give a most negative slope of $-0.0047$ (at $x_1 \approx 2.09$) with maximal residual $0.10$. 

\emph{The closing paragraph} reads (ii) to (iv) together: modes outside at the descent are suppressed, modes near the descent scale ring and modes well inside are flat, and no window of the measured width has the measured red drop. A reading, argued and not proved: a state fixed at a single time with no second scale depends on $k$ only through $k|\eta_d|$ and tends to the flat spectrum for $k|\eta_d| \gg 1$, which suggests that a descent producing the tilt would need dilatation breaking lasting while the observed window is set (about seven e-folds of the frozen phase if horizon exit sets each mode); other initial states (adiabatic vacua of higher order) change $A$ and $B$ by terms of higher order in $1/x$ and are not computed here. Transport content: none in the computation, which is standard de Sitter field theory; the setting (frozen phase, massless point, descent at the origin) is the series'. Which de Sitter scale the frozen phase has during the descent is not addressed.

synthesis.tree-level-curvature-couplings.technical: A stored result found that on a Kasner approach a scalar coupled to curvature matches the measured tilt only for a coupling near $1.53$ fitted to it, and left open whether the series fixes that coupling. Such an approach would have to precede the descent, a stage the series now takes as hypothesis (P1). The series' rule for how a scalar feels the geometry is its mass-weight dictionary, a pairing of the field's Thomas tractor with the frozen point, proved on vacuum Einstein regions. Away from them the pairing splits into a curvature coupling and a constant mass, and the split depends on the connection that builds the Thomas operator, which the store does not record. With the transport's operator and the frozen point in its stored form the coupling is $-w/6$; with the field-space connection it is zero; pairing with the metric's own scale tractor instead, which is not the frozen point there, gives $-w(w+3)/12$. For the real weights of the unitary range these lie between $0$ and $\tfrac12$; the heavy fields of the series, the rung field's modes among them, sit on the principal series, where the first reading is complex and the second enormous, so for them the exclusion rests on the stored actions, which have no curvature term at tree level, and on the field-space reading. At the Kasner points the store fixes, the curvature vanishes on the vacuum circle, at the five-dimensional vacuum ends and in their induced four-metrics, so a coupling acts only at the isotropic point reached by a massless scalar. There these couplings give an index of at least $3 - \sqrt{3}$, or $3 - \sqrt{7}$ once the stored hidden-scale weights are included: blue in both cases. Read back, the fitted coupling needs a weight below $-9$, a tachyon in the de Sitter stage, outside the unitary fields the dictionary uses; only the reading that drops the field-space premise reaches it, and then with a scalar heavier than four times the Hubble rate of $\Lambda$ and lighter than five, which no stored field is. Loop corrections are not treated.
synthesis.tree-level-curvature-couplings.lay: In standard cosmology the slight tilt of the early universe's ripples comes from a stage of rapid expansion, which this framework lacks. If the framework allowed a squeezing stage before its origin, an earlier result found that a field feeling the curvature of space strongly enough could give the right tilt there, but only if the strength of that coupling were set by hand. This result asks whether the framework itself sets that strength, in its basic equations before quantum corrections. It collects the couplings the framework's own rules give its fields, reading its rule for masses in each way it allows. All are much weaker than needed, so the ripples come out tilted the wrong way. The value that would match corresponds to a field that would be unstable in today's accelerating universe, or to a field of a particular tiny mass that the framework does not contain. So the framework does not supply the needed coupling; adding one would be a new assumption.
